- Former et sensibiliser les utilisateurs à l’utilisation des outils professionnels et aux bonnes pratiques de sécurité.
- Évaluer régulièrement la satisfaction des utilisateurs et proposer des mesures d’amélioration.

**Gestion budgétaire, achats et prestataires**

- Élaborer le budget annuel du service informatique et assurer le suivi de son exécution.
- Préparer les prévisions de dépenses liées aux équipements, logiciels, abonnements, connectivité et maintenance.
- Définir les spécifications techniques des acquisitions informatiques.
- Participer à l’évaluation technique des offres conformément aux procédures de passation des marchés de DCA.
- Coordonner avec les services Finances et Logistique le suivi des commandes, des livraisons, des contrats et des factures.
- Évaluer la qualité des services rendus par les fournisseurs et proposer les mesures correctives nécessaires.
- Rechercher des solutions adaptées aux besoins opérationnels, au budget disponible et aux exigences de sécurité.
- Assurer la traçabilité des décisions techniques et des dépenses relevant du service informatique.

**Management et développement des compétences**

- Encadrer, accompagner et évaluer les membres de l’équipe informatique placés sous sa supervision.
- Répartir les tâches et assurer le suivi des objectifs individuels.
- Élaborer un plan de renforcement des capacités techniques de l’équipe.
- Favoriser le partage de connaissances et la documentation des procédures.
- Veiller au respect du code de conduite, des politiques de protection et des règles de confidentialité.
- Promouvoir un environnement de travail collaboratif, responsable et orienté vers la qualité du service.

**Reporting et coordination**

- Produire des rapports mensuels sur la performance du service informatique.
- Présenter les incidents majeurs, les risques, les dépenses, les besoins et les mesures correctives à la Direction.
- Assurer le suivi des recommandations issues des audits, des contrôles et des évaluations des risques.
- Participer aux réunions de coordination et aux exercices de planification opérationnelle.
- Maintenir une documentation actualisée des systèmes, des actifs, des incidents et des procédures.
- Informer rapidement la hiérarchie de toute situation susceptible d’affecter la sécurité ou la continuité des opérations.

**Qualifications et expérience requises**

**Formation**

- Diplôme de niveau Bac+3 à Bac+5 en informatique, systèmes et réseaux, cybersécurité, télécommunications ou domaine équivalent.
- Toute certification pertinente en administration des systèmes, réseaux, cybersécurité ou gestion des services informatiques constitue un atout.

**Expérience professionnelle**

- Au moins cinq (5) années d’expérience professionnelle dans les systèmes informatiques, les réseaux ou l’administration des infrastructures IT.
- Expérience confirmée dans la gestion d’un parc informatique et la supervision du support aux utilisateurs.
- Expérience en gestion de la sécurité informatique, des sauvegardes et de la continuité des services.
- Expérience en encadrement d’équipe, gestion de prestataires et suivi budgétaire.
- Une expérience dans une ONG internationale ou une organisation multisite est fortement souhaitable.
- Une expérience en environnement opérationnel contraint, notamment dans des bureaux décentralisés ou des zones à connectivité limitée, constitue un avantage.

**Compétences techniques**

- Administration des environnements Windows et, selon les besoins, Linux.
- Gestion des réseaux LAN/WAN, Wi-Fi, VPN, pare-feu et équipements de communication.
- Administration des comptes, des droits d’accès et des solutions collaboratives.
- Connaissances solides en cybersécurité, sauvegarde, restauration et gestion des incidents.
- Maîtrise des outils de suivi du parc informatique et de gestion des demandes d’assistance.
- Capacité à élaborer des procédures techniques, des plans de continuité et des rapports de performance.
- Connaissance des principes de protection des données, de gestion des risques et de contrôle interne.

**Compétences comportementales**

- Leadership et capacité à prendre des décisions techniques.
- Intégrité, discrétion et sens des responsabilités.
- Rigueur et respect des procédures.
- Esprit d’analyse et capacité à résoudre les problèmes.
- Aptitude à travailler avec plusieurs départements et des équipes multiculturelles.
- Capacité à prioriser les demandes dans un environnement exigeant.
- Bonne communication écrite et orale.
- Capacité à travailler sous pression et à effectuer des déplacements sur le terrain.

**Indicateurs clés de performance (KPI)**

Les indicateurs ci-dessous constituent une proposition de base. Les cibles définitives devront être validées par la Direction en fonction de l’infrastructure, des moyens disponibles, des politiques du siège et des contraintes opérationnelles.

**Le poste est réservé uniquement pour les candidats de la nationalité centrafricaine.**

jobs.title: GBV Programme Focal Point
jobs.description:
**JOB DESCRIPTION**

**PROJECT**

Integrated Shelter, Food Security and Livelihoods Support for Safe, Dignified and Sustainable Return in Abul Thohur (Idleb) and Madiq Castle (Hama)

**POSITION SUMMARY**

The GBV Programme Focal Point will support the integration of gender-based violence (GBV) risk mitigation, protection mainstreaming, safeguarding and accountability measures across IHH’s integrated Shelter/NFI and Food Security and Agriculture/Livelihoods activities in Abul Thohur, Idlib Governorate, and Madiq Castle, Hama Governorate. The role will provide practical guidance to project teams to help ensure that assistance is delivered safely, accessibly, and with dignity, and that concerns are handled confidentially and referred through established pathways where appropriate. This is a mainstreaming and risk-mitigation role; it does not replace specialized GBV case management or other specialized protection services.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

**GBV Risk Mitigation and Protection Mainstreaming**

- Provide practical advice to project staff on identifying and reducing GBV-related risks across shelter rehabilitation, cash assistance, food assistance, bakery support, agricultural support and irrigation-related activities.
- Promote safe, dignified, accessible and inclusive participation in assessments, beneficiary verification, distributions, cash transfers, community consultations and other project activities, with attention to the different needs and risks faced by women, girls and other at-risk groups.
- Support project teams to consider safe locations, timing, privacy, communication methods, staff presence and other relevant measures when planning and delivering activities.
- Review activity plans and field arrangements and recommend proportionate risk-mitigation measures in coordination with the Project Manager and relevant technical staff.

**Staff Awareness and Safeguarding**

- Support staff briefings on GBV risk mitigation, respectful conduct, confidentiality, informed consent, safeguarding and Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA), in line with IHH policies and available guidance.
- Promote adherence to the Code of Conduct and reporting procedures, and raise safeguarding or PSEA concerns through established internal channels without conducting investigations independently.
- Help ensure that project teams understand appropriate boundaries when receiving sensitive disclosures and communicate respectfully with affected people.

**Feedback, Referrals and Confidentiality**

- Coordinate with the project team and relevant focal points to help ensure that feedback and complaint channels are safe, accessible, confidential and appropriate for women, girls and other community members.
- Maintain information on available specialized protection and GBV service providers and referral pathways in the target areas, verified through appropriate coordination channels.
- If a person discloses a GBV incident or other sensitive protection concern, respond respectfully, avoid probing for details, explain available options, and facilitate a referral only with informed consent and in accordance with approved protocols.
- Ensure that sensitive information is not recorded or shared unnecessarily and that documentation or referrals follow confidentiality and data-minimization principles.

**Coordination, Monitoring and Reporting**

- Coordinate with the Project Manager, Field Engineer, FSAL Project Officer, Field Assistants, Agronomists and MEAL colleagues to integrate relevant GBV risk-mitigation measures into implementation and monitoring.
- Review monitoring findings, community feedback and field observations to identify emerging risks and recommend practical corrective actions, without collecting unnecessary sensitive personal data.
- Contribute to internal updates and project reporting on protection mainstreaming and risk-mitigation actions, using aggregated and non-identifying information wherever possible.
- Coordinate with relevant local actors and specialized service providers when appropriate and authorized by IHH.
- Carry out other related duties assigned by the line manager that are consistent with the position and project scope.

**QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE**

- Bachelor’s degree in social sciences, social work, gender studies, psychology, law, humanitarian studies, development studies or another relevant field.
- At least two years of relevant experience in protection, gender, GBV risk mitigation, safeguarding, PSEA, community engagement or related humanitarian work.
- Good understanding of GBV risk mitigation, survivor-centred principles, confidentiality, informed consent, safe referrals and the Do No Harm approach.
- Familiarity with humanitarian accountability and feedback mechanisms and the ability to communicate respectfully with diverse communities.
- Experience delivering staff briefings or awareness sessions on protection, safeguarding, PSEA or related topics is an advantage.
- Previous experience in Syria or in integrated shelter, cash assistance, food security or livelihoods programmes is an advantage.
- Fluent Arabic and good working knowledge of English. Turkish is an advantage.
- Strong communication, coordination, documentation and organizational skills, with the ability to handle sensitive information responsibly.
- Commitment to IHH’s humanitarian principles, safeguarding policies, Code of Conduct and PSEA requirements.

**DUTY STATION AND FIELD TRAVEL**

The position will be based in Idlib, Syria, with regular field visits to Abul Thohur in Idlib Governorate and Madiq Castle in Hama Governorate.

jobs.title: FSAL Project Officer
jobs.description:
**JOB DESCRIPTION**

**PROJECT**

Integrated Shelter, Food Security and Livelihoods Support for Safe, Dignified and Sustainable Return in Abul Thohur (Idleb) and Madiq Castle (Hama)

**DUTY STATION**

Idlib, Syria, with regular field visits to project locations

**ABOUT THE PROJECT**

IHH is implementing an integrated humanitarian and early-recovery project funded by the OCHA Syria Humanitarian Fund (SHF), supporting safe, dignified and sustainable return in Abul Thohur, Idleb Governorate, and Madiq Castle, Hama Governorate.

The project combines shelter rehabilitation, winterization and Core NFI assistance, cash assistance for food, bakery rehabilitation and subsidized bread provision, agricultural support for returning wheat farmers, and rehabilitation of community irrigation infrastructure. These complementary interventions aim to address urgent household needs, restore essential infrastructure and support agricultural livelihoods and community recovery.

**JOB SUMMARY**

IHH is seeking a qualified and experienced FSAL Project Officer to coordinate and oversee the day-to-day implementation, monitoring and reporting of the project's Food Security and Agriculture/Livelihoods (FSAL) activities.

The position will focus on cash assistance for food, bakery rehabilitation and subsidized bread provision in Abul Thohur, and agricultural support for returning wheat farmers and irrigation-related interventions in Madiq Castle. The FSAL Project Officer will ensure that activities are implemented in accordance with the approved project proposal, work plan, budget, targeting criteria and relevant technical and donor requirements.

The successful candidate will coordinate with Field Assistants, Agronomists, the Field Engineer, finance, procurement, logistics and monitoring staff, as well as beneficiaries, service providers and relevant local authorities. The role will require regular field visits, effective follow-up of implementation progress, oversight of beneficiary selection and verification, monitoring of activity quality and results, and timely preparation of reports.

The FSAL Project Officer will report to the Project Manager and contribute to effective coordination across project components, ensuring that implementation challenges are identified promptly and that activities achieve their intended results in a transparent, accountable and timely manner.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Project Planning and Implementation**

- Lead the day-to-day planning, coordination and follow-up of FSAL activities in accordance with the approved project proposal, logical framework, work plan, budget and implementation schedule.
- Prepare and regularly update activity plans, implementation schedules and field follow-up plans in coordination with the Project Manager and relevant technical and support teams.
- Coordinate the implementation of cash assistance for food, bakery rehabilitation and subsidized bread provision, agricultural support for returning wheat farmers, and irrigation-related interventions.
- Monitor implementation progress against approved outputs, indicators, targets and timelines, identifying delays, operational constraints and implementation gaps.
- Conduct regular field visits to verify implementation progress, engage with beneficiaries and field teams, and follow up on outstanding actions.
- Ensure that activities are implemented in line with approved procedures, eligibility criteria, technical requirements and donor conditions.
- Identify operational risks and propose corrective measures to the Project Manager when implementation deviates from approved plans.
- Ensure effective coordination between FSAL activities and other project components, particularly where agricultural interventions, irrigation rehabilitation and shelter-related activities require joint planning.

**Food Security and Cash Assistance**

- Coordinate the implementation and follow-up of cash assistance for food, ensuring that activities are delivered in accordance with approved targeting criteria, transfer arrangements and implementation schedules.
- Coordinate with the designated Financial Service Provider (FSP), finance team and relevant project staff to support the timely and orderly delivery of cash assistance.
- Oversee beneficiary identification, registration and verification processes in coordination with the field team, ensuring transparent selection and accurate documentation.
- Monitor the implementation of cash assistance, identify delivery challenges and follow up on unresolved cases or discrepancies with the relevant teams.
- Ensure that beneficiaries receive clear information regarding eligibility, assistance arrangements, delivery schedules and feedback and complaints channels.
- Review field monitoring findings and beneficiary feedback to identify implementation gaps and recommend appropriate follow-up.
- Maintain accurate activity records and supporting documentation for verification, reporting and donor compliance.

**Bakery Rehabilitation and Subsidized Bread Provision**

- Coordinate the programme implementation and operational follow-up of bakery rehabilitation and subsidized bread activities in Abul Thohur.
- Work closely with the Field Engineer to ensure that rehabilitation progress, technical requirements and completion milestones are followed up and that engineering issues are referred to the responsible technical staff.
- Coordinate with relevant service providers, bakery operators, local authorities and other stakeholders as required for implementation.
- Follow up on the availability and delivery of approved inputs, including wheat flour and operational support, in coordination with procurement, logistics and finance teams.
- Monitor subsidized bread provision against approved arrangements, including the quantities delivered, distribution records, operational continuity and intended beneficiary reach.
- Review implementation records and field observations to identify supply, operational or delivery challenges and report them to the Project Manager.
- Ensure that records relating to bakery rehabilitation, operational support and subsidized bread provision are complete, accurate and properly maintained.

**Agricultural Support and Livelihoods**

- Coordinate the implementation of agricultural support activities targeting returning wheat farmers in Madiq Castle, in accordance with approved project plans and eligibility criteria.
- Work closely with Agronomists to plan field activities, follow up on beneficiary selection and verification, and monitor the delivery of agricultural inputs and related technical guidance.
- Ensure that agricultural assistance is provided to eligible beneficiaries and documented in accordance with approved procedures.
- Monitor progress against planned targets and schedules, following up on delays, supply constraints, beneficiary concerns and other implementation challenges.
- Coordinate with the Agronomists to collect information on activity progress, beneficiary participation, delivery records and emerging agricultural needs.
- Support the organization and follow-up of agricultural awareness sessions or technical guidance activities included in the approved project plan.
- Facilitate coordination with farming communities, local authorities and relevant agricultural stakeholders to support implementation and resolve operational issues.
- Ensure that beneficiary records, input distribution documents and field monitoring information are complete and available for reporting and verification.
- Refer technical agricultural questions and recommendations to the Agronomists rather than making specialized agronomic decisions outside the position's responsibilities.

**Irrigation Infrastructure Rehabilitation**

- Coordinate the programme-level implementation and follow-up of community irrigation infrastructure rehabilitation in Madiq Castle.
- Work closely with the Field Engineer to align field implementation schedules, community engagement and operational requirements with the approved rehabilitation plan.
- Monitor overall progress against agreed milestones and report delays, access constraints, community concerns or other implementation challenges.
- Facilitate communication with farmers, community representatives and relevant local authorities regarding planned works and implementation arrangements.
- Support coordination around irrigation water access and distribution arrangements in consultation with the relevant technical staff and stakeholders.
- Ensure that field observations, community feedback and implementation updates are documented and communicated to the Project Manager.
- Refer engineering assessments, designs, Bills of Quantities, technical specifications and construction quality concerns to the Field Engineer.

**Team Coordination and Field Supervision**

- Provide day-to-day task coordination and programme guidance to Field Assistants supporting FSAL activities.
- Coordinate with Agronomists and the Field Engineer to ensure clear division of responsibilities, consistent field follow-up and timely resolution of implementation issues.
- Review field updates, activity records and reports submitted by Field Assistants and relevant technical staff, following up on incomplete information or outstanding actions.
- Organize regular activity follow-up meetings with the relevant team members to review progress, discuss challenges and agree on corrective actions.
- Ensure that field staff understand activity objectives, eligibility requirements, documentation procedures and reporting deadlines.
- Coordinate with finance, procurement, logistics and MEAL staff to ensure that operational requirements, monitoring arrangements and documentation are addressed in a timely manner.
- Escalate significant performance, operational, financial or compliance concerns to the Project Manager.

**Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Reporting**

- Monitor FSAL activities against the approved logical framework, indicators, targets, means of verification and implementation schedule.
- Ensure that beneficiary selection, registration, verification and activity records are complete, consistent and properly documented.
- Coordinate with MEAL staff to support activity monitoring, beneficiary feedback collection, post-assistance monitoring and other required monitoring exercises.
- Review monitoring findings and field feedback to identify implementation gaps, assess progress and recommend improvements.
- Prepare timely, accurate and evidence-based activity reports, progress updates and inputs for donor reporting.
- Maintain updated activity-tracking tools and ensure that supporting documents, beneficiary records, distribution lists and monitoring evidence are properly archived.
- Ensure that feedback and complaints received during implementation are documented, referred and followed up through established procedures.
- Document implementation challenges, lessons learned and good practices to support programme quality and informed decision-making.

**Budget Monitoring, Coordination and Compliance**

- Monitor activity implementation against approved budget lines and planned expenditures in coordination with the Project Manager and finance team.
- Coordinate with procurement and logistics teams to ensure that procurement, supplies, service delivery and operational arrangements support timely implementation.
- Review activity-related documentation and identify discrepancies or potential compliance concerns for follow-up with the relevant departments.
- Ensure that activities and related expenditures remain within the approved project scope and follow established authorization procedures.
- Maintain effective working relationships with local authorities, community representatives, service providers and relevant humanitarian actors.
- Participate in relevant coordination meetings and stakeholder engagements as assigned by the Project Manager.
- Support information sharing and coordination with relevant sector actors to promote complementarity and avoid duplication of assistance.

**Protection, Safeguarding and Accountability**

- Ensure that FSAL activities are implemented in accordance with the principles of impartiality, non-discrimination, accountability to affected populations and do no harm.
- Promote transparent beneficiary selection and equitable access to assistance, with appropriate attention to vulnerable and marginalized households.
- Ensure that beneficiaries receive clear information about eligibility criteria, assistance modalities and feedback mechanisms.
- Coordinate with the designated GBV Programme Focal Point and other relevant staff to identify and address protection risks associated with project activities.
- Comply with IHH's Code of Conduct, safeguarding policies, Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) procedures and confidentiality requirements.
- Ensure that sensitive complaints, safeguarding concerns and other incidents are reported and referred through established organizational channels.
- Promote responsible data management and ensure that beneficiary information is collected, stored and shared only for authorized purposes.

**REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE**

- Bachelor's degree in Agriculture, Agricultural Engineering, Agronomy, Economics, Business Administration, Development Studies or another relevant discipline.
- At least 3 years of relevant professional experience in implementing or coordinating humanitarian Food Security and Livelihoods (FSL/FSAL) activities.
- Demonstrated experience in at least one of the following areas: cash-based food assistance, agricultural support, livelihoods programming or food security interventions. Experience across multiple areas is an advantage.
- Experience in activity planning, field implementation, beneficiary selection and verification, monitoring, documentation and reporting.
- Experience coordinating with field teams, technical specialists, service providers, local authorities and community representatives.
- Familiarity with beneficiary accountability, feedback and complaints mechanisms, protection mainstreaming and safeguarding principles.
- Experience working with local or international humanitarian organizations in Syria is strongly preferred.
- Experience with donor-funded projects and familiarity with donor compliance and reporting requirements are an advantage.
- Strong organizational, analytical, communication and problem-solving skills.
- Good working knowledge of Microsoft Office, particularly Excel and Word. Familiarity with digital data-collection and monitoring tools is an advantage.
- Ability to analyze field information, prepare clear reports and follow up on implementation issues.
- Ability to conduct regular field visits and work effectively in a challenging operational environment.
- Fluency in Arabic and excellent proficiency in English, both written and spoken, are essential. Knowledge of Turkish is an advantage.

**CORE COMPETENCIES**

- Planning, coordination and implementation of FSAL activities.
- Food security, cash assistance and livelihoods programme follow-up.
- Coordination of agricultural support and irrigation-related interventions.
- Operational monitoring and results-based reporting.
- Beneficiary verification, documentation and accountability.
- Team coordination and stakeholder engagement.
- Analytical thinking, problem-solving and attention to detail.
- Organization, time management and ability to prioritize competing tasks.
- Integrity, confidentiality and commitment to humanitarian principles.
- Compliance with safeguarding, PSEA and protection requirements.

**WORKING CONDITIONS**

The position will be based at the IHH Idlib Office, with regular field visits to Abul Thohur, Idleb Governorate, and Madiq Castle, Hama Governorate, according to project implementation needs. The successful candidate must be able to coordinate effectively with field teams, beneficiaries, service providers and local stakeholders and travel to project locations when required.

jobs.title: Field Engineer
jobs.description:
**JOB DESCRIPTION**

**PROJECT**

Integrated Shelter, Food Security and Livelihoods Support for Safe, Dignified and Sustainable Return in Abul Thohur (Idleb) and Madiq Castle (Hama)

**DUTY STATION**

Idlib, Syria, with regular field visits to Abul Thohur and Madiq Castle

**ABOUT THE PROJECT**

IHH is implementing an integrated humanitarian and early-recovery project funded by the OCHA Syria Humanitarian Fund (SHF), supporting safe, dignified and sustainable return in Abul Thohur, Idleb Governorate, and Madiq Castle, Hama Governorate.

The project combines shelter rehabilitation, winterization and Core NFI assistance, cash assistance for food, bakery rehabilitation and subsidized bread provision, and agricultural and irrigation-related interventions. The Field Engineer will contribute specifically to the shelter rehabilitation and FSAL components.

**JOB SUMMARY**

IHH is seeking two Field Engineers to support the technical assessment, planning, implementation, supervision and verification of shelter rehabilitation activities under the project.

The positions focus on 150 conflict-damaged houses: 100 moderately damaged houses supported through Cash for Shelter and 50 heavily damaged but technically repairable houses rehabilitated through a contractor-led modality.

The Field Engineers will conduct household-level technical assessments, prepare Bills of Quantities (BoQs) and technical documentation, monitor rehabilitation works, verify quantities and quality, support Housing, Land and Property (HLP) due diligence, and maintain complete records in coordination with the Project Manager and field teams.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Technical Assessments and Engineering Documentation**

- Conduct household-level technical assessments of damaged houses in Abul Thohur and Madiq Castle.
- Assess structural and non-structural damage and classify houses in accordance with project eligibility criteria and applicable Shelter/NFI Sector guidance.
- Determine whether houses are technically suitable for rehabilitation and identify cases that are unsafe or beyond the approved scope.
- Prepare individual BoQs, technical specifications, cost estimates and clear scopes of work for approved housing units.
- For Cash for Shelter cases, verify the rehabilitation scope and technical documentation used to establish the assistance value and monitor progress against agreed works.
- For heavily damaged houses, prepare the required engineering documentation and support submission for review and approval by the Engineers Syndicate before implementation, as required.
- Maintain accurate assessment forms, measurements, drawings where required, and dated photographic evidence.

**Supervision of Rehabilitation Works**

- Conduct regular field visits to monitor rehabilitation progress and compliance with approved scopes, BoQs and technical specifications.
- Provide technical follow-up and field supervision for irrigation channel rehabilitation works, verifying implementation against approved engineering studies, technical specifications, quantities and quality requirements.
- Conduct technical assessments of the bakery and prepare the necessary engineering studies, designs, BoQs, cost estimates and technical specifications for its repair and rehabilitation, as required.
- Provide technical follow-up and field supervision for bakery repair and rehabilitation works, checking construction activities, materials, workmanship and completion against the approved scope and BoQ.
- Monitor contractor-led rehabilitation of heavily damaged houses, checking workmanship, materials and compliance with approved requirements.
- Provide technical follow-up and field supervision for the rehabilitation and repair of irrigation channels, verifying works against approved technical specifications, quantities and quality requirements.
- Provide technical follow-up and field supervision for bakery repair and rehabilitation works, checking construction activities, materials, workmanship and completion against the approved scope and BoQ.
- Measure and verify completed quantities against approved BoQs and document discrepancies, incomplete works or deviations.
- Identify technical defects, recommend corrective measures and follow up until issues are resolved.
- Monitor work schedules and promptly report delays, access constraints, risks or other implementation issues to the Project Manager.
- Ensure that changes to approved scopes or additional works are not undertaken without the required technical review and authorization.

**Quality Assurance, Inspection and Handover**

- Conduct inspections at appropriate stages of rehabilitation to verify quality and identify defects.
- Use relevant technical checklists and maintain records of inspections, findings and corrective actions.
- Carry out final technical inspections and confirm that works are completed in accordance with the approved scope before acceptance.
- Prepare or contribute to completion certificates and handover documentation, as applicable to the rehabilitation modality.
- Ensure that required photographs and technical records are complete and properly archived for each housing unit.

**Housing, Land and Property (HLP) Due Diligence**

- Support HLP due diligence before rehabilitation works are approved, in accordance with project procedures.
- Review available ownership and occupancy documents and record the household’s relationship to the housing unit.
- Verify that required owner consent and other applicable documentation are obtained before works begin.
- Refer unclear tenure, competing claims, property disputes or other HLP concerns to the designated focal point and ensure that unresolved cases are not advanced without the required clearance.
- Maintain accurate and confidential HLP records.

**Safety, Protection and Inclusive Rehabilitation**

- Promote safe implementation and apply the principles of do no harm, protection mainstreaming and non-discrimination during assessments and rehabilitation.
- Consider privacy, accessibility and the needs of older persons, persons with disabilities and other at-risk households when reviewing rehabilitation scopes.
- Where explosive-ordnance contamination is a concern, confirm that required site-safety checks and relevant risk-education measures have been completed in coordination with designated actors before works begin.
- Report unsafe conditions, serious technical risks, safeguarding concerns and incidents through established IHH procedures.
- Comply with IHH’s Code of Conduct, safeguarding requirements, Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) procedures and confidentiality standards.

**Coordination, Monitoring and Reporting**

- Coordinate closely with the Project Manager, other engineers, field assistants, beneficiaries, contractors and relevant local stakeholders.
- Explain approved technical scopes and requirements clearly to beneficiaries and contractors and report changes in site conditions promptly.
- Prepare regular technical updates covering assessments, BoQs, inspections, verified quantities, implementation progress and outstanding issues.
- Provide technical verification and supporting documentation for completed works to inform payment and financial-control procedures.
- Maintain up-to-date electronic and hard-copy records for each housing unit and contribute technical information to project reports, monitoring and audits.
- Promptly escalate suspected irregularities, quality concerns, deviations from approved procedures and other significant risks.

**REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE**

- Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering or Architectural Engineering.
- At least three years of relevant experience in construction supervision, building rehabilitation, shelter programming or a similar engineering position.
- Demonstrated experience in technical assessments, damage classification, preparation of BoQs, cost estimates, technical specifications and inspection reports.
- Practical experience monitoring construction or rehabilitation works and verifying quantities, materials and workmanship.
- Good knowledge of building rehabilitation methods, construction materials, technical standards and quality-control procedures.
- Experience in humanitarian shelter rehabilitation in Syria or with an international or local NGO is strongly preferred.
- Experience in Cash for Shelter and contractor-led rehabilitation is an advantage.
- Experience supervising irrigation channel rehabilitation, irrigation infrastructure or water-distribution works is an advantage.
- Experience supervising bakery rehabilitation, building repair or similar small-scale infrastructure works is an advantage.
- Familiarity with HLP due diligence and rehabilitation documentation is an advantage.
- Proficiency in AutoCAD and Microsoft Office, particularly Word and Excel.
- Strong reporting, documentation, organizational and problem-solving skills, with the ability to work independently in the field.
- Fluency in Arabic and excellent proficiency in English, both written and spoken, are essential. Knowledge of Turkish is an advantage.

**CORE COMPETENCIES**

- Technical assessment and damage classification.
- Preparation and verification of BoQs and technical specifications.
- Construction supervision and quality assurance.
- Technical follow-up of irrigation infrastructure and bakery rehabilitation works.
- Contractor coordination and verification of completed quantities.
- Accurate technical documentation and reporting.
- Problem-solving, attention to detail, planning and time management.
- Communication, teamwork, integrity and accountability.
- Commitment to safety, safeguarding, PSEA and protection mainstreaming.

**WORKING CONDITIONS**

The positions will be based at the IHH Idlib Office, with regular field visits to Abul Thohur, Idleb Governorate, and Madiq Castle, Hama Governorate, according to project implementation needs. Candidates must be able to travel to project locations and work effectively with field teams.

jobs.title: Field Assistant
jobs.description:
**JOB DESCRIPTION**

**PROJECT**

Integrated Shelter, Food Security and Livelihoods Support for Safe, Dignified and Sustainable Return in Abul Thohur (Idleb) and Madiq Castle (Hama)

**DUTY STATION**

Idlib, Syria, with regular field visits to project locations

**ABOUT THE PROJECT**

IHH is implementing an integrated humanitarian and early-recovery project funded by the OCHA Syria Humanitarian Fund (SHF), supporting safe, dignified and sustainable return in Abul Thohur, Idleb Governorate, and Madiq Castle, Hama Governorate.

The project combines shelter rehabilitation, winterization and Core NFI assistance, cash assistance for food, bakery rehabilitation and subsidized bread provision, agricultural support for returning wheat farmers, and rehabilitation of community irrigation infrastructure. These complementary interventions aim to address urgent household needs, restore essential infrastructure, protect agricultural livelihoods and strengthen community recovery.

**JOB SUMMARY**

IHH is seeking two Field Assistants to support the implementation, monitoring and documentation of project activities in the targeted communities. The Field Assistants will play a key role in day-to-day field operations, maintaining regular contact with beneficiaries and community representatives, supporting field assessments and verification, monitoring activity progress, collecting accurate information and reporting field findings to the relevant Project Officer or designated supervisor.

The position will involve frequent field visits and practical support across the project's activities, particularly food assistance, agricultural support, bakery rehabilitation and subsidized bread provision, irrigation infrastructure rehabilitation, and shelter-related activities when assigned. The Field Assistants will help ensure that activities are implemented according to approved plans, targeting criteria and organizational procedures, while promoting accountability, inclusion, protection and respectful engagement with affected communities.

The role requires strong communication and organizational skills, attention to detail, the ability to collect and document field information accurately, and readiness to work regularly in project locations. The Field Assistant will support implementation and follow-up rather than assume the technical, managerial or financial approval responsibilities of other project staff.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Field Implementation and Activity Follow-up**

- Conduct regular field visits to project locations to support activity implementation, monitor progress and identify operational challenges.
- Assist the project team in organizing and implementing field activities according to approved work plans, schedules and procedures.
- Support field-level implementation and follow-up of cash-for-food assistance, including beneficiary communication, verification activities and monitoring of relevant implementation steps.
- Support agricultural activities targeting returning wheat farmers in Madiq Castle, including coordination with beneficiaries, follow-up on the delivery of agricultural inputs and documentation of participation in agricultural training.
- Follow up on bakery rehabilitation and subsidized bread activities in Abul Thohur by coordinating field visits, documenting progress and reporting operational issues to the responsible Project Officer and engineering staff.
- Support field monitoring of irrigation channel rehabilitation activities in Madiq Castle, documenting progress and communicating observations or concerns to the responsible Project Officer and Field Engineer.
- Assist with shelter-related field activities when assigned, including beneficiary communication, field visits, verification and documentation, without undertaking engineering assessments or technical certification.
- Report delays, access constraints, implementation gaps and other field challenges promptly to the direct supervisor.

**Beneficiary Outreach, Verification and Community Engagement**

- Support beneficiary outreach and communication in accordance with approved targeting criteria and project procedures.
- Assist with household visits, beneficiary verification, registration and data collection using approved forms and digital tools.
- Explain project activities, eligibility requirements, assistance modalities, schedules and available feedback channels to beneficiaries in clear and accessible language.
- Coordinate with community representatives, Community Committees and relevant local stakeholders to facilitate field activities and support transparent communication.
- Help identify barriers that may prevent vulnerable households, women, older persons and persons with disabilities from accessing project assistance, and report these barriers to the responsible staff.
- Maintain professional, impartial and respectful relationships with beneficiaries and community members.
- Refer complaints, sensitive protection concerns and requests requiring technical or managerial decisions through established reporting and referral channels.

**Field Monitoring, Data Collection and Reporting**

- Collect accurate and timely information on activity implementation, beneficiary participation, delivery progress and field-level challenges.
- Complete field visit forms, beneficiary verification records, monitoring checklists, attendance sheets and other required documentation.
- Record relevant observations and supporting evidence, including photographs where authorized and appropriate, in accordance with project procedures and data-protection requirements.
- Prepare concise field visit reports and regular updates covering activities completed, progress against plans, outstanding issues, beneficiary feedback and recommended follow-up actions.
- Submit reports and field documentation to the relevant Project Officer or designated supervisor within agreed deadlines.
- Verify the completeness and consistency of field records before submission and promptly report discrepancies or missing information.
- Support the collection of monitoring data and follow-up information required by the MEAL team, including participation in monitoring visits and beneficiary follow-up when assigned.
- Maintain organized field records and ensure that beneficiary information and supporting documents are handled confidentially.

**Coordination and Administrative Support**

- Coordinate daily with the relevant Project Officer, Field Engineers, Agronomists, Field Assistants and other project team members to facilitate field implementation.
- Communicate field observations and implementation needs to the responsible technical staff without making unauthorized technical or operational decisions.
- Assist in arranging field visits, beneficiary meetings, training sessions and other project activities.
- Support the preparation and organization of attendance lists, activity records, field visit schedules and supporting documents.
- Follow up on agreed action points with relevant team members and report outstanding issues to the direct supervisor.
- Support coordination with local authorities, community representatives and other relevant stakeholders as assigned.
- Perform other field-related duties relevant to the position as assigned by the direct supervisor and consistent with the project's objectives.

**Accountability, Protection and Safeguarding**

- Ensure that beneficiaries receive clear information about project activities, eligibility criteria, assistance arrangements and available complaints and feedback mechanisms.
- Encourage beneficiaries to share feedback and concerns through established channels and ensure that complaints are referred appropriately.
- Apply the principles of impartiality, non-discrimination, confidentiality and do no harm in all field activities.
- Respect the privacy and dignity of beneficiaries and obtain appropriate consent before collecting or sharing personal information or taking photographs.
- Follow IHH's Code of Conduct, safeguarding policies, Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) procedures and relevant reporting requirements.
- Report safeguarding concerns, suspected misconduct, security risks and other serious incidents through established organizational channels.
- Support safe and inclusive access to project activities, with particular attention to vulnerable and marginalized groups.

**REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE**

- Bachelor's degree or diploma in a relevant field, such as Business Administration, Social Sciences, Agriculture, Development Studies or another related discipline.
- At least 2 years of relevant professional experience in field implementation, community engagement, beneficiary follow-up, data collection or similar roles, preferably with a humanitarian organization.
- Previous experience supporting humanitarian activities in Syria, particularly in food security, livelihoods, agriculture, shelter or early recovery, is an advantage.
- Experience conducting field visits, communicating with beneficiaries, supporting verification processes and preparing field reports.
- Familiarity with beneficiary registration, data collection and documentation procedures.
- Basic knowledge of accountability to affected populations, complaints and feedback mechanisms, protection mainstreaming and safeguarding principles.
- Good working knowledge of Microsoft Office, particularly Word and Excel.
- Familiarity with KoboToolbox or other digital data-collection tools is an advantage.
- Strong communication, interpersonal and organizational skills, with the ability to work effectively with diverse communities.
- Ability to collect information accurately, prepare clear reports and follow instructions and established procedures.
- Ability to work independently in the field, manage competing priorities and travel regularly to project locations.
- Fluency in Arabic, both written and spoken, is essential. Working knowledge of English is an advantage.

**CORE COMPETENCIES**

- Field activity implementation and follow-up.
- Beneficiary communication and community engagement.
- Accurate data collection, verification and documentation.
- Field reporting and identification of implementation challenges.
- Coordination and teamwork.
- Organization, time management and attention to detail.
- Professional conduct, impartiality and confidentiality.
- Accountability to affected populations and commitment to humanitarian principles.
- Compliance with safeguarding, PSEA and protection requirements.

**WORKING CONDITIONS**

The position will be based at the IHH Idlib Office, with frequent field visits to Abul Thohur, Idleb Governorate, and Madiq Castle, Hama Governorate, according to project implementation needs. The successful candidates must be willing and able to work regularly in the field and coordinate closely with project teams, beneficiaries and local stakeholders.

jobs.title: Enumerator (Data Collector)
jobs.description:
**JOB DESCRIPTION**

**PROJECT**

Integrated Shelter, Food Security and Livelihoods Support for Safe, Dignified and Sustainable Return in Abul Thohur (Idleb) and Madiq Castle (Hama)

**DUTY STATION**

Idlib, Syria, with regular field visits to Abul Thohur and Madiq Castle

**ABOUT THE PROJECT**

IHH is implementing an integrated humanitarian and early-recovery project funded by the OCHA Syria Humanitarian Fund (SHF), supporting safe, dignified and sustainable return in Abul Thohur, Idleb Governorate, and Madiq Castle, Hama Governorate.

The project combines shelter rehabilitation, winterization and Core NFI assistance, cash assistance for food, bakery rehabilitation and subsidized bread provision, agricultural support for returning wheat farmers, and rehabilitation of community irrigation infrastructure. These activities aim to address urgent household needs, restore essential infrastructure and support agricultural livelihoods and community recovery.

**JOB SUMMARY**

IHH is seeking five Enumerators (Data Collectors) to support accurate, timely and ethical collection of household and activity-related data for the project. The Enumerators will conduct field interviews, household registration and verification, needs and vulnerability assessments, and monitoring data collection using approved tools and procedures.

The positions will support different project components, including shelter rehabilitation, winterization and Core NFI assistance, cash assistance for food, subsidized bread provision, agricultural support and irrigation-related activities, as assigned. Enumerators will work under the guidance of the relevant project and monitoring staff and will not make independent decisions on beneficiary eligibility or technical assessments.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Field Data Collection and Household Assessments**

- Conduct household visits, interviews and surveys in targeted communities in Abul Thohur and Madiq Castle, following approved plans, tools and instructions.
- Collect accurate demographic, socioeconomic, vulnerability and needs-related information from households and community members using digital or paper-based forms, as assigned.
- Support household registration, verification and assessment processes for relevant project activities, including shelter assistance, winterization, Core NFI, cash assistance for food and agricultural support.
- Explain the purpose of data collection, how the information will be used and the respondent’s right to decline or stop participation; obtain informed consent before starting interviews.
- Ensure that information is recorded accurately, completely and objectively, without leading respondents or making assumptions on their behalf.
- Use approved tools such as KoboToolbox or other designated data-collection applications, and upload or submit completed forms within the required timeframe.
- Conduct follow-up visits or calls when authorized to clarify missing or inconsistent information, while respecting confidentiality and approved procedures.

**Beneficiary Registration and Verification Support**

- Support the registration and verification of households according to approved procedures and assigned caseloads.
- Check available documents and household information against the approved checklist, and flag discrepancies or missing information to the responsible staff for review.
- Support the prevention of duplicate registrations by accurately recording required identifiers and reporting potential duplicates to the supervisor; do not independently approve or reject applicants.
- Provide clear and consistent information to community members about registration steps, assessment visits and where to obtain official information on eligibility and assistance.
- Ensure that all forms, supporting documents and records are handled securely and submitted only through authorized channels.

**Activity Monitoring and Follow-up**

- Support field monitoring, post-distribution or post-assistance monitoring, and follow-up surveys as requested by the project or MEAL team.
- Support the MEAL team, when requested, in conducting monitoring visits, assessments, surveys, data verification exercises and other monitoring or evaluation activities, following approved methodologies, tools and instructions.
- Collect information related to assistance receipt, beneficiary experience, access barriers, satisfaction and feedback using approved questionnaires.
- Where assigned, assist with recording observations related to shelter rehabilitation, cash assistance, bakery and subsidized bread activities, agricultural support or irrigation-related interventions, without conducting engineering or agronomic assessments outside the role.
- Immediately report field access issues, complaints, protection concerns, suspected fraud, data inconsistencies or other implementation issues to the designated supervisor through established channels.
- Participate in team briefings and debriefings to review data-collection instructions, discuss challenges and correct identified errors.

**Data Quality, Reporting and Coordination**

- Review each completed form before submission to ensure that required questions are answered and information is internally consistent.
- Meet assigned daily or weekly data-collection targets while maintaining data quality and respectful engagement with respondents.
- Keep accurate records of completed interviews, unsuccessful visits, follow-up requirements and other assigned field activities.
- Coordinate daily with the designated supervisor, Field Assistants and relevant project or MEAL staff regarding schedules, locations and data-collection progress.
- Attend required training sessions on data-collection tools, assessment methodologies, safeguarding, protection and confidentiality.
- Perform other relevant data-collection and field-support duties assigned by the supervisor within the scope of the position.

**Protection, Safeguarding and Confidentiality**

- Treat all respondents with dignity, respect and impartiality, without discrimination based on gender, age, disability, displacement status or other characteristics.
- Apply the do-no-harm principle and ensure that interviews are conducted in a safe and appropriate manner, taking account of privacy and respondents’ comfort.
- Maintain strict confidentiality of personal and household information and never share data, photographs or documents through unauthorized channels.
- Comply with IHH’s Code of Conduct, safeguarding policies and Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) requirements.
- Report safeguarding concerns, protection risks and sensitive complaints promptly through established organizational procedures; do not investigate sensitive cases independently.
- Inform respondents about available feedback and complaints channels when appropriate and refer questions or complaints to the designated staff.

**REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE**

- At least a secondary school certificate; a baccalaureate or university qualification in social sciences, statistics, agriculture, engineering or another relevant field is an advantage.
- Previous experience in field data collection, household surveys, registration, assessments or monitoring is preferred; experience with a humanitarian organization is an advantage.
- Previous experience supporting Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL) activities, including monitoring visits, assessments, post-assistance monitoring or data-quality checks, is an advantage.
- Basic experience using smartphones or tablets and digital data-collection tools. Familiarity with KoboToolbox, KoboCollect, ODK or similar platforms is an advantage.
- Good Arabic communication skills and the ability to communicate respectfully with households and community members.
- Basic English reading skills are an advantage, particularly for understanding forms and instructions.
- Good attention to detail and the ability to record information accurately and objectively.
- Ability to maintain confidentiality and follow data-protection, safeguarding and informed-consent procedures.
- Ability and willingness to travel regularly to project locations in Abul Thohur and Madiq Castle and work in field conditions.
- Ability to work effectively in a team, follow instructions and meet agreed deadlines.
- Residence in or familiarity with the target locations and surrounding communities is an advantage.

**CORE COMPETENCIES**

- Accurate and ethical data collection.
- Attention to detail and data quality.
- Respectful communication and community engagement.
- Confidentiality and responsible handling of personal information.
- Ability to follow procedures and meet deadlines.
- Teamwork, reliability and flexibility.
- Commitment to humanitarian principles, safeguarding and accountability.

**WORKING CONDITIONS**

The positions will be based in Idlib, Syria, with regular field visits to project locations in Abul Thohur, Idleb Governorate, and Madiq Castle, Hama Governorate. Enumerators must be able to travel to targeted communities and conduct fieldwork in accordance with approved access and security procedures. The role may require flexible working hours depending on field schedules and assessment needs.

jobs.title: Agronomist
jobs.description:
**JOB DESCRIPTION**

**PROJECT**

Integrated Shelter, Food Security and Livelihoods Support for Safe, Dignified and Sustainable Return in Abul Thohur (Idleb) and Madiq Castle (Hama)

**DUTY STATION**

Idlib, Syria, with regular field visits to Madiq Castle, Hama Governorate, and other project locations as required

**ABOUT THE PROJECT**

IHH is implementing an integrated humanitarian and early-recovery project funded by the OCHA Syria Humanitarian Fund (SHF), supporting safe, dignified and sustainable return in Abul Thohur, Idleb Governorate, and Madiq Castle, Hama Governorate.

The project combines shelter rehabilitation, winterization and Core NFI assistance, cash assistance for food, bakery rehabilitation and subsidized bread provision, and agricultural and irrigation-related interventions. The agricultural component focuses on supporting wheat farmers and improving access to irrigation water through community-level rehabilitation and coordination.

**JOB SUMMARY**

IHH is seeking two qualified and motivated Agronomists to support the planning, implementation, monitoring and reporting of agricultural and livelihood activities under the project, with a particular focus on supporting wheat farmers in Madiq Castle, Hama Governorate.

The Agronomists will work closely with the FSAL Project Officer, Field Engineer, Field Assistants and MEAL team, as well as farmers, community representatives, relevant agricultural authorities and other stakeholders. They will provide agricultural technical guidance, support beneficiary assessment and verification, follow up on agricultural inputs and activities, and contribute to coordination around irrigation-related interventions.

The role focuses on agricultural and farmer-support expertise. Engineering designs, Bills of Quantities (BoQs), construction specifications and technical supervision of civil works remain the responsibility of the Field Engineer and other qualified engineering staff.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Agricultural Activity Implementation and Farmer Support**

- Support the planning and implementation of agricultural and livelihood activities in line with the approved project proposal, work plan, targets and technical guidance.
- Conduct field visits and consultations with wheat farmers to understand agricultural needs, production constraints, seasonal priorities and access to irrigation water.
- Provide practical technical guidance to farmers on appropriate agricultural practices, crop management, input use and other relevant measures to support wheat production, within the scope of the project.
- Support the identification and verification of eligible farming households in accordance with approved selection criteria and procedures, ensuring accurate documentation and transparent processes.
- Assist in assessing farmers’ needs for agricultural inputs or services and contribute technical recommendations for activity planning and implementation.
- Follow up on the delivery and use of project-supported agricultural inputs or services, where applicable, and document field observations and implementation issues.
- Facilitate farmer awareness sessions, demonstrations or training activities on relevant agricultural practices when included in the approved activity plan.
- Identify implementation challenges affecting farmers and raise them promptly with the FSAL Project Officer, recommending practical corrective actions.

**Irrigation and Agricultural Infrastructure Coordination**

- Coordinate with farmers, water users, community representatives and relevant local authorities on agricultural water needs and irrigation-related activities.
- Work closely with the Field Engineer to ensure that the agricultural needs of farmers are communicated and considered during the planning and implementation of irrigation-channel rehabilitation.
- Support field-level consultations on irrigation access, water distribution arrangements and the practical use of rehabilitated infrastructure, in coordination with relevant stakeholders.
- Help document farmer feedback and potential agricultural benefits or constraints related to irrigation interventions.
- Refer engineering assessments, designs, BoQs, construction methods and infrastructure quality concerns to the Field Engineer; do not approve engineering designs or civil works outside the role’s technical competence.

**Beneficiary Engagement, Monitoring and Reporting**

- Communicate project objectives, eligibility criteria, activity schedules and relevant procedures clearly and respectfully to farmers and communities.
- Collect and maintain accurate records related to farmer assessments, beneficiary verification, field visits, training sessions and agricultural activities, using approved tools and templates.
- Coordinate with the MEAL team to support baseline or needs assessments, routine monitoring, post-assistance monitoring, data verification and other evaluation activities as required.
- Contribute to tracking project indicators and targets by providing timely, accurate and verifiable field information and supporting documentation.
- Prepare regular field updates and activity reports, highlighting progress, challenges, community feedback, lessons learned and follow-up actions.
- Ensure that feedback and complaints received from farmers are documented and referred through the established feedback and complaints mechanisms.

**Coordination and Teamwork**

- Coordinate day-to-day with the FSAL Project Officer, Field Engineer, Field Assistants and MEAL colleagues to ensure coherent planning, implementation and follow-up of project activities.
- Maintain constructive working relationships with farmers, farmer groups, community representatives, relevant agricultural departments and local authorities.
- Participate in project meetings, field coordination visits and technical discussions as requested by the FSAL Project Officer or Project Manager.
- Coordinate with procurement, logistics and other support teams through the relevant project staff to communicate technical requirements and ensure timely activity implementation.
- Perform other relevant duties within the scope of the position as assigned by the line manager.

**Protection, Safeguarding and Accountability**

- Apply the principles of impartiality, non-discrimination, accountability to affected populations and do no harm in all interactions with farmers and communities.
- Promote safe, inclusive and equitable participation, with attention to vulnerable farmers and households facing barriers to accessing assistance.
- Comply with IHH’s Code of Conduct, safeguarding policies, Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) procedures and confidentiality requirements.
- Ensure that personal and beneficiary information is collected, stored and shared only for authorized project purposes.
- Report safeguarding concerns, protection risks or other incidents through established organizational channels.

**REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE**

- Bachelor’s degree in Agriculture, Agricultural Engineering, Agronomy or another closely related discipline.
- At least two years of relevant professional experience in agricultural activities, farmer support, agricultural extension, food security or livelihoods programming.
- Practical understanding of crop production and agricultural practices relevant to wheat farming and rural livelihoods.
- Experience conducting field visits, engaging with farmers, collecting information and documenting agricultural needs or activity progress.
- Ability to communicate technical information clearly and respectfully to farmers and community members.
- Experience working with local or international humanitarian or development organizations in Syria is an advantage.
- Experience supporting irrigation-related activities, water users’ coordination, agricultural input assistance or farmer training is an advantage.
- Knowledge of monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning (MEAL) processes, digital data-collection tools or beneficiary verification is an advantage.
- Good organizational, communication, reporting and problem-solving skills, with attention to detail and accurate record-keeping.
- Good working knowledge of Microsoft Office. Familiarity with KoboToolbox or similar data-collection tools is an advantage.
- Fluency in Arabic is required. Good English skills, particularly for reading technical materials and preparing reports, are an advantage.
- Ability to conduct frequent field visits and work effectively in rural locations and a challenging operational environment.

**CORE COMPETENCIES**

- Agricultural technical knowledge and farmer-support skills.
- Field assessment, beneficiary verification and community engagement.
- Understanding of wheat production and agricultural livelihoods.
- Coordination with farmers, local authorities and multidisciplinary project teams.
- Field monitoring, documentation and results-based reporting.
- Communication, teamwork, problem-solving and attention to detail.
- Integrity, confidentiality and commitment to humanitarian principles.
- Compliance with safeguarding, PSEA and protection requirements.

**WORKING CONDITIONS**

The positions will be based at the IHH Idlib Office, with regular field visits to Madiq Castle, Hama Governorate, and other project locations as required. The Agronomists will report to the FSAL Project Officer and work in close coordination with the Field Engineer, Field Assistants, MEAL team and Project Manager.

jobs.title: Country Directore
jobs.company: Medecins du Monde - Turkey / Dunya Doktorlari Dernegi
jobs.description:
**Dünya Doktorları Derneği**

Dünya Doktorları Derneği (DDD / MdM Türkiye) is a Turkish international health organization working to improve access to healthcare, strengthen local health systems, and support vulnerable populations.

DDD operates through its headquarters in Istanbul and its country missions, combining operational implementation with technical expertise and institutional partnerships.

The General Services Department provides the institutional infrastructure, administrative services, and digital working environment required for the effective functioning of the Turkish offices.

DDD is the 16th member of the Doctors of the World International Network that is committed to meeting the health needs of vulnerable people globally.

Please visit [www.dunyadoktorlari.org.tr](http://www.dunyadoktorlari.org.tr) to learn more.

**About the Position**

DDD is seeking an experienced Country Director to lead the establishment, consolidation and development of its operations in Syria.

The Country Director will provide strategic, institutional and managerial leadership, positioning DDD as a technical cooperation agency supporting the restoration and strengthening of local healthcare systems.

The position combines institutional engagement, country strategy development, resource mobilization and overall supervision of country operations.

**Key Responsibilities**

- **Country Strategy & Positioning:** Develop and implement DDD's country strategy, identify operational priorities and strengthen its institutional presence.
- **Institutional Relations:** Represent DDD before government authorities, healthcare institutions, international cooperation agencies, donors and strategic partners.
- **Operations Leadership:** Oversee country operations, field offices and multidisciplinary teams, ensuring effective coordination, performance and resource allocation.
- **Program Oversight:** Ensure that the country portfolio responds to health system priorities, institutional needs and DDD's technical and quality standards.
- **Resource Mobilization:** Develop funding opportunities, institutional partnerships and strategic alliances in coordination with headquarters.
- **Financial & Organizational Management:** Oversee budgets, financial sustainability, workforce planning and organizational development.
- **Risk & Compliance:** Ensure appropriate security, access, legal compliance and risk management arrangements.
- **Executive Coordination:** Maintain effective coordination with DDD headquarters and report on country performance, priorities and strategic developments.

**Required Qualifications & Experience**

- University degree in Management, Public Administration, International Cooperation, Public Health, International Relations or a related field.
- At least 8 years of progressively responsible experience, including significant senior management responsibilities.
- Demonstrated experience in institutional representation, government engagement and strategic partnership development.
- Proven ability to lead multidisciplinary teams, oversee complex operations and manage substantial budgets.
- Experience in international cooperation, public sector development, technical assistance or comparable operational environments.
- Strong strategic planning, negotiation, financial oversight and organizational leadership skills.
- Experience in healthcare systems strengthening or health-related cooperation is a strong advantage.
- Experience in Syria or comparable complex environments is highly desirable.
- Professional fluency in Arabic and English.

Experience in international NGOs is welcome but not mandatory. Candidates from technical cooperation agencies, public institutions and other relevant sectors are encouraged to apply.

**Candidate Profile**

We are looking for a strategic and operational leader with strong institutional diplomacy, sound managerial judgment and the ability to establish and develop an effective country organization.

The successful candidate will combine institutional credibility, strategic vision and practical management capabilities, with a strong commitment to sustainable healthcare systems development.

**Compliance & Ethics**

Promote and encourage a culture of compliance and ethics throughout Dünya Doktorları Derneği. As applicable to the position, maintains a clear understanding of Dünya Doktorları Derneği and donor compliance and ethics standards and adheres to those standards. Conducts work with the highest level of integrity. Communicates these values to staff and to partners and requires them to adhere to these values.

**Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse**

Actively promote PSEA (Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse) standards within Dünya Doktorları Derneği and amongst beneficiaries served by Dünya Doktorları Derneği.

**NB:** Considering the purpose and values of the organisation, DDD requests to its employee complete flexibility in term of duties and commitment, as their job description and job title can be adjusted throughout the year according to needs and priorities.

Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis.Please be advised that female candidates are highly encouraged.

*Dünya Doktorları Derneği is an equal opportunity employer whereby we ensure all hiring and employment decisions, and operates all programs, services, and functions without the practices that discriminate against any person employed or seeking employment based on race, colour, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national or ethnic origin, age, marital status, disability, genetic information or any other status or characteristic protected under applicable law.*

**Closure Date: 1**0.11.2026

Due to the urgency to fill this post, DDD reserves the right to review the CVs on a rolling basis and selected candidates may be interviewed prior to the closing dates listed, therefore early applications are encouraged.
DDD is not in a position to respond to every applicant individually due to the anticipated high number of applications.
Please note that only short-listed candidates will be contacted for the first interview.

Any offer made to the candidate in relation to this vacancy notice is subject to funding confirmation.

**General Information**
DDD retains the discretion to re-advertise the vacancy, to cancel the recruitment, to offer a contract with a modified job description or for a different duration, or to offer a contract at a lower grade.
