jobs.description:
**Join MSF OCG as a RMP for Cell 1 !**

**We are looking for passionate candidates ready to contribute to our humanitarian mission.**

**Below, you will find the job details and the qualifications we are looking for.**

## Inclusivity and Diversity at MSF

Do your qualifications and experience not exactly match all requirements of the job?

At MSF OCG, we are committed to an inclusive culture that supports and amplifies the diverse voices of our staff members. We strive to create workplaces where teams of people with diverse backgrounds, characteristics, perspectives, ideas and experiences work together to advance MSF's social mission and create better outcomes for our patients and the communities we work with.

We understand that some people may hesitate to apply for employment if they don't meet all listed job requirements. Research shows that this is especially true for women. If you believe your profile is a good match for this position, we invite you to apply even if you don’t fulfil every listed qualification.

We encourage applications from individuals of all genders, ages, sexual orientations, ethnicities, background, religions, beliefs, ability status, and all other diversity characteristics.

MSF does not tolerate sexual exploitation and abuse, any kind of discrimination or harassment, including sexual harassment. All selected candidates will undergo reference checks.

## Context & mission

Médecins Sans Frontières is an independent, international medical and humanitarian organization that provides care to people in need, people affected by natural or man-made disasters, and victims of armed conflict, without discrimination and without regard to race, religion, creed or political affiliation (MSF Charter).

The MSF movement is built around 5 operational centers supported by 24 sections and offices worldwide. MSF Operational Center Geneva (MSF OCG) is one of these centers.

OCG has established a matrix organisation to support its field operations. Operational cells act as the direct interface with the field, providing supervision and operational support, while specialised departments contribute technical expertise. Each cell is a multidisciplinary team coordinated by a Programme Manager (PM/RP – Responsable de Programmes) and composed of a Deputy Programme Manager (DPM/ARP), a medical profile (RMP), and representatives from logistics, finance, human resources, communications and supply. This position is part of Cell 1, which supports field operations in Sudan, South Sudan and Ethiopia.

Within this structure, the RMP reports hierarchically to the Programme Manager and works in close collaboration with the Medical Department, under the technical supervision of the Deputy Medical Director (DMD). The RMP acts as a key link between Operations and the Medical Department, ensuring coherent and relevant medical support to field operations, while providing strategic and technical guidance to Medical Coordinators.

## Scope of Responsibilities

- Define strategic medico-operational priorities to respond to specific medico-humanitarian situations, whether in emergencies or protracted crises.
- Support the implementation of current projects across different countries by acting as a technical referent for Medical Coordinators in the field and advising the A/RP in the cell.
- Bring in technical expertise from the Medical Department to enable integrated work between the Operations and Medical Departments. This is achieved by creating collaborative platforms focusing on specific medico-operational challenges, the selection of standards and the improvement of practices.
- Plan medical resources and ensure their coherence with medico-operational objectives. This requires a collaborative approach with other departments (HR, Finance, Logistics, Supply). While this work takes place regularly during programme implementation, it represents a greater share of the workload during annual planning and mid-year reviews, when resources are planned and reviewed.
- Filter and prioritize field requests for support, considering the needs identified in projects and their capacity to absorb additional support at any given time.
- Evaluate and adjust medico-humanitarian projects by monitoring medical and project indicators, debriefing field teams, conducting field visits and monitoring the broader medical situation in countries of operation. Based on this, and jointly with in-country medical teams, propose project adjustments to operational colleagues in the field or at headquarters.

## Responsibilities, Tasks and Duties

**Towards the coordination and the cell:**

- Ensures the medical pertinence and adequacy of the projects with the MedCo.
- Matches medical and institutional ambitions with operational reality and needs in the field (adaptability, feasibility).
- Contributes to the development of medical policies and strategies by sharing context-specific experiences and by checking their field adequacy.
- Supports country programmes in the development of a medical advocacy and/or operational research agenda.
- Contributes, through their health and medical experience, to the definition of objectives and intervention strategies adapted to the project's context, particularly through direct support to coordination (Medical Coordinator):
- Shares their health and medical experience to determine the intervention strategies.
- Advises the Medical Coordinator in terms of needs assessments and analysis of medical data gathered during assessments.
- Checks the coherence between medical resources and medico-operational objectives.
- Validates job profiles and skills and approves matching according to the matching process rules.
- Supervises the Medical Coordinator in terms of adequate monitoring of field pharmacy management (and kit management), the proper implementation of national staff health policies and compliance with medical supply rules.
- Participates in the process of approving a project through the consolidation of project documents (PoA, project committee, definition of objectives and indicators, adequate means and resources, logical framework and realistic timeframes).
- Follows up on the monitoring of medical activities and provides medical follow-up for projects through systematic analysis, feedback on sitreps, quarterly and annual reports and regular project visits.
- Supervises field analysis of the epidemiological context of the countries under their charge.
- Participates in the capitalisation of field experiences and technical support needs, identifying obstacles to good medical practices in the projects, and promotes or puts forward proposals for innovative technical tools in order to facilitate medical work.

**Responding to Medico-Operational Needs:**

- Ensures that medical fundamentals are met and that medical support is contextualized within the framework of good practices and the implementation of minimum standards.
- Contributes, through the process of consolidation and prioritization of medical support needs, to the yearly PoA objectives and activities and the programming of additional support and expertise priorities. Matches them to the capacities of the Medical Department, depending on the specificity and required investment.
- Provides direct technical support and guidance to the Medical Coordinator regarding all aspects of their function, through advice, coaching and transfer of knowledge and skills.
- Ensures medical solutions (protocols, minimum standards, best practices, guidelines, innovative tools, etc.) are properly implemented in the field.
- Is responsible for the adaptation of tools and means to the needs, making sure they provide a benefit for operations.
- Creates space for matching medical recommendations to operational reality, monitors the integration of medical policies depending on the context and guides the Medical Coordinator in developing the resulting strategies.

**Towards the Collaborative Platforms and the Medical Department:**

- Identifies the needs in terms of expertise to be developed by the Medical Department and contributes to the improvement of medical practices.
- Participates in and/or facilitates thematic forums/collaborative platforms and medical seminars, including with the Medical Department during PoA development, and for deeper moments of medical reflection such as an annual results review.
- Encourages and proposes the development of operational research projects: informs and updates Medical Coordinators, identifies operational research needs, integrates them into operational objectives, ensures follow-up and participates in the drafting of scientific articles linked to results obtained in the field.
- Undertakes advocacy initiatives, provides medical documentation on populations in distress and liaises with the Access to Essential Medicines Campaign.
- Participates in the annual exercise to rationalize and prioritize project support needs in collaboration with L&D and DMed.

In line with the OCG Collaborative Teamwork Framework 2026, the role is expected to evolve towards a stronger focus on mentoring and supporting field teams. Responsibilities may be adapted accordingly as the framework is progressively implemented.

## Your profile

*Education*

- Medical doctor or nurse.
- Medical or paramedical degree.
- A diploma in Tropical Medicine, Public/International Health or Epidemiology is an asset.

*Experience*

- 3 – 5 years professional experience in developing countries.
- A diversity of MSF experience, possibly as a Medical Coordinator or similar medical managerial position in another health organization.
- Knowledge of recent developments in the field of humanitarian relief, international public health and tropical medicine.
- Experience with field research in resource poor settings is an asset.
- Proven affinity with advocacy.

*Languages*

jobs.title: Senior Manager, Donor Support - Individual Giving
jobs.description:
**Opportunity Type:**

Regular

**Summary:**

At Habitat for Humanity International, we believe everyone deserves a decent place to live. As Senior Manager, Donor Support, Individual Giving, you will play a critical role in advancing our mission by supporting the Planned Giving program and helping build meaningful, lasting relationships with donors who are investing in Habitat’s future.
This role serves as a key partner to Planned Giving Officers, providing operational, donor engagement, reporting, and marketing support that helps deliver an exceptional donor experience. You will work across fundraising, marketing, finance, and operations to ensure donor inquiries are addressed promptly, campaigns run effectively, and reporting and data systems support informed decision-making.

**Key Responsibilities:**

**Why This Role Matters**

Planned gifts help create long-term, sustainable impact for families and communities around the world. In this role, you will help strengthen donor relationships, improve fundraising operations, maintain data integrity, and provide the reporting and insights needed to support strategic growth across the Planned Giving program.

**What You'll Do**

· Serve as a primary operational partner to Planned Giving Officers, helping manage donor inquiries and ensuring timely, donor-centered responses.

· Support the Legacy Builders program through donor communications, recognition activities, participation tracking, and record maintenance.

· Coordinate planned giving marketing campaigns across print and digital channels, including lead generation, donor cultivation, and stewardship efforts.

· Maintain campaign calendars, project plans, audience files, vendor coordination, approvals, and campaign documentation.

· Track campaign performance and response data to support reporting, analysis, and future strategy.

· Reconcile fundraising revenue and gift activity between Finance reports and CRM systems, research discrepancies, and coordinate resolutions.

· Maintain recurring revenue reports and support forecasting processes.

· Populate and maintain dashboards, scorecards, KPI reports, and other fundraising performance tools.

· Monitor CRM data quality and work with gift officers to ensure accurate documentation of donor interactions, opportunities, and pipeline activity.

· Collaborate across teams to support fundraising operations, reporting, and strategic decision-making.

**What You'll Bring**

**Required Qualifications**

· Bachelor's degree or equivalent combination of education and relevant experience.

· 3-5 years of experience in fundraising, donor relations, donor services, fundraising operations, project management, nonprofit marketing, or a related field.

· Experience supporting fundraising programs, donor engagement activities, gift officers, or donor-facing operations.

· Experience working with fundraising CRMs such as Blackbaud CRM, Raiser's Edge, Salesforce, or similar systems.

· Strong analytical, organizational, and project management skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities and deadlines.

· Experience preparing and maintaining reports, dashboards, and performance metrics.

· Experience working with financial or fundraising revenue data and reconciliation processes.

· Strong attention to detail and commitment to data accuracy.

· Proficiency with Microsoft Excel, Word, PowerPoint, and other Microsoft Office applications.

· Excellent written and verbal communication skills and a strong customer service orientation.

· Ability to work independently and collaboratively within a complex organization.

**Preferred Qualifications**

· Background supporting planned giving, major gifts, or other relationship-based fundraising programs.

· Understanding of charitable gift planning concepts and planned giving donor pipelines.

· Demonstrated ability to communicate directly with donors and respond to donor inquiries.

· Track record of supporting fundraising teams and gift officers.

· Knowledge of multi-channel fundraising or donor marketing campaigns.

· Proven success managing campaign workflows, marketing data, project schedules, and vendor deliverables.

· Familiarity with fundraising revenue reconciliation and financial reporting practices.

· Expertise in maintaining dashboards, scorecards, pipeline reports, and fundraising performance metrics.

· Proficiency in CRM data quality management, bulk data uploads, segmentation files, and data validation.

· Experience navigating a federated or similarly complex organizational environment.

· Interest in building expertise in planned giving, donor engagement, fundraising operations, and nonprofit resource development.

**What We Offer**

Habitat for Humanity International offers the opportunity to do meaningful work alongside a mission-driven team committed to building strength, stability, and self-reliance through shelter. Team members receive a competitive total rewards package, professional development opportunities, and the chance to contribute to lasting global impact.

**Hiring Range:**

The actual salary offered for this role will be based on a variety of factors, including location, internal equity and the candidate’s qualifications and professional experience. HFHI offers a competitive, comprehensive benefits package that varies by country and typically includes vacation leave, sick leave, personal days, health insurance options, retirement plan contributions and life insurance. For work locations in the US, the hiring range for this position is:

$63,900.00 USD

\-

**About Us:**

Habitat for Humanity, founded in 1976, is a global, Christian-based nonprofit organization that grew out of an intentionally multi-racial community in rural Georgia. Seeking to put God’s love into action, Habitat brings together people of all faiths and people of no faith to build homes, communities and hope. Working alongside each other, we help families and individuals build and improve places to call home and achieve the strength, stability and self-reliance they need to build better lives for themselves. Habitat seeks individuals who have a willingness to affirm these principles and values.

At Habitat for Humanity International, we are compelled by our Koinonia roots to put God’s love for all into action and pursue housing equity and opportunity by bringing all people together to build community and drive impact. jobs.title: Consultancy services to produce a briefing paper on the law and practice of universal jurisdiction in South Africa.
jobs.description:
**BACKGROUND & OBJECTIVES**
TRIAL International is a non-governmental organization that fights impunity for international crimes
and supports victims in their pursuit of justice.
To support its activities, the organization is seeking a consultant to collect information, analyze and
draft, in English, a briefing paper on the law and practice of universal jurisdiction in South Africa.
This briefing paper will be part of the Universal Jurisdiction Law and Practice Briefing Papers series,
comprising 12 reports comparing the legal systems of Germany, England and Wales, Argentina,
Belgium, Canada, the United States, Finland, France, Norway, the Netherlands, Senegal, Sweden
and Switzerland.

**SCOPE OF SERVICES**
\- Collect information through desk research and interviews on the legal framework and practice
relevant to extraterritorial and universal jurisdiction in South Africa;
\- Analyze and compile the information collected;
\- Draft a report on “Universal Jurisdiction Law and Practice in South Africa”.

jobs.title: Programme Manager - Community Health
jobs.description:
**Position Overview**

SEED Madagascar is a medium-sized British NGO working in partnership with communities in the southeast of Madagascar. We are looking for a Programmes Manager to coordinate the development and management of our community health programme. This is a unique opportunity for a development professional with two to four years’ experience to take on greater responsibility for programme delivery, working alongside national and international colleagues to lead programme development, grant writing, reporting and evaluation.

The role would suit someone with experience in international development who is ready to take the next step in their career and develop their skills in managing a team and a portfolio of projects. The postholder will play an important role in shaping the continued development of SEED’s Community Health Programme, working closely with colleagues to ensure that our programmes are well designed, effectively delivered and responsive to the needs of the communities we work with.

Experience in grant writing, knowledge of community health and a minimum C1 level or equivalent in French are essential. The postholder must also be able to work in English to a high standard. Candidates who do not meet these essential requirements will not be considered.

SEED Madagascar is a British charity which integrates community health, WASH, rural livelihoods, schools and conservation programmes to support long-term, sustainable change. We are committed to high-quality programme delivery and to contributing to international best practice through research, learning and publication across our programme areas.

*Location:* Fort Dauphin, Anosy Region, Madagascar

*Contract minimum duration:* 2 years

*Probationary period:* 3 months

*Terms and conditions:* Local salary, plus £1,200 contribution to flight and £650 to insurance

*Reporting to:* Director of Programmes & Operations

**Responsibilities:**

**Programme Development**

1. Work with national and international staff to design community health projects that fulfil local needs and align with SEEDs' strategic aim, taking into account past learning, international best practice, contextual constraints and government objectives.
2. Oversee the development of project frameworks (e.g. Log Frames and Theory of Change) and proposals to ensure they are representative of the community needs whilst being attractive to donors.
3. Support the team to conduct research into international and national development best practice and funding opportunities for the Community Health Programme
4. Ensure the high standard of all project documents submitted to donors to secure the ongoing funding of SEED’s projects – currently at around £150,000 per annum across all active interventions
5. Identify partners and build networks and collaborations across the Community Health Programme to increase the impact of SEEDs' work in these areas
6. Use evidence-based advocacy from research and project findings in briefing papers for staff, local and regional stakeholders, and government departments to inform regional and national development strategy.

**Programme Management**

1. Provide timely updates to the UK-based Programme and Partnerships Manager and support them to communicate any changes in project activities to donors when necessary
2. Oversee effective systems for monitoring project progress against activity plans, working with project teams to ensure objectives are met and using learning from ongoing evaluation to inform the development of projects
3. Conduct fieldwork and monitoring visits to project sites when appropriate and ensure observations are fed back into ongoing project design.

**People Management**

1. Recruit, support, manage, review and provide professional development to a team of Programme Officers and Specialists, delegating to and managing their work to achieve departmental objectives and support organisational ethos and strategy
2. Foster essential cross-cultural collaboration and learning, providing support to both the national and international teams to bridge gaps in understanding and priorities for project development and implementation
3. Provide pastoral care and guidance and act as a role model, both professionally and personally, for a team of early-career professionals living in country

**Budget Management**

1. Oversee the development of budgets, including full cost allocation with consideration of the organisational strategy and priorities over the coming years
2. Provide monthly overview of financial reports, ensuring project spending is on track and identifying trends in expenditure, and management of exchange rate gains

**General**

1. Provide core support to the Director of Programmes & Operations in management and ensuring the support and security of all international staff, including acting as an intermediary of organisational priorities to the wider team
2. Work flexibly, including changing work priorities at short notice and working unsociable hours when necessary to meet a short deadline, for example the submission of project funding documents within the timeframe set by donors
3. Ensure all of SEEDs policies and procedures are evident throughout the work of the department, including those for safeguarding, whistleblowing, and anti-corruption, and undertake continual training to ensure these are always promoted
4. Represent SEED Madagascar in external meetings with other agencies, donors, and partners on the ground in Madagascar and in the UK
5. Act as a temporary stand-in for the Director of Programmes & Operations and/or other Programme Heads when required during a period of leave and absences

**Required Skills & Experience**
**Essential**

- At least a first degree-level qualification or equivalent experience in community health, or related discipline
- Sound knowledge of international development frameworks and contemporary global issues facing countries in the global south
- Sound knowledge of and interest in community health issues and approaches in the global south
- Minimum of four years’ experience of community health projects in a developing context
- Minimum of two years’ professional experience in line management and supervising, mentoring and appraising international staff
- Minimum of four years’ professional experience in project management
- Familiarity with the use of project management tools including Logical Frameworks, Theory of Change models, Activity Plans and Monitoring & Evaluation frameworks
- Fluency in English (written and spoken) with excellent written communication skills, to the level of editing English documents for publication and donors
- A minimum of C1 proficiency in French.
- Excellent listening and verbal communication skills, and a flexible and patient attitude
- Excellent proposal and report writing and editing skills, with previous experience compiling project proposals and reports and the ability to tailor written information to various audiences
- Cross-cultural negotiation skills and a curiosity in effective work practices in a cross-cultural setting
- Ability and desire to build capacity both within international and national teams
- Ability and desire to develop, support and manage a team of volunteers and staff
- Ability to demonstrate and support staff to develop appropriate professional and social attitudes required for living in another country, and to manage these aspects of volunteers’ behaviour when required
- Proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Word, Excel and PowerPoint
- Excellent problem-solving and analytical skills, with demonstrable ability in gathering and assimilating facts and data from various sources
- Experience of living and working in a least developed country with the ability and desire to work with teams from different economic and cultural backgrounds and across multiple language barriers

jobs.description:
## Organizational Profile

Founded in 1991, Secours Islamique France (SIF) is a national and international non-governmental organization that has responded to humanitarian and social needs in France and around the world for more than three decades. SIF supports vulnerable individuals and communities through emergency assistance, development programmes and advocacy initiatives, without discrimination or proselytism.

The SIF Kenya and Somalia Mission, registered in 2012, implements humanitarian and development programmes across both countries, focusing on Education and Child Protection, Food Security and Livelihoods, and Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH).

## Position Overview

SIF is seeking an experienced and motivated Program Manager to lead the implementation and coordination of activities under the FIFSAN programme in Kismayo, Somalia. Based in Kismayo, Jubaland State, Somalia, the position involve regular field visits to Dhobley and Jamaame and travel to Nairobi as required for coordination.The successful candidate will provide overall programme leadership, ensuring quality implementation, effective team management, stakeholder coordination, monitoring and reporting, and compliance with approved project documents, donor requirements and SIF policies. The role requires strong experience in humanitarian programming, preferably in nutrition, food security, livelihoods and resilience.

The successful candidate will be responsible for:

- lead programme planning, implementation and quality assurance, ensuring activities are delivered in line with approved proposals, workplans, budgets and programme objectives.
- support the integration of nutrition, food security, agriculture, livestock, financial inclusion and women's economic empowerment interventions, while coordinating with government institutions, implementing partners and community structures.
- supervise and supporting programme staff, strengthen team capacity and promote effective collaboration across programme, MEAL, finance, logistics and partner teams.
- oversee programme performance monitoring, beneficiary targeting, reporting and documentation of results, lessons learned and implementation challenges.
- monitor programme budgets and operational requirements, support timely procurement and delivery of project inputs, and ensure compliance with donor requirements, SIF procedures and relevant humanitarian standards.
- promote accountability, protection, inclusion and gender equality, and ensure feedback and complaints are handled appropriately in accordance with SIF policies and safeguarding procedures.

The successful candidate should be skilled and competent in:
- strong programme planning, implementation, monitoring and reporting skills, with a focus on results and programme quality.
- proven leadership, team management and staff development abilities.
- effective communication, coordination and relationship-building skills with communities, partners, authorities and other stakeholders.
- strong analytical, problem-solving and decision-making abilities, including the capacity to manage competing priorities.
- sound understanding of accountability, gender equality, safeguarding, risk management and the Do No Harm principle.
- good organisational and financial management skills, with attention to compliance and the responsible use of resources.
- fluency in English and Somali language is required.

## Qualifications and Experience

Candidates should meet the following requirements:

- A university degree in International Development, Humanitarian Studies, Nutrition, Public Health, Agriculture, Livelihoods, Project Management or a related field.
- At least seven years of progressive experience with humanitarian or non-profit organizations.
- A minimum of four years of supervisory or management experience.
- Relevant experience managing multi-sector humanitarian or development programmes, preferably in nutrition, food security, livelihoods and resilience.

**Do No Harm Principle**

*Secours Islamique France considers diversity a strength. We therefore review all applications, provided they demonstrate the skills required for the position to be filled. As a humanitarian NGO, SIF is committed to respecting the humanitarian principle of “Do No Harm” and ensures that the safety of our beneficiaries (including children), employees, volunteers, partners, and service providers is a primary consideration in all its activities. SIF maintains a zero-tolerance policy toward any form of fraud, corruption, psychological/sexual harassment, abuse or violence of any kind, and, more broadly, any breach of legislation, regulations, the Child Safeguarding Policy (CSP), or the internal code of conduct, both at headquarters and in the field. In line with these principles, this position is subject to a criminal record check as well as professional reference checks. Our charter is a genuine commitment: we mobilize all of our staff to promote, share, and uphold the principles set out. Together, let’s rise to the challenge for solidarity that transcends differences."*

jobs.description:
## **About One Acre Fund**

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our [Why Work Here](https://oneacrefund.org/careers/why-work-here) blog post.

Our Kenya program, founded in 2006, operates under the local brand Tupande. Close to 500 staff in our Kakamega headquarters support 1,747 field staff and serve more than 1 million farmers. In Nairobi, around 50 staff support global functions like procurement, recruitment, government relations, and communications.

## **About the Role**

Seeking a commercial professional with 2+ years of FMCG experience to drive Tupande's market expansion in Kenya, get products onto major supermarket shelves, launch Animal Feed and BioChar, and secure high-value B2B sales for excess produce.

Business Development & Market Expansion:

- Identify, evaluate, and pursue new market opportunities and distribution networks for Tupande’s retail products (roasted macadamia and dried fruit), and animal feed products.
- Place products in major supermarkets, wholesale distributors, and key retail avenues
- Map local demand for excess produce and processing byproducts generated by export value chains.
- Develop direct-to-business (B2B) or alternative local sales channels to sell Biochar, Animal Feed, excess produce and processing byproducts from across Tupdande’s value chains.

Sales Management:

- Build, negotiate, and maintain strategic partnerships with B2B customers, retail buyers, distributors, and store managers
- Take full ownership of current customer relationships, ensuring consistent engagement, satisfaction, and retention.
- Drive the sales pipeline and close deals to achieve or exceed targets.
- Provide accurate revenue forecasting to department leadership.

Account Management:

- Maintain and grow strategic accounts by providing excellent service, understanding client needs, and offering tailored solutions.
- Ensure a high standard of customer experience at all times.

Strategy design and execution

- Design and execute the go-to-market strategies for Tupande Retail products, Animal Feed and Bio Char

Performance Monitoring:

- Track and analyze sales performance, provide regular updates, and implement corrective actions to meet objectives.

## **Career Growth and Development**

We have a strong culture of constant learning and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months, and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

## **Qualifications**

Across all roles, these are the [general qualifications we look for](https://oneacrefund.org/work-with-us/application-process/qualifications/). For this role specifically, you will have:

- 2+ years of experience in fast-moving consumer goods (FMCG), or retail distribution (experience getting products onto major supermarket shelves is strongly preferred)
- Experience in selling at scale: managing a minimum recurring revenue of $5m personally, structuring commercial agreements, negotiating trade terms, managing credit risks, and international import/export regulations
- Experience in building new accounts.
- Proven track record of taking new products—ideally in food, agriculture, or animal nutrition—from concept to market launch.
- You can bridge market opportunities with on-the-ground operational capacities
- Strong ability to negotiate listing fees, payment terms, and margins with retail giants and commercial distributors.

## **Preferred Start Date**

As soon as possible

## **Job Location**

Nairobi, Kenya

## **Benefits**

Health insurance, housing, and comprehensive benefits

## **Eligibility**

This role is only open to citizens or permanent residents of Burundi, Ethiopia, Kenya, Nigeria, Malawi, Rwanda, Tanzania, Uganda, Zambia and Democratic Republic of Congo.

14 January 2027. Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

**Organizational Profile**

Founded in 1991, Secours Islamique France (SIF) is an international NGO that has worked in France and around the world for over 30 years. SIF acts wherever there are humanitarian and social needs by delivering emergency relief, development programs and advocacy campaigns without proselytism or discrimination. The SIF Kenya and Somalia Mission was registered in 2012 and implements humanitarian and development programs in Education and Child Welfare, Food Security and Livelihoods, and Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) interventions to support vulnerable communities.

**Position overview**

SIF is seeking a qualified and motivated Logistics Assistant to support the implementation of its operations in Kismayo, Somalia, under the FIFSAN program. The Logistics Assistant will provide day-to-day operational and technical support across procurement, logistics, asset tracking and office administration. The role will support in ensuring that procurement and logistics activities are efficient, properly documented and compliant with SIF policies, donor requirements and applicable regulations. The successful candidate will demonstrate strong organizational skills, integrity, accountability and the ability to work effectively in a humanitarian operating environment in carrying out the following responsibilities:

- Procurement: Support procurement planning, supplier sourcing and evaluation, purchase documentation, delivery follow-up and maintenance of accurate procurement records in line with organizational and donor requirements.
- Fleet and Transport Management: Assist with vehicle movement planning, fuel monitoring, maintenance scheduling and tracking of vehicles, generators and other assets.
- Stock and Warehousing: Monitor stock levels, verify incoming deliveries, maintain inventory records and support regular stock counts and asset tracking.
- Office and Equipment Management: Support the proper functioning of office facilities and equipment and ensure logistics documentation is securely maintained and well organized.
- Reporting and Compliance: Contribute to logistics reporting, maintain accurate records for audit purposes, and ensure compliance with organizational procedures, donor requirements and relevant regulations.
- Coordination and Safeguarding: Coordinate with relevant teams and service providers, promptly report operational or security concerns, and uphold organizational safeguarding and Do No Harm principles.

**Qualifications and Experience**

The successful candidate should meet the following requirements:

- A degree or diploma in Purchasing and Procurement, Supply Chain Management, Business Administration or a related field.
- At least two years of relevant experience in logistics, procurement or supply chain management with a non-governmental organization (NGO).
- Good knowledge of logistics and supply chain management principles, including inventory, fleet and asset management.
- Basic knowledge of electricity, engines and vehicle mechanics.
- A valid driving licence is an added advantage.

**Additionally, the successful candidate should demonsrate competencies in:**

- Good computer skills, particularly in Microsoft Word, Excel and Outlook.
- Strong organizational, planning and prioritization skills, with attention to detail.
- Good communication and teamwork skills.
- High standards of integrity, accountability and professionalism.
- Practical problem-solving skills and the ability to adapt to changing operational needs.
- Commitment to child safeguarding, confidentiality and the Do No Harm principles.

**Do No Harm Principle**

*Secours Islamique France considers diversity a strength. We therefore review all applications, provided they demonstrate the skills required for the position to be filled. As a humanitarian NGO, SIF is committed to respecting the humanitarian principle of “Do No Harm” and ensures that the safety of our beneficiaries (including children), employees, volunteers, partners, and service providers is a primary consideration in all its activities. SIF maintains a zero-tolerance policy toward any form of fraud, corruption, psychological/sexual harassment, abuse or violence of any kind, and, more broadly, any breach of legislation, regulations, the Child Safeguarding Policy (CSP), or the internal code of conduct, both at headquarters and in the field. In line with these principles, this position is subject to a criminal record check as well as professional reference checks. Our charter is a genuine commitment: we mobilize all of our staff to promote, share, and uphold the principles set out. Together, let’s rise to the challenge for solidarity that transcends differences."*

jobs.description:
## Job Brief

This position is open to suitably qualified PNG National candidates only.

**Program Background**

DT Global has been engaged by the Australian Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade (DFAT) to manage the next phase of Australia’s investment in strengthening the delivery of law and justice services in Papua New Guinea for a 4-year period to 31 December 2027.

APLJ seeks to contribute to PNG’s law and justice sector capacity to provide inclusive, safe, secure and accountable law and justice foundations for peaceful and prosperous communities, equitable economic development and private sector growth.

The program aligns with the Government of Papua New Guinea’s (GoPNG) law and justice sector goal of ‘building peaceful and prosperous communities together’. APLJ will focus on three End of Program Outcomes (EOPOs):

**EOPO 1 – Community Safety and Access to Justice at the Local Level:** Communities in target locations, especially women, children, persons with disabilities, vulnerable people and those accused of sorcery, have improved access to selected justice and support services.

**EOPO 2 – Law and Justice Services Supply:** Responsible law and justice sector agencies increasingly provide selected inclusive, responsive, and accountable essential law and justice services in target locations.

**EOPO 3 – Leadership, Coordination and Accountability:** Responsible law and justice mechanisms demonstrate improved sectoral leadership and coordination of national and subnational law and justice services and improved sector integrity systems.

**About DT Global Asia Pacific**

At DT Global Asia Pacific, we aim to positively impact people’s lives through delivery excellence. As a leading implementing partner across Asia and the Pacific, we co-create locally led solutions in partnership with governments, communities, and stakeholders. We bring together talented teams and deep regional expertise to deliver initiatives that promote inclusive economic growth, essential services, and resilient, secure communities. With over 1,500 staff, experts in 22+ countries and more than 60 years of development experience, we tackle complex community, national and transnational challenges — from governance and justice systems to climate resilience, infrastructure and social equity — with innovative thinking and a commitment to long-term impact.

For more information, please see [**www.dt-global.com**](http://www.dt-global.com/)

**The Role**

The **HSE Coordinator** will support the Security and HSE Manager to implement and continuously improve APLJ’s health, safety and environmental management arrangements across program offices, activities and travel. The role will coordinate routine HSE systems, inspections and assessments, records, training, incident follow-up and emergency preparedness so that personnel, contractors and visitors can work safely and APLJ can demonstrate compliance with applicable DT Global and program requirements. The HSE Coordinator will be responsible for supporting reporting of incidents, hazards and near misses.

Click on the link or copy paste it to access the full Terms of Reference for this position:

[**https://tinyurl.com/4c3fyf75**](https://tinyurl.com/4c3fyf75)

**About You**

The preferred candidate will have:

· Relevant tertiary qualification or recognised vocational training in occupational health and safety, environmental management, risk management or a related field, or equivalent demonstrated professional experience.

· 3 to 5 years’ relevant experience supporting HSE, workplace safety, risk, compliance or operational systems in an office, program, project or comparable environment.

· Practical experience maintaining HSE registers and records, coordinating inspections and risk assessments, and tracking corrective actions to closure.

· Experience supporting incident and near-miss reporting, initial fact gathering, investigation follow-up and confidential recordkeeping.

· Experience coordinating staff inductions, safety briefings, training, consultation meetings or emergency drills.

· Sound knowledge of hazard identification, risk assessment and control principles, emergency preparedness and continuous improvement.

· Strong organisational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to manage multiple priorities, meet deadlines and maintain accurate, audit-ready documentation.

· Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to prepare clear reports and communicate practical HSE requirements to diverse audiences.

· Demonstrated ability to work collaboratively and respectfully with colleagues, contractors, service providers and stakeholders in a culturally diverse environment.

· Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, particularly Word, Excel, Outlook, Teams and SharePoint or comparable document-management systems.

· Willingness and ability to travel within Papua New Guinea as required.

**Why join the Australia-Papua New Guinea Law and Justice Partnership (APLJ)?**

*By joining the APLJ, you will be part of a dynamic and effective team where you can collaborate with leading experts and professionals from diverse backgrounds, access development programs to achieve your career goals, and be challenged to take a global outlook.*

jobs.title: Iraq Country Director
jobs.description:
## IRAQ COUNTRY DIRECTOR

### FULL-TIME - ERBIL, IRAQ

#### ABOUT FREE TO RUN

Free to Run’s mission is to advance gender equity globally through running. We are a registered nonprofit/nongovernmental organization that has been operating community-led programs for adolescent girls and young women since 2014. We are known for delivering long-term, youth-led, progressive running, leadership, rights, and health programs directly to adolescent girls and young women living in protracted conflict zones. However, the longer-term impact of our work is building enduring social change - decreasing barriers to public participation, increasing women in leadership, and making power structures more equitable and inclusive. Free to Run identifies as an organization working at the intersections of feminism, human rights, development, and humanitarian interventions.

In 2027, we will begin to execute on a new three-year strategic plan which has the organization positioned to grow in a multitude of directions - programmatically, operationally, financially and geographically. The achievement of our mission will continue to be rooted in our work across three strategic pillars: direct service (EMPOWER), capacity building for local NGOs (EQUIP), and building a global movement of activists who are passionate about gender equity and running (MOVE).

**POSITION OVERVIEW**

The Iraq Country Director is responsible for overseeing all aspects of the organization’s work in Iraq – from big picture to the small details. The Country Director is responsible for building the Free to Run network in the country, with a specific focus on donor-relations to achieve fundraising goals and grow the organization’s profile. The Country Director reports directly to the (internationally-based) Executive Director.

**CORE ACCOUNTABILITIES**

**1) Develop and Manage an Effective and Informed Iraq Country Strategy (10%)**

- Envision a high-impact Iraq strategy that aligns with Free to Run’s global strategy
- Develop and track key performance indicators related to strategy
- Participate in organizational strategic planning, budgeting and performance reporting activities

**2) Oversee Free to Run Programs (20%)**

- Oversee program development and design efforts for Iraq-based programs, with support of Senior Program Officer who will directly manage program cycles, currently designed to be operating in three provinces by 2023
- Ensure all programs are adequately staffed and resourced, support staff training and development
- Oversee safe and high-quality program implementation, monitor day-to-day activities of Program staff
- Ensure all programs are monitored and evaluated using standard instruments, work closely with the Executive Director to improve current data collection tools to provide more accurate and timely information on project indicators for success
- Lead program learning and analysis activities with staff, contribute to global learning practices
- Develop and maintain relationships with key local, regional and national stakeholders to ensure smooth operations
- Ensure program data and learning is shared with other relevant staff for program improvement, external reporting and communications

**3) Grow and Lead a High-Performing Team (30%)**

- Lead recruitment, interviewing, hiring and on-boarding/off-boarding of Iraq Free to Run team
- Manage Senior Program Officer and Finance and Operations Officer (others as deemed necessary for growth and as resources allow)
- Ensure the organization and employees comply with all relevant in-country employment laws and best practices
- Coordinate the bi-annual goal setting and performance review processes for all administrative employees and support a culture of constant feedback and learning through targeted coaching and mentoring organization-wide
- Support visits from international staff, Board members and volunteers

**4) Oversee Country-level Finances and Operations (20%)**

- Develop and manage organizational country budget and finances as well as program budgets for specific projects
- Work with bookkeeper to manage administration of expenses, handling of cash and procurement processes, and accounts payable and receivable
- Prepare timely, high-quality financial and narrative reports
- Ensure financial compliance with national and local laws, as well as Free to Run’s finance policies
- Ensure all office operations are functional, with support from Finance and Operations Officer
- Liaise with Executive Director on a regular basis to ensure financial cohesion
- Confirm all registrations and permits to operate as an NGO are up to date, secure licenses to operate in new geographies as needed

**5) Build Support for Free to Run in Iraq (20%)**

- Identify, cultivate and follow through on funding opportunities across sectors, including mapping potential funding opportunities, meeting with potential and current partners and developing funding proposals (with support from the Executive Director)
- Use strong storytelling and persuasion skills to build individual and community support for Free to Run in Iraq amongst key stakeholders
- Compile and prepare Iraq case studies and stories, provide regular input to Free to Run’s social media channels
- Communicate regularly with Free to Run’s community partners and coordinating their participation in events
- Represent Free to Run at influential events and speaking engagements locally, regionally and internationally
- Write press releases and editorial content for website and earned media opportunities

LOCATION

The Country Director position is based in Erbil (KRI) with an expectation of travel to other parts of Iraq regularly and international travel on occasion. Must have a passport and/or residency permit that allows for travel throughout (federal) Iraq and KRI.

**WORKING HOURS**

The Country Director position is a full-time role, estimated at 40 hours per week. Due to the nature of the organization’s business, hours may fluctuate outside regular core hours (Sunday–Thursday; 9AM-5PM), with the possibility of some nights or weekends, depending on the needs of the organization.

**COMPENSATION**

Based on experience. Aligned with market rate for a Country Director in Iraq. (Free to Run uses MSF Salary Survey as one of a handful of benchmarks for salary calculations in Iraq).

**EXPERIENCE AND COMPETENCIES**

Below is what we are looking for as we evaluate applications. Candidates *don’t need to have all these experiences* *and competencies* but should be able to display strengths across multiple areas.

Free to Run seeks an experienced, values-driven leader with a demonstrated ability to mobilize resources, build strategic partnerships, and lead high-performing teams. The successful candidate will combine strong knowledge of Iraq's civil society and development landscape with a commitment to feminist leadership, human rights, and locally-led development. We recognize that strong leaders bring diverse professional and educational experiences.

**Education and Language:**

- Bachelor's degree in international development, human rights, women’s/gender studies, public health or MHPSS, nonprofit management, business administration, or a related field required. An advanced degree is preferred; equivalent relevant professional experience may be considered.
- Professional fluency in written and spoken English is required.
- Professional fluency in Kurdish (Sorani or Kurmanji/Badini) or Arabic required; proficiency in both is strongly preferred.

**Professional Experience:**

- Minimum 10 years of progressively responsible professional experience in international development, humanitarian assistance, human rights, civil society, or related sectors, including at least three years in a senior management or leadership role.
- Demonstrated track record of successful fundraising and resource mobilization in Iraq and/or the wider Middle East region, including personally cultivating donor relationships, securing institutional or private funding, and developing successful funding proposals or partnerships.
- Established relationships with, and strong understanding of, the regional donor landscape, including bilateral and multilateral donors, foundations, international NGOs, and private-sector funding partners.
- Proven experience leading, managing, and developing diverse teams, including responsibility for staff performance, professional development, organizational culture, and effective team collaboration.
- Experience managing organizational budgets, operational systems, and financial accountability, including compliance with donor requirements and applicable national regulations.
- Deep understanding of Iraq's political, social, cultural, and operating environment, including the Kurdistan Region, and demonstrated ability to navigate complex stakeholder relationships.
- Experience engaging with government authorities, civil society organizations, institutional donors, and community-based partners.
- Experience working in women's rights, gender equity, youth leadership, refugee and displacement, or community-based development programming strongly preferred.
- Experience managing institutional grants and working within international NGO accountability, safeguarding, and compliance frameworks preferred.
- Experience working in collaboration with a global headquarters and other country-teams strongly preferred

**Skills, Leadership Approach and Competencies:**

Feminist and Rights-Based Leadership

- Demonstrated commitment to feminist principles, gender equality, and human rights, with the ability to translate these values into everyday leadership, management practices, and organizational decision-making.
- Proven ability to lead through an empowering, inclusive, and participatory management approach that shares power appropriately, encourages staff agency and ownership, values diverse perspectives, and creates opportunities for individual and collective leadership.
- Ability to foster a respectful, psychologically safe, and accountable working environment in which team members feel empowered to raise concerns, challenge ideas constructively, and contribute meaningfully to decisions.
- Strong understanding of power dynamics, discrimination, and structural inequalities, with the ability to apply intersectional and culturally responsive approaches to staff management, partnerships, and programming.
- Commitment to safeguarding, prevention of sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment (PSEAH), non-discrimination, and the dignity and rights of staff, participants, and communities.

Fundraising and External Relations

- Excellent relationship-building, networking, and negotiation skills, with the confidence and credibility to engage senior government officials, institutional donors, private-sector partners, and civil society leaders.
- Strong fundraising and business development capabilities, including donor cultivation, strategic positioning, proposal development, and negotiation of funding partnerships.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including persuasive writing, public speaking, and the ability to represent Free to Run effectively with diverse audiences.
- Ability to identify and pursue strategic opportunities that strengthen Free to Run's financial sustainability, institutional credibility, and influence.

Strategic and Operational Leadership

- Strong strategic thinking and planning skills, with the ability to translate organizational priorities into achievable country-level objectives, operational plans, and measurable results.
- Demonstrated ability to balance strategic leadership with sound financial management, operational oversight, and organizational accountability.
- Strong judgment, integrity, and problem-solving skills, including the ability to make sound decisions in complex, politically sensitive, and rapidly changing environments.
- Ability to lead organizational change constructively, foster innovation, and build a culture of continuous learning and improvement.
- Strong cross-cultural communication, emotional intelligence, and conflict-resolution skills, including the ability to provide constructive feedback, address performance challenges fairly, and navigate difficult conversations with professionalism.
- Ability to collaborate effectively within a globally distributed organization, maintaining clear communication, mutual accountability, and alignment between country-level and global teams.
- Proficiency with standard digital collaboration, communication, and financial management tools, including Google Workspace and Microsoft Office.

**PERSONAL ATTRIBUTES**

The successful candidate will demonstrate integrity, humility, resilience, sound judgment, and a genuine commitment to Free to Run's mission. They will be a confident external representative and an empowering internal leader who understands that effective leadership is measured not only by organizational results, but also by the capacity, confidence, and agency developed in others.

*Free to Run is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We don’t just accept differences — we celebrate, support and thrive on them for the benefit of our team, our programs, and our organizational strength. We are proud to be an affirmative action employer, committed to diversity, equity and inclusion of ALL people in our hiring and employment practices. We encourage applications from people who have non-dominant identities based on race, ethnicity, migration status, ability, age, gender identity, sexual orientation, socioeconomic class, etc.*

jobs.title: Final Evaluation of the Leveraging and Expanding Agri-Aqua Production in Bangsamoro (LEAP) Project
jobs.description:
For detailed information, click this link. [https://drive.google.com/drive/u/3/folders/1YLOcoIjszvoDH6sdzAIGIoIowTa7x_WM](https://drive.google.com/drive/u/3/folders/1YLOcoIjszvoDH6sdzAIGIoIowTa7x_WM)

## Terms of Reference (ToR)

### Final Evaluation of the Leveraging and Expanding Agri-Aqua Production in Bangsamoro (LEAP) Project

**Funded by the European Union**

### 1. Background

#### About People in Need

People in Need (PIN) is an international non-governmental organisation founded in the Czech Republic in 1992. It has implemented hundreds of humanitarian and development projects across Europe, Asia, Africa and Central America. PIN began its operations in the Philippines in 2013 in response to Super Typhoon Yolanda, and its programmes have since grown to cover market systems development, sustainable livelihoods, disaster resilience, renewable energy, peace and social cohesion, including in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM).

PIN seeks the services of a qualified external evaluator or evaluation team, referred to in this ToR as the Evaluator, to conduct the final evaluation of the LEAP project. The assignment will be carried out in close cooperation with the PIN project and MEAL teams and the consortium partners.

#### About the LEAP Project

The Leveraging and Expanding Agri-Aqua Production in Bangsamoro (LEAP) project develops the coffee and seaweed value chains in the island provinces of Basilan, Sulu and Tawi-Tawi (BaSulTa) in BARMM. It is implemented by People in Need as lead applicant, together with the co-applicants MARADECA and UNyPHIL-Women, under the European Union’s Bangsamoro Agri-Enterprise Programme (BAEP). The project runs from 1 July 2023 to 31 December 2026.

**Overall objective:** To contribute to a peaceful, cohesive, secure and inclusive development of agri- and aqua-culture value chains in Bangsamoro.

**Specific objective:** Coffee and seaweed production improved in quality, diversity, consolidation and its response to the needs of the market.

#### Outputs

- **Output 1:** Coffee and seaweed value chains in the island provinces are mapped, analysed and better coordinated.
- **Output 2:** Individual farmers and farmer or fisher folk groups are equipped for diversified, quality production through access to crop and sea inputs and extension services.
- **Output 3:** Farmer and fisher folk small social enterprises within the coffee and seaweed value chains are established and strengthened.
- **Output 4:** Enhanced post-harvest and processing facilities are in place.

#### Target Groups

The main target group is coffee and seaweed farmers, small farmer groups and cooperatives in Basilan, Sulu and Tawi-Tawi, a minimum of 2,000 farmers, with particular focus on women, youth and indigenous people.

Other target groups are traders and input suppliers in the three provinces; local, regional and provincial authorities, including MAFAR, MTIT and OPAG and the provincial agricultural offices; and academia, in particular MSU Tawi-Tawi.

The final beneficiaries are farmers, cooperatives and traders across BARMM and the general population of the island provinces.

### 2. Purpose and Objectives of the Evaluation

The final evaluation will assess the extent to which LEAP achieved its objectives and results, and how the intended and unintended changes came about. In line with the project design, the evaluation is conducted by an external evaluator with strong expertise and experience in markets development in the Philippines. It will provide lessons and recommendations that assist PIN, the consortium partners and other stakeholders to enhance the impact of future interventions in BARMM.

The specific objectives of the evaluation are to:

- Assess the project's performance against its overall objective, specific objective and the four outputs, measured against the logframe baseline and targets.
- Identify what worked, what did not, and why, across the coffee and seaweed value chains and the three island provinces.
- Generate practical lessons learned and actionable recommendations for future value-chain programming in BARMM.
- From a market systems perspective, the evaluation should assess not only what LEAP delivered, but the extent to which the project contributed to changes in how the coffee and seaweed market systems function. This should include changes in relationships, incentives, behaviours, capacities and roles among farmers, cooperatives, private-sector actors, service providers and public institutions, and the likelihood that these changes will continue, adapt or expand beyond direct project support.

### 3. Scope of the Evaluation

**Type of evaluation.** This is a performance evaluation against the standard OECD-DAC evaluation criteria. Impact is assessed as the project's plausible contribution to change measured against baseline values, and not through a counterfactual design. A separate impact evaluation of the programme will be conducted by the European Union, so this evaluation focuses on performance and does not attempt to measure the macro-level impact indicators.

**Period under review.** The whole project duration, from 1 July 2023 to the time of the evaluation.

**Geographic scope.** The three island provinces of Basilan, Sulu and Tawi-Tawi, with in-person data collection in each province.

**Coverage.** The evaluation covers the whole project, both the coffee and the seaweed value chains, the specific objective and all four outputs, assessed against the logframe baselines and targets.

### 4. Evaluation Criteria and Questions

The evaluation applies the standard OECD-DAC criteria of relevance, coherence, effectiveness, efficiency, impact and sustainability, together with EU added value, inclusivity and gender equality and social inclusion, and cross-cutting themes. The questions below are the key areas to be answered. The Evaluator is expected to refine them and develop the corresponding judgement criteria, indicators and data sources in an evaluation matrix as part of the inception report.

#### Relevance

- To what extent did the project respond to the real needs and priorities of coffee and seaweed farmers in the island provinces, including women, youth and indigenous people?
- To what extent were interventions informed by identified market demand, commercial opportunities and underlying constraints within the coffee and seaweed market systems, as opposed to primarily responding to the immediate needs of producers?
- Was the project design and its modalities of support appropriate and conflict-sensitive given the security context of the island provinces?

#### Coherence

- How well did the project align with BARMM priorities and relevant sector roadmaps, and complement the work of MAFAR, MTIT, OPAG, the provincial agricultural offices and other actors in the coffee and seaweed sectors?
- How coherent were the interventions internally, across the four outputs and the two value chains?

#### Effectiveness

- To what extent were the specific objective and the four output targets achieved, measured against the baseline?
- How did results differ between the coffee and seaweed value chains, and what explains the differences?
- How well did the distinctive components perform, in particular the coordination platforms, the private nurseries, the post-harvest and processing facilities, savings groups, and the solar technologies and climate services?
- What were the major factors influencing the achievement or non-achievement of results?

#### Market Systems Effectiveness

- What market-system constraints did LEAP successfully address, and which constraints remain binding for the growth and inclusivity of the coffee and seaweed sectors?
- What changes occurred in the behaviour, practices, relationships and incentives of key market actors as a result of LEAP?
- To what extent have market actors taken ownership of functions initially supported or facilitated by the project?
- Is there evidence that practices, services, business models or relationships introduced or strengthened through LEAP have been adopted by actors beyond those directly supported by the project?
- Where systemic change has not occurred, what prevented it (weak commercial incentives, capacity constraints, institutional barriers, limited demand, conflict dynamics, project design or another factor?)

#### Efficiency

- Were the financial and human resources used economically to deliver the outputs across two value chains and three provinces?
- Did the consortium model of PIN, MARADECA and UNyPHIL-Women deliver in an efficient and well-coordinated manner?
- Was implementation timely, including the use of the 6-months extended implementation period to December 2026?

#### Impact (Contribution)

- What significant changes occurred in production, quality, diversification, market access, sales and household income, and to what extent did LEAP plausibly contribute to these changes? What other actors or contextual factors contributed to the observed results?
- Were there different effects for women, youth and indigenous people, and any unintended effects, positive or negative?

#### EU Added Value

- What did EU funding of this project add beyond what regional or national actors could have delivered on their own?

#### Sustainability

- Are the coordination platforms and the emerging industry bodies, such as the Sulu Coffee Industry Development Board and the Basilan Coffee Industry Cluster Council, likely to continue functioning after the project ends?
- How durable is the institutional anchoring of the seaweed value chain, which is weaker than that of coffee?
- Are the post-harvest and processing facilities likely to be maintained and continue to operate independently?
- Are the social enterprises and savings groups viable beyond the life of the project?
- For key functions supported by LEAP, which actors now have both the capacity and commercial or institutional incentive to continue performing these functions without project support?
- If LEAP support ended completely, which changes would continue, which would weaken, and which would stop, and why?
- Is there evidence of replication, imitation, crowding-in or spontaneous adoption by farmers, businesses, service providers, government institutions or other actors that were not directly supported by LEAP? What factors enabled or constrained such scale?

#### Inclusivity and Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI)

- To what extent did the project reach and benefit women, youth and indigenous people as intended, and was their participation meaningful rather than only numerical?

#### Cross-Cutting Themes

- How well did the project apply conflict sensitivity and a do-no-harm approach in practice?
- Were the Community Feedback and Response Mechanism (CFRM) and safeguarding measures functioning and accessible to target groups?
- How were environmental sustainability considerations addressed?

#### Lessons and Learning

- What are the main lessons from LEAP that PIN and partners should carry into future value-chain programming in BARMM?

### 5. Methodology

The Evaluator is responsible for developing the evaluation design and detailed methodology to meet the objectives above. A mixed-methods approach is expected, combining qualitative and quantitative data collection and analysis. Findings must be measured against the logframe baseline values wherever the indicators allow. The proposed approach, the sampling strategy and the data collection tools are to be presented in the inception report and agreed with PIN.

#### Desk Review

The Evaluator will review the project's logframe and description of the action including amendments, the baseline study, narrative and progress reports, monitoring data, the coffee and seaweed value chain studies and other studies conducted under the project, and summaries of feedback received through the CFRM.

#### Field Data Collection

- Key informant interviews with project and MEAL teams, consortium partners, government and private stakeholders.
- Focus group discussions with farmers and other value chain actors, held in person in all three provinces.
- Direct observation of nurseries, post-harvest and processing facilities and donated equipment, to verify that they are in place and functional.

Given the cultural context of the island provinces, the evaluation team should be gender-balanced so that women farmers can be interviewed by women enumerators where appropriate. The team must also cover the local languages in use in the target areas, including Tausug, Sama and Yakan, either within the team or through qualified interpreters.

The qualitative methodology should include purposive interviews with market actors positioned both within and beyond LEAP's direct intervention portfolio, including buyers, traders, processors, input suppliers, financial/service providers and relevant public institutions. This will enable the evaluation to test whether observed changes extend beyond direct beneficiaries and project-supported structures.

Evaluator should use contribution analysis and/or outcome harvesting to reconstruct the change pathway, assess LEAP's contribution alongside other influencing factors, and identify evidence of behavioural change, ownership, replication and sustainability.

#### Note on the Inception Report

Once approved by PIN, the inception report becomes the reference document for the assignment, and the final evaluation report will follow it. Approval of the inception report is internal to PIN.

### 6. Key Deliverables

Deliverable

Description

Inception report

Methodology, evaluation matrix, sampling strategy, data collection tools and workplan, developed in consultation with the PIN project and MEAL teams. Once approved, it becomes the reference document for the assignment.

Draft evaluation report

Main findings presented for review by PIN and the consortium partners.

Final evaluation report

Feedback incorporated. The executive summary should not exceed 3 pages. The report should be concise and evidence-led.

Validation presentation

Key findings and recommendations presented to the project team and relevant stakeholders.

Findings-sharing event

A one-day findings-sharing event in Zamboanga City/Cotabato for about 30 external stakeholders, organised and fully funded by the Evaluator, including venue, participant transport, meals and logistics. PIN will support coordination with the stakeholders and agrees the participant list.

Datasets, tools and transcripts

Cleaned and anonymized datasets, the data collection tools, transcripts, and the analysis files or calculations used in the evaluation.

Thematic learning briefs

One or two short briefs on specific components or approaches, for example the market systems development approach, designed for reuse in future programming. E.g. Market Systems Learning Brief: What did LEAP teach us about facilitating inclusive market-system change in fragile and conflict-affected island economies?

Inputs to the PIN evaluation brief

A short summary of the key findings and recommendations for the PIN evaluation brief.

#### Structure of the Final Report

The final report should include an executive summary, an introduction describing the project and the purpose and questions of the evaluation, the methodology and its limitations, the findings organised by evaluation question, conclusions against each criterion, lessons learned, actionable recommendations, and annexes including this ToR, the evaluation tools and the logframe.

The final report should include a dedicated synthesis of market-system change, distinguishing between:

1. Direct beneficiary-level results.
2. Changes in market actor behaviour and relationships.
3. Changes in supporting functions, rules or institutions.
4. Evidence of sustainability, replication, crowding-in or scale.

### 7. Indicative Timeline

The timeline below is indicative and will be confirmed at contracting. The Evaluator should propose a detailed workplan in the inception report.

Stage

Indicative period

Call for evaluators published

7th October 2026

Application deadline

Evaluation of applications, selection and contracting

22nd December 2026

1 January 2027 to 15 February 2027

Draft report and PIN and partner feedback

28th February 2027

Validation and final report

10th March 2027

Event to present the results

TBC

### 8. Qualification Requirements

#### Mandatory

- Proven experience in conducting final evaluations of EU-funded projects, or final evaluations for international non-governmental organisations.
- Demonstrated experience evaluating market systems development (MSD) and/or systemic value-chain development programmes, including assessment of market actor behaviour change, sustainability, facilitation, crowding-in and systemic change.
- Experience applying contribution analysis, outcome harvesting or other theory-based approaches to assessing systemic change.
- Strong quantitative and qualitative research skills, including survey design, key informant interviews, focus group discussions and data analysis.
- Experience working in conflict-affected or conflict-sensitive areas, and with marginalized communities.

#### Desirable

- Knowledge of the BARMM and BaSulTa context.
- Experience with the coffee or seaweed value chains and with agriculture, fisheries or aquaculture programmes.
- Experience in inclusive and gender-sensitive approaches. The proposed team should be gender-balanced.
- Coverage of the local languages in use in the target areas, including Tausug, Sama and Yakan, within the team or through qualified interpreters.
- Excellent analytical, report-writing and presentation skills in English.

### 9. Selection Criteria

Applications will be assessed against the following criteria, for a maximum total score of 100 points. Only proposals meeting all mandatory qualifications will be scored. The budget is published and fixed, so the financial offer carries a low weight in order to focus selection on quality.

The maximum budget available for this evaluation is EUR 30,000. This is inclusive of all professional fees, travel, accommodation, translation and interpretation, transcription, the cost of the findings-sharing event and all other costs related to the assignment. Offers exceeding this amount will not be considered.
