- Bonne compréhension des principes de confidentialité, non-discrimination et signalement sûr.
- Une expérience dans une ONG ou un projet de terrain constitue un atout.

***Caractéristiques :***

- Intégrité, discrétion, empathie et respect.
- Capacité à écouter sans jugement et à respecter strictement les limites du rôle.
- Bonnes capacités de sensibilisation et de communication communautaire.
- Disponibilité pour des déplacements fréquents dans la zone.

**Type de contrat :** CDD de projet / contrat local à durée déterminée, aligné sur la durée et les besoins du projet, sous réserve des dispositions légales applicables, de la disponibilité des financements et des politiques RH de Tostan.

jobs.title: Team Leader, Syria Education Programme III (SEP III)
jobs.description:
**SYRIA EDUCATION PROGRAMME III (SEP III)**

Building on SEP I (2018–2022) and SEP II (2022–2027), which supported primary educatio in Idleb and Aleppo, FCDO plans to procure a new Technical Assistance (TA) contract, SEP III, to support the Syrian Ministry of Education (MoE) in implementing its nationally-led reform agenda, complementing the Ministry's wider reform programme, including support provided through the Global Partnership for Education (GPE). Since December 2024, the MoE has begun to reunify a fragmented education system, but progress has been constrained by limited institutional capacity, a lack of data, weak policy development processes and the absence of a clear long-term strategy for recovery. Unlike earlier phases, which focused primarily on service delivery in northwest Syria, SEP III will work directly with the MoE and local Education Directorates, generally at national level and directorate level, in partnership with Ministry officials, to help the Ministry translate its policy and process reforms into practice through technical advice, capacity building, coaching and support to implementation.

SEP III has two components. The first, which is the subject of this contract, is politically informed TA to the MoE and Education Directorates to strengthen inclusive, effective and evidence-based policy making. The second is non-formal education (NFE) for returning refugees and internally displaced persons, which is outside the scope of this contract and will be delivered by a separate provider. The TA supplier will be required to work collaboratively with the NFE component.

The exact scope of the TA work will be determined jointly with FCDO and the MoE through a demand-led, co-designed and flexible approach. No reform priorities are set in advance; they will be identified with the Ministry during inception. The work is expected to focus on strengthening the education system to improve foundational learning outcomes for primary-school-aged children across Syria, delivered through: 1) Services and Analysis to inform TA and policy decisions; 2) Foundational Learning thematic TA (for example teacher development, coaching and supervision, safeguarding, learning data generation and use, and inclusive education); and 3) Education Systems Strengthening TA (sector planning and prioritisation, policy development, financial management, and monitoring and accountability). Given the difficult fiscal choices likely to shape the sector over the coming years, the programme is also expected to support the Ministry's public finance and value-for-money decision-making. Illustrative technical priorities include: supporting policy reform and Ministry-led coordination, standard-setting, and system strengthening; supporting the roll-out of child safeguarding and Codes of Conduct; improving the quality and consistency of teaching through professional development and a national Teacher Competency Framework; and data-driven planning, including through education management information systems (EMIS/SIMIS).

Given the fluid transition context, the programme will need to operate flexibly, respond quickly to changes, and seize windows of opportunity for reform as they arise. FCDO expects a politically informed, 'test, learn, adapt' approach rather than a fixed blueprint. Delivery must be aligned with government systems, avoiding parallel platforms and the substitution of government functions, and must be underpinned by gender equality, disability and social inclusion (GEDSI) and conflict sensitivity. This requires strong political judgement, including a clear understanding of how decisions are made within the Ministry and government and where opportunities for reform are most likely to emerge, an in-depth understanding of the Syrian education system and its institutional actors, and the ability to sustain trusted relationships with the Ministry, FCDO, and other sector stakeholders, including UNICEF, GPE, Education Cannot Wait (ECW), and the World Bank.

The anticipated delivery model comprises i) a **Core Delivery Team** responsible for overall leadership, technical oversight, coordination, MEAL, governance and quality assurance, which should be predominantly Syrian and mostly based in Syria; and ii) a **demand-led TA Pool** of experts with education and governance backgrounds. The contract is expected to begin on 1 July 2027 with a six-month inception period, during which the supplier must mobilise rapidly, establish a presence in Damascus and operationalise its delivery systems. Details are indicative and will be confirmed in FCDO's Tender Notice.

**POSITION SUMMARY**

The Team Leader holds overall accountability for the design, rapid mobilisation, and delivery of SEP III, including leading the Core Delivery Team and overseeing the TA Pool, ensuring the programme is implemented in accordance with the contract, FCDO requirements, IRC policies and principles, and internationally recognised quality of assistance standards. The Team Leader is the primary point of contact with FCDO and, working closely with the ESS Technical Director and senior Ministry counterparts, provides strategic direction to support the Ministry's implementation of its reform priorities.

The Team Leader is responsible for the programme's overall management, including budget oversight and value for money, performance against contractual KPIs, and risk management (including fiduciary and reputational risk in a sensitive political environment), with the technical quality of the programme's workstreams assured by the ESS Technical Director. The postholder ensures the programme operates adaptively — using political analysis, evidence, monitoring data, and regular review points to prioritise, test, learn and adapt in response to a fast-moving political and institutional context — while maintaining the flexibility needed to respond to emerging windows of opportunity for reform.

The Team Leader maintains strong working relationships with the implementing team, consortium/delivery partners (if applicable), the MoE and Education Directorates, FCDO, the provider of the NFE component, and other education sector stakeholders, and represents the programme and IRC in relevant coordination fora, technical working groups, and policy dialogues. The postholder also oversees programme staffing, procurement, and administrative functions, and ensures robust communications and knowledge management, both internally and with external stakeholders, to share progress, evidence, and lessons learned.

**JOB RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Strategic Leadership**

● Provide overall strategic leadership for SEP III, ensuring the programme's support to the MoE and Education Directorates, led technically by the ESS Technical Director, is relevant to, and aligned with, the Ministry's evolving reform priorities and helps translate these priorities into practice.

● Lead the six-month inception period (July –December 2027), including establishing the Damascus presence, mobilising the Core Delivery Team and TA Pool, operationalising delivery systems, formalising ways of working with the MoE, developing the screening and prioritisation framework and Tasking Order criteria, and delivering inception milestones to FCDO's standard and timetable.

● Provide strategic oversight of the ESS Technical Director's technical leadership, ensuring the programme's technical direction remains aligned with strategic priorities and senior-level MoE relations.

● Ensure the programme operates flexibly and applies a 'test, learn, adapt' approach: agreeing clear reform objectives and decision criteria with the Ministry, co-designing and trialling options, using evidence and learning to decide whether to continue, scale, adapt, pause or pivot workstreams, and documenting adaptation decisions.

● Think and work politically, with a strong understanding of how decisions are made within the Ministry and government and where opportunities for reform are most likely to emerge, drawing on strong contextual and institutional analysis to ensure these opportunities are identified early and acted upon in a timely way.

● Take explicit responsibility for reform sequencing, political economy analysis, and navigating institutional constraints, ensuring a regularly updated PEA and periodic political reviews inform programme design, prioritisation and delivery, and that support is prioritised and paced in line with the Ministry's capacity and the political space available for reform.

● Ensure delivery remains aligned with government systems, avoids parallel platforms and substituting for government functions, and is designed for sustainability and capacity transfer, while supporting coalitions of reform-minded actors within and beyond government.

● Champion evidence-based, gender-responsive, and inclusive approaches throughout programme design and delivery, including dedicated attention to the needs of girls and children with disabilities, and ensure conflict sensitivity is embedded throughout.

● Provide leadership on GEDSI, ensuring diversity and inclusion are reflected in team and partner selection, programme design and implementation, and programme reporting.

**Donor, Government and Stakeholder Relations**

● Serve as the primary point of contact and representational link with FCDO, ensuring high-quality, timely reporting through formal and informal debriefings, and annual and semi-annual reports.

● Build and maintain a trusted, politically informed working relationship with senior officials in the MoE and other relevant government counterparts, supporting the Ministry's stewardship of the education sector and complementing the ESS Technical Director's ongoing technical-level engagement with MoE and Education Directorate representatives at all levels to identify technical assistance needs and design and implement ESS interventions.

● Coordinate with sector stakeholders, including UNICEF, GPE, ECW, the World Bank, and other donors and implementing partners, to support coordinated reform efforts across government and development partners, and to ensure the programme complements ongoing initiatives and other TA investments and adheres to national and global standards.

● Ensure close coherence and collaboration with the provider of the separate NFE component of SEP III, including joint planning, information sharing and coordination of engagement with the Ministry.

● Represent the programme and IRC at national and international forums, including technical conferences and policy dialogues, sharing programme achievements and lessons learned.

● Champion accountability to affected populations, partners, and diverse stakeholders, ensuring that feedback and complaints mechanisms, transparent communication, and participatory approaches inform programme design, delivery, and adaptive management.

**Programme, Risk and Financial Management**

● Oversee overall programme and budget management, ensuring value for money across all components, informed by a sound understanding of the Ministry's public finance context, and robust compliance with FCDO and IRC financial and procurement requirements.

● Oversee the Tasking Order mechanism for the TA Pool, ensuring requests are screened and prioritised against agreed criteria, co-created with the Ministry and Education Directorates, approved by FCDO, costed transparently against the agreed rate card with clear milestones, and delivered to a high-quality standard.

● Lead on identification and management of programme risks, including fiduciary, safeguarding, political, and reputational risks associated with operating within Syrian government structures during a period of political transition.

● Develop, review, and monitor, in coordination with key programme staff, the annual work plan (updated quarterly) and performance plans, and ensure quarterly and annual reports are submitted in the agreed format and to the required standard, so that long-term and short-term priorities remain on track.

● Take responsibility for contractual performance against FCDO's KPIs (indicatively covering reporting, work planning, expenditure variance, risk, safeguarding and fraud notification compliance, political analysis, timely delivery of TA outputs, Ministry adoption of TA outputs, and evidence of adaptive management), taking early corrective action where performance is at risk.

● Ensure monitoring, evaluation, and learning (MEL) data systematically feed into adaptive management processes, including regular reviews of cost-effectiveness and progress against outcomes.

**People and Operations Management**

● Manage programme staff, including through direct line management of the ESS Technical Director and other senior team members, and, where applicable, consortium or delivery partners, ensuring proper reporting, financial management, and compliance with donor and organisational requirements.

● Build a Core Delivery Team and TA Pool, drawing on national and international expertise only, and ensure all consortium or delivery partners can deploy Syrian expertise, with at least one member registered in Syria.

● Create and maintain a work environment that promotes teamwork, trust, mutual respect, and empowers staff to take responsibility.

● Oversee procurement, logistical, and administrative functions in support of programme delivery.

● Ensure appropriate internal and external communications and knowledge management, sharing achievements and lessons learned with diverse audiences.

**PROFILE AND QUALIFICATIONS**

● Advanced degree (Master's or equivalent) in education, public administration, international development, or a related field; equivalent experience may be substituted for a graduate degree.

● Minimum of 10 years' experience managing large-scale, complex, donor-funded technical assistance or education programmes, ideally including experience with FCDO-funded contracts and performance-based or KPI-linked payment mechanisms.

● Significant prior experience working directly with government ministries or line departments on system-level policy and process reform, ideally within the education sector.

● Substantial experience working in conflict, crisis, or politically sensitive transition contexts; experience in Syria or the broader MENA region strongly preferred.

● Sound understanding of public finance and value-for-money principles, with the ability to support the Ministry in navigating the fiscal choices shaping education sector reform.

● Proven ability to provide strategic leadership while harnessing the multi-disciplinary skills of technical personnel, consortium or delivery partners, and government counterparts.

● Demonstrated ability to create and nurture strong, trusted working relationships with Ministry of Education representatives and other relevant government, donor, and sector stakeholders.

● Strong political judgement, including a sound understanding of how decisions are made within government and where opportunities for reform are most likely to emerge, and demonstrated ability to apply thinking and working politically, using PEA to inform decisions, and to operate flexibly and adaptively in a fast-moving, sensitive institutional environment, responding to windows of opportunity as they arise.

● Demonstrated ability to build and sustain effective, trusted relationships with senior government officials, donors, and a broad range of stakeholders, including civil society and multilateral partners.

● Familiarity with the Syrian education system, or comparable fragile/post-conflict education systems, and with the priorities of foundational learning, safeguarding, and inclusion, including for girls and children with disabilities.

● Experience with adaptive management approaches and evidence-based programming, ideally including leading demand-led technical assistance facilities that use tasking orders or similar call-down mechanisms.

● Experience rapidly mobilising a programme team and establishing an operational presence in a new or complex setting, ideally Syria or a comparable context.

● Demonstrated commitment to localisation, including experience leading predominantly national teams and working in partnership with national and sub-national organisations.

● Strong analytical, communication, and writing skills, with the ability to articulate evidence-based positions to influence sector and government stakeholders.

● Demonstrated ability to apply safeguarding, ethics, and do-no-harm principles throughout programme delivery, particularly when working with or on behalf of children.

● Fluency in English required; Arabic language skills strongly preferred.

***Please note that this position is contingent on the outcome of the FCDO procurement and award of SEP III (tender publication currently anticipated for January 2027 and award for May 2027). Programme details are indicative and remain subject to FCDO approval and the final Tender Notice.***

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

jobs.title: Deputy Director of Operations for Programme and Development – Geneva, Switzerland
jobs.description:
**Department:** Operations

**Duty Station:** Geneva

**Contract Type:** Full-time (100%)

**Direct report:** Director of Operations

**Grade:** Head of

## **Mission**

Geneva Call is a neutral and impartial non-governmental organisation dedicated to promoting respect by Armed Groups and De Facto and/or Provisional Authorities (AGDAs) for international humanitarian norms in armed conflict and other situations of violence, in particular those related to the protection of civilians. Geneva Call focuses its efforts on banning the use of anti-personnel mines, protecting children from the effects of armed conflict, prohibiting sexual violence in armed conflict, working towards the elimination of gender discrimination, protecting civilian infrastructure, and ensuring humanitarian access.

## **Why this role?**

Under the overall supervision of the Director of Operations, the role of Deputy Director of Operations for Programme and Development (DDOPD) is to lead the Programme and Development unit and develop standardised programmatic approaches and models in alignment with programmatic cycle management tools and ensure programmatic interventions are based on Geneva Call’s mission – Theory of Change, strategic priorities, conflict specification framework and humanitarian principles. The DDOPD is accountable for the global programme strategy and quality.

## **Work Relations**

The DDOPD will partner and coordinate as a peer with other operational heads of units such as Policy, Research and Legal (PRL), MEAL and Donor Relations units, and with the Deputy Director of Operations for Africa, to promote coherence in programmatic plans and strategies for internal applications and external dissemination. The DDOPD will be the functional manager of the Regional Heads of Programme and Development to ensure technical guidance and support on programme models and designs from inception to implementation and end evaluation is provided at a regional and country-level, and medium to long term impact is generated. The position in coordination and collaboration with other units will develop strategic programmatic partnerships with other international organisations and networks and organise events in global capitals on protection of civilians through AGDA engagement.

## **Duties and Responsabilities**

**Programme Quality Assurance and Standards**

- Sets global Project Cycle Management standards and ensures the dissemination and application of the Project Cycle Management handbook across all existing and new missions. In consultation with PRL and MEAL units, leads the design, development and streamlining of specific programme models, particularly for new missions, based on Geneva Call’s conflict spectrum framework while incorporating humanitarian engagement principles and thematic priorities in line with Geneva Call’s mission and strategy.
- Leads programme quality reviews at a global level, based on the results matrix and evaluation methodologies developed by the MEAL unit, and contributes to the development of Geneva Call’s internal programmes audit framework in consultation with relevant programme focal points at HQ and regional levels.
- Identifies and coordinates learning needs at a global level and supports the Regional Heads of Programme & Development in building the capacities of programming teams to develop long-term sustainable programmes and measurable impact by incorporating data and lessons learnt from the MEAL unit.
- Uses the progress tracker system designed by MEAL across all missions and produces quarterly reports on programme progress and implementation quality against agreed targets. Develops a standardised programme versus cost estimation simulation model based on GC AGDA engagement programme design.
- Provides functional guidance to Regional Heads of Programme and Development in their technical advisory role to country teams, facilitating the coordination and implementation of projects and programme activities in close consultation with country teams, which retain ownership and accountability for programme delivery. Owns global learning approaches and supports Regional Heads of Programme & Development to host regular learning and collaboration opportunities for field and HQ staff to discuss programme/project implementation strategies and good practices.

**Operational Coordination**

- In close coordination with the Deputy Director of Operations for Africa and Director of Operations, aligns programmatic plans and supports Geneva Call’s institutional strategic development through the implementation of the updated Theory of Change and Strategic Plans in line with GC mission.
- Designs thematic programmes with policy and legal input from the PRL unit on protection of civilians in different conflict context situations.
- In coordination with the MEAL unit, ensures the organisational MEAL framework is fully integrated into programmatic designs from inception to end evaluation stages, utilising data from MEAL activities to enhance programme quality. Ensures all programme designs fully incorporate conflict sensitivity, gender equality, diversity and inclusion, and do not harm principles.
- Provides technical guidance in developing high-quality new project proposals for cross-regional programme design and multi-country donors and leads the management of multi-regional grants.
- In coordination with the Humanitarian Diplomacy & Communications unit, guides programme team to produce impact stories based on successful programmatic intervention. Develops global strategic partnerships and relationships with international organisations to support country missions.

**Fundraising, Grant Management and Donor Briefings**

- Coordinates programme input globally for overall fundraising and relationship building efforts, in close collaboration with the Donor Relations unit.
- Provides regular updates and briefings to donors on programmatic updates and impacts and leads global programme briefings and reporting.
- Provides programmatic guidance to the Grants and Reporting Coordinator.

**Representation and Strategic Partnerships**

- Maintains and strengthens Geneva Call’s role as a neutral, impartial and independent humanitarian actor, positioning the organisation and its operations within the geographical areas to gain maximum access to AGDAs, influential stakeholders and affected populations.
- Engages frequently with high‑level stakeholders and international organisations to secure appropriate support for Geneva Call operations.
- In coordination with the Director of Operations, the DDOPD represents Geneva Call in global forums and performs such other duties as may be assigned.

**Management**

- Shared direct line management of the Regional Heads of Programme and Development, with clearly defined and complementary areas of responsibility. The DDOPD exercises line management authority over programmatic strategy, technical quality, programme delivery, and achievement of functional objectives, while the Deputy Director of Operations exercises line management authority over regional operational management, coordination, and alignment with regional priorities.
- Direct line management of the Programme and Reporting Coordinator at headquarters.

## **Requirements**

**Education (Essential)**

- Master’s degree in political or social sciences, Humanitarian Affairs, International Relations, International Humanitarian Law, Human Rights Law or a related field.

**Experience (Essential)**

- 14+ years of highly relevant experience, with a minimum of 8 years of experience in the field and 3 years of experience at headquarters.
- A minimum of 3 years of experience leading and managing senior managers, included within the overall professional experience requirement.
- Demonstrated experience in implementing programme cycle management tools and leading programme development and quality assurance, as well as experience in humanitarian settings and/or crisis and post-crisis settings.
- Progressively responsible experience in liaising with governmental and diplomatic authorities and international institutions. Demonstrated experience in engaging with armed actors and facilitating constructive dialogue on humanitarian concerns, particularly to promote respect for international humanitarian law and the protection of civilians.
- Advanced understanding of the complex needs of humanitarian operations. Proven experience in resource mobilisation.

**Job related Competencies (Essential)**

- Sound knowledge of financial and business administration and of the principles and practices of management.
- Outstanding interpersonal communication skills and ability to work in a team and across departments to ensure an inclusive, respectful and safe working environment.
- Sound knowledge of the project cycle, as well as of monitoring and evaluation.
- Strong analytical thinking, planning and organising skills, with attention to detail, and structured, strong planning and organisation skills.
- Strategic thinking combined with strong execution skills.

**Organisational Competencies**

- Strong leadership and people management skills.
- Ability to build and maintain trusting and collaborative relationships.
- Ability to promote teamwork and effective collaboration across departments.
- Commitment to fostering an inclusive, respectful and safe working environment.
- Ability to demonstrate accountability, sound judgement and alignment with Geneva Call’s organisational values.

**Language (Essential)**

- Fluency in English and French both spoken and written.

**Language (Desirable)**

- Knowledge of Spanish, Arabic, or any other language relevant to Geneva Call’s operations is an advantage.

## **Why join Geneva Call?**

Geneva Call brings together people of diverse nationalities, cultures, languages and perspectives, fostering an inclusive working environment for all staff.

This role offers the opportunity to advance a meaningful humanitarian mission by strengthening the protection of civilians in armed conflict. The role combines strategic leadership, programme quality and innovation to develop sustainable, impactful programmes, strengthen partnerships and foster collaboration across missions, ultimately contributing to lasting change for communities affected by armed conflict.

jobs.title: Research Manager
jobs.description:
We’re hiring

Research Manager

**LOCATION:** Freetown, Sierra Leone

**GROSS SALARY RANGE:** $4,725.85 – $5,608.40 (gross monthly)

**CONTRACT:** Indefinite

Laterite is looking for an experienced professional to lead research teams, strategy, and operations in our office in Freetown, Sierra Leone.

**WHO WE ARE**

Laterite is a data, research, and analytics firm working on complex development challenges. We partner with universities, global think tanks, international NGOs, multilateral donors, and government ministries. Our clients include the World Bank, TechnoServe, the Mastercard Foundation, and others.

We operate across the Netherlands, Rwanda, Ethiopia, Kenya, Uganda, Tanzania, Sierra Leone, and Peru, with 90+ full-time staff and more than 2,000 enumerators. We believe meaningful impact requires being on the ground, building local teams, and establishing long-term trust. Our office culture is collaborative and gives people autonomy to grow into their roles. Learn more: [www.laterite.com](http://www.laterite.com)

**THE ENVIRONMENT YOU’RE STEPPING INTO**

You will join our Sierra Leone team in a high-trust environment. We are low on bureaucracy but high on individual accountability. You won’t be micromanaged here—we want you to use your judgment to solve problems, support our fast-paced field teams, and actively improve the systems you work with.

Laterite Sierra Leone started operations in 2023. Our office in Freetown is Laterite’s first step in West Africa and will build on our 12+ years of experience of research and data collection. Since then, our Freetown office has been using innovative techniques to study education outcomes in the region. Our team in Freetown currently consists of four team members.

**HOW YOU’LL MAKE AN IMPACT**

As a Research Manager based in Freetown you will:

- Oversee the technical delivery and operations of a portfolio of research projects, from design to data collection, analysis and follow-through.
- Provide technical advice, coaching and steering for research design, project management, analysis, and reporting to ensure we deliver value for our clients and use rigorous and innovative research methods.
- Manage the country office, including structuring Laterite’s research agenda, contributing to corporate strategy, overseeing process improvements, and financial and personnel management.
- Design and lead training and professional development activities for the research team and the wider Laterite team.
- Build and manage the pipeline of research projects, turning internal research ideas into externally funded projects and designing evaluations for clients.

As a member of Laterite’s senior management team, you will consult on corporate strategy, business operations, and opportunities for growth. You will serve as role model for the team, actively promoting our corporate culture, mentoring colleagues, and helping us to achieve our mission as an organization.

Laterite is expanding rapidly, and we are open to the possibility of hiring exceptional candidates at a higher grade.

**WHAT YOU BRING**

We are looking for an accomplished researcher who combines excellent technical skills with management experience. This role is based in Freetown, Sierra Leone, and requires relocation to Sierra Leone as well as a minimum commitment of two years in-country.

Our future colleague has:

- Demonstrated experience leading an organization, department, or program, including financial and operational management.
- Direct supervisory experience and demonstrated experience training and mentoring researchers.
- Demonstrated experience designing and overseeing complex research projects.
- Demonstrated experience building business pipelines and nurturing relationships with clients and stakeholders from the public and private sectors.
- Motivation to work in social and economic research in Sub-Saharan Africa
- 5+ years of research or project management experience and at least 2 years in a management role in education, youth, public health, agriculture and/or urbanization.
- A postgraduate degree (master’s or above) in Economics, Econometrics, Development Research, or in one of Laterite’s core sectors

*Additionally, we are looking for:*

- A self-motivated team leader with excellent interpersonal skills who thrives in a fast-paced environment where timelines can be unpredictable
- Technical expertise in quantitative or qualitative research methods.
- Excellent written and oral communication skills (in English)
- Proficiency in STATA, R, or Python.

**WHAT’S IN IT FOR YOU**

- **Competitive compensation. $4,725.85 – $5,608.40** gross monthly salary (exact grade determined by experience/interviews), medical insurance, pension contribution, and 25 days of annual leave.
- **Professional growth.** We are also committed to supporting our staff’s learning, providing an annual learning budget of up to USD 1,000 per person and 10 days of time off for professional learning each year.
- **Flexibility**: Laterite has a hybrid work policy, with employees expected to work from the office three days per week and the flexibility to work from home for the remaining two days. Employees can also work remotely, away from their home office, for up to six weeks (30 working days) per year.

jobs.title: Chargé-e de Sauvegarde et Protection
jobs.description:
**Aperçu de l'organisation**

Tostan est une organisation internationale à but non lucratif qui accompagne depuis 1991 les communautés d'Afrique de l'Ouest dans la réalisation de leur vision du bien-être et du développement durable. Son approche d'éducation autonomisante et de gouvernance communautaire soutient notamment l'autonomisation des femmes et des filles, le leadership communautaire, la santé, l'éducation, la cohésion sociale, l'autonomisation économique et l'abandon de pratiques néfastes. Dans le cadre de son Plan d'engagement stratégique 2023-2030, Tostan poursuit une stratégie de mise à l'échelle, de partenariat et d'apprentissage visant à renforcer l'impact durable porté par les communautés.

**Aperçu du département**

La fonction Sauvegarde et Conformité veille à prévenir, identifier, signaler et traiter les risques de sauvegarde, de protection et de conduite dans le respect des politiques de Tostan. Elle renforce les mécanismes de prévention, de sensibilisation, d'alerte et de référencement et accompagne les équipes afin de garantir un environnement sûr, respectueux et redevable pour les communautés et le personnel. Dans le cadre du projet HERS, Tostan mobilise des équipes au Sénégal et en Gambie afin de contribuer à l'autonomisation économique et au leadership des jeunes femmes, en s'appuyant sur ses approches de gouvernance communautaire et de transformation sociale. Le poste contribue à la mise en œuvre du projet conformément aux politiques, procédures, standards de sauvegarde et exigences de conformité de Tostan.

**1. Rôles et responsabilités**

Sous la supervision de Responsable Sauvegarde & Conformité, le/la Chargé-e de Sauvegarde et Protection sera responsable d' assurer la mise en œuvre des politiques de sauvegarde et de PEAS/PSEA, la prévention et la gestion des risques de sauvegarde et de protection liés aux activités du projet au Sénégal ,au renforcement des capacités , accompagner les équipes et veiller à l'accessibilité des mécanismes sûrs de signalement et de référencement et garantir un environnement sûr, éthique et conforme.

Il/Elle aura pour mission de :

- Déployer les standards et plans de sauvegarde dans les activités au Sénégal.
- Mettre en œuvre et former le personnel et les partenaires sur la PSEA/PSEAH, le Code de conduite et les voies de signalement.
- Réaliser des analyses de risques et assurer le suivi des mesures de mitigation.
- Maintenir des mécanismes de signalement et des informations de référencement adaptés au contexte local.
- Produire les rapports de prévention et assurer l'escalade des incidents conformément aux procédures.
- Veiller au respect des normes, principes éthiques et exigences de conformité en matière de sauvegarde.
- Documenter les incidents et assurer leur clôture et le suivi des actions correctives ;

Veiller au respect des principes de Do No Harm, confidentialité, non-représailles et approche centrée sur la personne survivante.
**2. Résumé de la position**

Déployer et suivre l’application des politiques, procédures et standards de sauvegarde et de PEAS/PSEA, assurer la prévention et la gestion des risques de sauvegarde et de protection liés aux activités du projet au Sénégal , accompagner les équipes et veiller à l'accessibilité des mécanismes sûrs de signalement et de référencement.

**Responsabilité 1 :** ***Prévention et intégration de la sauvegarde***

- Intégrer les mesures de sauvegarde dans la planification, les activités, événements et partenariats.
- Réaliser des analyses de risques et mettre à jour les plans de mitigation.
- Vérifier que les équipes comprennent les politiques, codes de conduite et voies de signalement.

**Responsabilité 2 :** ***Renforcement des capacités***

- Organiser des formations, briefings et sensibilisations régulières pour le personnel et les parties prenantes.
- Accompagner les points focaux zonaux et assurer un suivi de leurs activités.
- Développer des messages et outils adaptés aux différents publics et langues locales.

**Responsabilité 3 :** ***Signalement, référencement et suivi***

- Veiller à l'accessibilité des canaux de signalement et à leur utilisation sûre et confidentielle.
- Recevoir et transmettre les alertes conformément aux procédures et au principe du besoin d'en connaître.
- Maintenir les répertoires de services de référencement et soutenir la mise à jour des dispositifs de réponse.

\*\*Responsabilité 4 :\*\****Gestion des incidents de sauvegarde***

- Recevoir , documenter, trier et suivre les signalements conformément aux procédures et aux principes de confidentialité et de protection.

**Responsabilité 5 :** ***Conformité et suivi des actions***

- Suivre les écarts, les recommandations et les mesures correctives, et contribuer à l’amélioration continue du dispositif de sauvegarde.

**Responsabilité 6 :** ***Monitoring et reporting***

- Effectuer des visites de suivi et contrôles de conformité de la sauvegarde dans les zones d'intervention.
- Documenter les activités de prévention, risques et actions correctives sans exposer de données sensibles.
- Produire les rapports périodiques et contribuer aux audits et revues de conformité.

> **Cette liste n'est pas exhaustive. Le/la Chargé.e de Sauvegarde et Protection pourra être appelé.e à effectuer toute autre tâche qui pourrait lui être confiée en rapport avec ses compétences ou son poste**.

**3. Relations clés :**

***Superviseur direct (N+1) :*** Responsable Sauvegarde & Conformité

***Collaborateurs directs (N-1) :*** Aucun à la prise de fonction, sauf disposition organisationnelle spécifique validée.

***Rapports directs (liens fonctionnels directs) :*** Équipes Programmes, SERA/MERL, Finance, Opérations, Ressources Humaines, Communication et Sauvegarde concernées, selon les besoins du poste.

***Autres collègues :*** Coordinations pays et zones, équipes support, communautés, prestataires, autorités et partenaires concernés par la fonction.

***Localisation :*** Sénégal - base à préciser, avec déplacements terrain

**4. Qualifications clés requises :**

***L'éducation :***

- Bac+4/5 en sciences sociales, droit, protection, genre, travail social, psychologie, développement ou domaine connexe.

***Compétences linguistiques :***

- Excellente maîtrise du français.
- Bon niveau d'anglais souhaité pour la coordination régionale.
- La maîtrise de langues nationales pertinentes constitue un atout important.

***Connaissance et expérience :***

- Au moins 4 ans d'expérience dans la sauvegarde, protection, PSEA/PSEAH, genre ou domaine connexe.
- Expérience de formation d'adultes, analyse de risques et mise en place de mécanismes de signalement.
- Bonne connaissance des principes de confidentialité, approche centrée sur les survivant.e.s et référencement.
- Expérience de travail communautaire ou au sein d'une ONG fortement souhaitée.

***Caractéristiques***

- Intégrité, discrétion, empathie et jugement professionnel.
- Capacité à gérer des informations sensibles avec un strict respect de la confidentialité.
- Très bonnes capacités de formation, communication et écoute.
- Courage professionnel, neutralité et capacité à escalader les risques au bon niveau.

\*\*Type de contrat :\*\*CDD de projet / contrat local à durée déterminée, aligné sur la durée et les besoins du projet, sous réserve des dispositions légales applicables, de la disponibilité des financements et des politiques RH de Tostan.

jobs.title: WASH Specialist - Mozambique
jobs.description:
**Position Title - WASH Specialist**

**Duty Station - Pemba with travel to districts**

**Reports To - Programme Coordinator**

**Contract Type - Service Provider Consultancy Contract (approx one year)**

**Closing date of applications - 2 November 2026**

The WASH Specialist leads the planning, design, implementation, monitoring and quality assurance of all Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH) activities in Mozambique - in both communities and health facilities - ensuring that objectives are achieved on time and in line with technical standards and donor requirements.

Reporting to the Programme Coordinator, the WASH Specialist provides technical and leadership on WASH infrastructure, from design and technical specifications through to construction supervision and operation and maintenance, as well as on hygiene promotion and infection prevention and control.

The WASH Specialist works closely with local authorities, health institutions, communities, partners and contractors to improve access to safe water, sanitation and hygiene, and ensures WASH activities are well integrated with the other programme components.

**Requirements for the role:**

- Degree in Civil Engineering, Water/Environmental Engineering, Public Health or a related field.
- Proven technical expertise in WASH infrastructure design and supervision, including water supply systems, sanitation facilities, drainage, and healthcare waste management.
- Demonstrated experience in WASH within Health Facilities and Infection Prevention and Control (IPC), as well as community-level WASH and hygiene promotion activities.
- Strong experience in construction supervision and contractor management, including technical specifications, Bills of Quantities (BoQs), site inspections, and ESHS (Environmental, Social, Health, and Safety) compliance.
- Familiarity with emergency WASH interventions, climate-resilient designs, and inclusive/accessible infrastructure (gender and disability sensitivity).
- Proven track record in M&E, budget management, procurement coordination, and donor reporting within international NGO environments.
- Excellent representation and coordination skills for active engagement with the WASH Cluster, government health/water authorities, and local partners.
- Experience working in conflict or emergency settings (Experience in Mozambique, particularly Cabo Delgado, is a strong advantage).
- Fluent in Portuguese and English (both written and spoken, essential).

**The main responsibilities of this post include the following:**

**1. Technical Coordination and Programme Management**

- Lead the planning, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of all WASH activities.
- Develop annual, quarterly and monthly WASH work plans to ensure programme targets and objectives are achieved.
- Ensure compliance with MENTOR policies, donor requirements, technical standards and national regulations.
- Conduct assessments, technical surveys and programme reviews to identify needs and improve programme quality.
- Support the development of proposals, budgets and donor reports.
- Ensure integration of WASH activities with other programme components where appropriate.

**2. Infrastructure Design and Construction Supervision**

- Prepare designs for water supply systems, sanitation facilities, handwashing stations and waste management infrastructure.
- Ensure designs are climate-resilient, accessible and inclusive (gender, disability).
- Draft technical specifications and bills of quantities; support bid evaluation and contractor mobilisation.
- Conduct regular site inspections, verify the progress and quality of works, manage variation orders and follow up on defect rectification.
- Monitor contractor compliance with Environmental, Social, Health and Safety (ESHS) requirements.

**3. Community WASH Activities**

**Safe Water Supply**

- Oversee activities to improve access to safe and adequate water in targeted communities.
- Supervise the rehabilitation, installation, operation and maintenance of water supply systems.
- Ensure regular water quality monitoring and the implementation of water safety measures.
- Coordinate emergency water supply interventions when required.
- Promote sustainable community management of water infrastructure.

**Sanitation**

- Supervise the rehabilitation, construction and improvement of sanitation facilities in communities.
- Promote safe sanitation and environmental health practices.
- Ensure facilities are accessible and inclusive for all users.

**Hygiene Promotion**

- Lead the design and implementation of hygiene promotion and behaviour change activities.
- Develop and adapt information, education and communication materials.
- Ensure community participation throughout implementation.

**WASH Kits and Supplies**

- Plan and oversee the distribution of hygiene kits, water treatment products and other WASH supplies.
- Ensure transparent and accountable distribution processes, including post-distribution monitoring.

**4. WASH in Health Facilities**

**Infrastructure**

- Conduct assessments of WASH conditions in health facilities.
- Oversee the rehabilitation and upgrading of water systems, sanitation facilities, drainage, handwashing stations and healthcare waste management infrastructure.

**Infection Prevention and Control (IPC)**

- Support the implementation of WASH and IPC standards in health facilities, including healthcare waste management and environmental cleaning.
- Organise training for health facility staff on WASH-related IPC practices.

**Operation and Maintenance**

- Develop operation and maintenance plans for rehabilitated infrastructure.
- Build the capacity of health facility staff to maintain WASH systems and monitor their functionality.

**5. Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning**

- Develop and implement WASH monitoring tools, in coordination with the M&E team.
- Conduct regular field monitoring visits and technical supervision.
- Analyse programme data and prepare technical reports.
- Document lessons learned and good practices.
- Ensure timely and accurate internal and donor reporting.

**6. Staff Supervision and Capacity Building**

- Supervise WASH staff and provide technical guidance.
- Conduct regular performance reviews and support staff development.
- Identify training needs and organise capacity building for staff, contractors, partners and community water and sanitation committees.
- Promote teamwork and a positive working environment.

**7. Budget and Resource Management**

- Prepare and monitor budgets for WASH activities.
- Ensure efficient and accountable use of programme resources.
- Coordinate closely with the logistics, finance, administration and procurement teams.

**8. Representation and Coordination**

- Represent MENTOR in WASH Cluster meetings and technical working groups.
- Maintain effective relationships with government water, sanitation and health authorities, donors and partners.
- Contribute technical inputs to proposals, strategic plans and programme development.

**9. Other**

- Uphold MENTOR's values, policies, safeguarding principles and Code of Conduct.
- Ensure all WASH activities are implemented in line with humanitarian principles and quality standards.
- Undertake any other duties reasonably assigned by the Programme Coordinator.

The MENTOR Initiative is an equal opportunity employer and values diversity in the organisation. We ensure constant non-discrimination throughout the recruitment process.

The MENTOR Initiative is committed to promoting diversity and gender equality and strongly encourages candidates from under-represented backgrounds to apply.

The MENTOR Initiative applies a zero-tolerance approach to sexual exploitation, abuse, mistreatment or harassment, and other types of unethical behaviour including fraud.

The MENTOR Initiative will contact previous employers of applicants to determine if they have any history of violating international standards and codes of conduct relating to such matters.

jobs.title: Somalia - Head of Mission (National Candidates Only)
Functional Lead, Humanitarian ERP
jobs.description:
NGO finance & procurement · Business analysis

**Remote · EuropeContract4 days / week**

Relief Applications is a humanitarian tech company headquartered in Toulouse, France. We build digital tools with and for NGOs, UN agencies and mission-driven organisations, bringing solutions to those changing the world.

We are growing our ERP offer for NGOs: Finance, Procurement and HR modules designed for how humanitarian organisations actually work.

## **About the role**

You will be the business brain of the project. Working side by side with our project manager, you will turn NGOs’ finance, procurement and HR needs into features.

Your work makes our ERP stronger with every deployment and decides whether client teams adopt it. You will run workshops with them, shape the workflows, test what is built and train the users. Occasional travel to clients is expected.

## **Key responsibilities**

### **Requirements & functional design**

- Co-run user-requirement workshops with client Finance, Procurement and HR teams
- Write clear user stories, workflows and acceptance criteria
- Own the functional design of the Finance, Procurement and HR modules: approval chains, budgets and cost codes, data model and reporting
- Flag early when deeper expertise is needed, such as local payroll or HR law

### **Building & testing**

- Prototype and ship features, screens and fixes with AI-supported tools (Claude, Cursor or similar)
- Work through Git with the tech lead and developers, who review your code
- Test features against real NGO scenarios and run user acceptance testing with clients

### **Adoption**

- Review and complete user guides
- Design and deliver trainings for finance, procurement and HR users
- Collect feedback after go-live and turn it into improvements

## **Candidate profile**

### **Additional assets**

- Previous ERP implementation or rollout (Sage, Dynamics, Odoo, SunSystems…)
- Experience with charity finance across several countries
- MEAL or logframe exposure
- Training and documentation experience

### **Experience**

- 3–5+ years in NGO or humanitarian operations, ideally in finance, grants or procurement
- Solid working knowledge of donor rules, budget lines, cost codes, purchase-to-pay flows and grant reporting
- Hands-on experience building with AI

### **Languages**

- Fluent English; French is a plus

### **Skills**

- Business analysis: running workshops, mapping processes, writing user stories
- Comfortable with Git, reading code, and basic data and SQL
- Able to turn rules into working features

### **Soft skills**

- Autonomous and pragmatic
- Confident facing a client’s team
- Honest about what you know and what you don’t

jobs.title: Full-time Programme Internship (New York)
jobs.description:
**About ISHR**

ISHR is an independent, non-profit organisation with offices in Geneva and New York. This internship offers a unique opportunity to view the United Nations human rights system at work in New York. It provides hands-on experience working for an international non-governmental organisation (NGO) as well as the opportunity to contribute to our work supporting human rights defenders, strengthening human rights systems, building and leading human rights coalitions, and responding to significant and systemic human rights concerns. For more information, consult our website [https://ishr.ch/](https://ishr.ch/).

**Internship position**

The Intern will work closely with Programme Officers/Managers and Directors, contributing to our work supporting human rights defenders, strengthening human rights systems, building and leading human rights coalitions, and responding to significant and systemic situations of concern.

Working in a small team, the Intern will have the opportunity to learn at close hand what it means to work for an international human rights advocacy organisation. The Intern will also have the opportunity to collaborate with ISHR staff in all locations and gain hands-on experience on the application of international human rights law in a multilateral human rights system, including advocacy on normative and policy advances for the protection of human rights defenders.

**Training and Opportunities**

Our Interns are fully included as part of the team, including in staff meetings, which provide a comprehensive understanding of the work of an international human rights NGO. Interns also have opportunities to interact and network with human rights defenders, diplomats or other UN and NGO professionals both at the United Nations and at ISHR’s office (or remotely) during meetings.

Where appropriate or necessary for their work, ISHR staff will provide practical sessions and guidance, for example, on monitoring UN mechanisms, drafting reports and advocacy documents, utilising communications technologies, etc. Interns will be supervised by one or two experienced programme managers and supported in achieving their learning objectives through regular check-ins with the Intern Coordinator.

**Key tasks**

- Providing support to programme staff in the implementation of project activities, across ISHR’s strategic programme areas including improving civil society engagement at the UN, addressing reprisals, as well as other projects seeking to enhance protection for human rights defenders;
- Contributing to ISHR’s outreach and communications, including regular online publications;
- Monitoring and reporting on UN human rights meetings, including the ECOSOC’s Committee on NGOs and General Assembly’s Third Committee;
- Approximately 15-20% of the work will be administrative in nature, including assisting with the organisation and preparation of events, training and meetings.

**Internship modalities**

The internship will be in person, in ISHR’s New York Office and will start on 11 January 2027. It is a 6-months full-time (37.5 hours per week) position with no possibility of extension.

**Stipend**

Internships will be compensated with:

- a stipend of USD700/month.
- 25 annual vacation days per calendar year, pro-rated based on start/departure date (12,5 days for six months)

**Requirements**

We expect the successful candidates to:

- be an advanced undergraduate student or graduate student in international relations, law, international public law, human rights or a related field, or have recently completed such studies;
- be motivated to pursue a career in human rights and have a particular interest in the UN and regional human rights systems;
- have **an excellent level of written and spoken English;**
- be detail-oriented and attentive to nuance, in particular in diplomatic environments;
- be motivated, autonomous and a self-starter, and comfortable occasionally working with limited supervision;
- be able to work as a member of an international and multicultural team and willing to participate in a variety of tasks, as required;
- **be authorised to work in the U.S.**

Additional particularly appreciated skills:

- **Advanced to fluent Spanish and/or French and/or Arabic language; Mandarin is also an asset.**
- interest or background, including activism in, corporate accountability, women’s rights, and/or LGBTI rights;
- legal drafting and research including on treaty body jurisprudence;
- interest or background in training/capacity building, including online learning, logistics, travel and event planning;
- be proficient with Google Suite and/or Microsoft tools.

**Equal opportunity**

ISHR is firmly committed to the principle of equal employment opportunity and aims to have a diverse team. ISHR's policy is to practice fair and non-discriminatory recruitment and selection procedures and strive for diverse, international and multicultural personnel. We welcome all kinds of diversity.

Applications are encouraged from all qualified candidates without distinction including on grounds of race, colour, national origin, age, religion, disability status, sexual orientation, gender identity and expression or sex characteristics, pregnancy, genetic information, protected veteran status, socio-economic status, or any other characteristic protected by law. We particularly welcome applications from systematically, historically and/or traditionally discriminated against under-represented groups, including women, persons of colour, LGBTIQ+ persons, persons with disabilities and other groups.

To request reasonable accommodation to participate in the job application or interview process, please contact ISHR’s Human Resources department at hr@ishr.ch

jobs.title: Operations & Finance Coordinator - Mozambique
jobs.description:
**Position Title - Operations & Finance Coordinator (HR, Finance, and Logistics)**

**Duty Station - Pemba (Cabo Delgado, Mozambique) with travel to field bases / districts**

**Reports To - Country Director and HQ Grants Manager**

**Contract Type - Full-time, fixed term approx one year (International Consultant)**

**Closing date of applications - 2 November 2026**

The MENTOR Initiative (‘MENTOR’) is a humanitarian organisation specialising in disease control and improving access to healthcare in emergency settings across countries in Africa, the Middle East and South America. MENTOR is the leading organisation dedicated to the control of malaria and other vector-borne diseases in complex, vulnerable settings.

MENTOR delivers large scale disease control interventions working with communities affected by emergencies such as conflict and natural disasters and at higher risk of diseases. We also help build the technical and operational capacity of local and international partners to incorporate medium- and long-term disease control systems into their operations and country strategy.

**Requirements for the role**

- Education: Advanced University Degree (Master's preferred) in Business Administration, Finance, Accounting, Logistics, Human Resources, International Relations, or related field.
- Professional background in financial, administrative and operational management is essential.
- Minimum of 10 years of field experience in international NGOs, with at least 5 years in senior coordination roles in emergency or conflict settings.
- Extensive experience managing various departments (HR, Finance, and Logistics), including supply chain, procurement and team leadership.
- Familiarity with Mozambican labour and tax regulations, as well as local legal compliance (Experience working in Mozambique, specifically Cabo Delgado, a strong advantage).
- Extensive knowledge of financial management rules and procurement procedures of major international donors.
- Highly organised with strong coordination and project management skills, proficient in accounting software (preferably SAGA) and advanced Excel.
- Excellent communication and reporting skills for efficient collaboration with HQ and donors.
- Ability to work in a multicultural environment under high pressure, demonstrating strong ethical principles, compliance, and problem-solving skills in volatile contexts.
- Fluent in Portuguese and English (both written and spoken, essential).

**Position Overview**

The Operations and Finance Coordinator (OFC) is a key member of the Country Management Team (CMT) and serves as the primary executive responsible for the leadership, oversight, and integrity of the Human Resources, Finance and Logistics departments of The MENTOR Initiative in Cabo Delgado, Mozambique.

Working in close coordination with the Country Director and the HQ Grants Manager, the OFC ensures financial sustainability, operational supply chain efficiency, and strict compliance with local and international labor, tax and safeguarding policies. The role ensures that all humanitarian interventions are executed with high quality, transparency, and full adherence to donor regulations.

**Main Responsibilities**

**1. Human Resources Management and Leadership (National and International)**

As the primary head of the HR department in Mozambique:

- Legal and Tax Compliance: Lead the rigorous application of Mozambican Labor Law, tax codes (INSS, IRPS), and local regulations, acting as the focal point with the General Labor Inspection and local legal advisors.
- Recruitment and Contract Management: Oversee the complete lifecycle of national staff and community volunteers (job postings, screening, hiring, renewals, and separations), ensuring transparent and auditable processes.
- Payroll Management: Lead and approve the monthly processing of salaries, allowances, and per diems, ensuring accurate and timely payments.
- Team Administration: Oversee the administration of the international team in Cabo Delgado, including work visas, international travel, leave schedules, and direct coordination with HQ HR.
- Performance Management and Staff Development: Implement continuous performance appraisal systems, manage disciplinary procedures, and design capacity-building and training plans for local teams.
- Safeguarding, Code of Conduct, and PSEAH: Enforce zero-tolerance policies and ensure strict adherence to MENTOR’s Code of Conduct by leading briefings, trainings, and in-country complaint/incident handling in coordination with HQ.

**2. Financial Management, Accounting, and Budget Monitoring**

As the primary lead for the mission's financial integrity:

- Accounting Systems: Ensure the proper operation and maintenance of high-quality financial systems using MENTOR’s accounting software (SAGA) and supervise monthly mission book-closing.
- Budget Tracking and Control: Prepare and update monthly Budget Versus Actual (BVA) trackings for all active grants, identifying variances and proposing timely reallocations in coordination with the HQ Grants Manager.
- Treasury and Cash Flow: Lead liquidity management across Pemba and field bases, overseeing local bank accounts, cash safes, fund transfers, and routine Cash Requests to HQ.
- Accountability and Audits: Ensure 100% of financial documentation, invoices, and receipts comply with MENTOR and donor auditability standards; lead preparation for internal and external audits.
- Proposal Development: Collaborate with HQ and the Country Director in developing realistic budgets for new funding proposals.

**3. Logistics, Supply Chain and Transport Management**

As the primary lead for operational logistics support:

- Procurement: Supervise all local and national procurement of goods, equipment, and services, ensuring strict adherence to threshold rules, market surveys, quotation collection, and Procurement Committee processes.
- International Procurement and Customs: Coordinate with HQ on tracking international orders, managing customs clearance processes, and securing VAT/customs duty exemptions with Mozambican authorities.
- Inventory and Warehouse Management: Guarantee rigorous control over central and field warehouses (stock cards, waybills, monthly physical counts), paying special attention to cold chain systems, medical stocks, and WASH supplies.
- Fleet and Transport Management: Oversee the vehicle fleet (owned and rented), ensuring preventive maintenance schedules, fuel monitoring, insurance, logbooks, and safe road, air, and sea transport for staff and cargo to field locations.
- Asset and Facility Management: Maintain an updated master asset register and ensure the functional operational infrastructure of bases and guesthouses (generators, satellite/HF/VHF communications, internet, and utilities).

**4. Security Management Support and Field Operations**

- Serve as the Operational Security Focal Point as delegated by the Country Director.
- Ensure all bases, vehicles, and field teams are equipped with appropriate security equipment (hibernation kits, communications, pre-movement route checks).
- Monitor the evolving security situation in Cabo Delgado in coordination with INSO, UNDSS, and humanitarian partners, supporting updates to evacuation and contingency plans.

**5. Team Leadership, Communication, and External Representation**

- Directly line manage HR, Finance, and Logistics officers/managers in Pemba and field bases.
- Represent The MENTOR Initiative in external coordination forums in Mozambique (Logistics Cluster, NGO HR/Admin Forums, Finance Working Groups).
- Produce regular operational and financial contributions to internal situation reports (sit-reps) and meet all reporting requirements established by the HQ Grants Manager.

jobs.title: Point Focal Suivi-Evaluation- Recherche et Apprentissage (SERA) - Zonal
jobs.description:
**Aperçu de l'organisation**

Tostan est une organisation à but non lucratif 501(c)(3) dont le siège est à Dakar, au Sénégal, et qui opère actuellement dans cinq pays d'Afrique de l'Ouest. Sur le plan stratégique, l'organisation s'est engagée à poursuivre le développement de sa compétence de base, à savoir l'autonomisation de l'éducation, et à documenter et mettre à l'échelle l'impact durable qu'elle crée sur toute une série de questions. Le modèle phare de Tostan, le Programme de Renforcement de Capacités des Communautés (PRCC) de trois ans, a déjà touché des milliers de communautés en Afrique de l'Ouest et de l'Est depuis 1991. Les résultats en matière de gouvernance, d'éducation, de santé, d'autonomisation économique et d'environnement sont actuellement suivis, et Tostan est particulièrement fier d'avoir joué un rôle important dans l'autonomisation à grande échelle des femmes et des filles et dans l'abandon par la communauté de pratiques néfastes telles que l’excision et le mariage des enfants. Dans le cadre de son [plan d'engagement stratégique ](https://tostan.org/tostan-strategy-2023-2030-in-partnership-for-community-well-being/)2023-2030, Tostan se concentre sur la mise à l’échelle stratégique. L'organisation développe de nouvelles stratégies de mise en œuvre pour soutenir le leadership communautaire en débloquant des changements systémiques à plus grande échelle au niveau régional. Elle crée également de nouveaux modèles pour partager et reproduire ses programmes avec d'autres partenaires de développement et étend ses capacités à partager l'approche globale de Tostan pour soutenir et influencer un éventail de publics locaux et mondiaux. Pour plus d'informations, veuillez consulter le site : [www.tostan.org ](http://www.tostan.org/).

**Aperçu du département**

L’équipe de Suivi, Evaluation, Recherche et Apprentissage (SERA) est partie intégrante du Département Programme de Tostan. Elle a pour mission de coordonner et d’appuyer le système de suivi et évaluation des programmes dans les pays où Tostan travaille mais aussi la recherche et l’apprentissage. A travers cette équipe, Tostan suit constamment les performances réalisées dans les communautés partenaires et réalise des évaluations internes impliquant des études de base, des évaluations à mi-parcours et des évaluations finales.

**1. Rôles et responsabilités**

Sous la supervision technique du SERA et la supervision administrative de…………. , Coordonnateur zonal le point focal sera/chargé-e de veiller à la stricte mise en oeuvre de toutes les activités de suivi-évaluation dans sa zone d’affectation

Il/Elle aura pour mission de :

- Soutenir et coordonner les stratégies et les actions de suivi/évaluation mises en œuvre par SERA au niveau des coordinations zonales
- Assurer le contrôle des fiches de suivi
- S’assurer que les données sont collectées ;
- S’assurer que les données collectées sont transmises à SERA national et/ou international ;
- Assurer des missions de suivi en collaboration avec le Coordonnateur zonal et le responsable SERA Sénégal pour s’assurer de l’état d’avancement des activités sur le terrain
- Appuyer la formation des CGC sur les aspects liés au Suivi-Évaluation ;

**2. Résumé de la position**

En tant qu’agent de l’équipe du SERA:

**Responsabilité 1:** ***veiller à l’application stricte du dispositif de suivi mis en place par SERA***

- Connaître le dispositif de suivi - évaluation mis en place
- Partager les composantes du dispositif avec les collègue de la coordination (coordonnateur, superviseurs et autres acteurs concernés)
- Veiller à ce que toute contrainte rencontrée dans la mise en oeuvre du dispositif soit documentée et partagée avec la hiérarchie

**Responsabilité 2:** ***renforcer les capacités du staff de terrain (superviseurs et facilitateurs) en Suivi Évaluation, sur la méthodologie de collecte de données et sur le remplissage des fiches de collecte***

- Former le staff de la coordination en particulier Coordonnateur et superviseurs sur le suivi évaluation ;
- Former les superviseurs sur le remplissage des fiches de collecte.

**Responsabilité 3:** ***s’assurer que les données de suivi sont collectées à temps selon les périodicités convenues***

- Vérifier si les fiches de collectes sont à jour
- S’assurer que les données sont collectées par chaque superviseur dans sa zone
- S’assurer de la complétudes et de la qualité des données collectées
- S’assurer que les données collectées sont transmises au SERA

**Responsabilité 4:** ***appuyer ou piloter la planification et le recueil, des données qualitatives et quantitatives sur le terrain lors des études de milieu, études de base, évaluations à mi-parcours et finales***

- Participer à la planification des études et évaluations ;
- participer et jouer un rôle actif dans la formation sur la méthodologie et les outils pour la collecte de données lors des études et évaluations ;
- Participer à la supervision de la collecte des données ;
- S’assurer de la qualité et de la complétude des données pour chaque étude et évaluation.

**3. Relations clés :**

- ***Superviseur direct (N+1) :*** Coordonnateur zonal
- ***Collaborateurs directs (N-1) :***
- ***Rapports directs (liens fonctionnels directs) :*** superviseurs
- ***Autres collègues :*** staff de la coordination
- ***Localisation :*** Kolda, Tambacounda, Ziguinchor, Kaolack

**4. Qualifications clés requises :**

***L'éducation :***

- Avoir au moins 3 ans d’expérience dans le domaine du suivi évaluation des projets de développement ;
- Avoir un diplôme de niveau licence ou équivalent en développement communautaire/local ou en planification, élaboration et gestion des projets de développement, en Suivi-évaluation des projets.

***Compétences linguistiques :***

- Savoir parler, lire et écrire en français ;
- Avoir une bonne connaissance d’au moins une langue nationale pratiquée dans la zone d’affectation.

***Connaissance et expérience :***

Le point focal zonal SERA doit avoir des compétences et aptitudes avérées dans les domaines suivants :

- Avoir des capacité à coordonner simultanément plusieurs projets différents ;
- Avoir des connaissances et qualifications en matière de développement communautaire ;
- Avoir des connaissances et une expérience avérée dans la conception, la mise en œuvre et le suivi évaluation des projets de développement ;
- Maîtriser l’outil informatique et en particulier savoir utiliser les logiciels courants (Word, EXCEL, Power Point). La maîtrise d’autres logiciels tels que Airtable, Tableau etc serait un atout ;
- Savoir utiliser les tablettes pour une collecte de données électroniques ;
- Avoir l’expérience de travailler en milieu rural avec les populations dans le respect de la dignité humaine, et être apte à supporter le travail sous pression.

***Caractéristiques :***

- Etre ouvert et coopératif ;
- Savoir travailler sous pression et dans un environnement complexe et multiculturel ;
- Avoir d'excellentes compétences en gestion du temps, ainsi que la capacité à mener plusieurs tâches de front et à hiérarchiser les priorités ;
- Avoir le permis de conduire.

***Type de contrat :*** Contrat local

jobs.title: Programme Coordinator - Mozambique
jobs.description:
**Position Title - Programme Coordinator**

**Duty Station - Pemba with travel to districts**

**Reports To - HQ Programme Manager**

**Contract Type - Full-time, fixed term approx one year**

**Closing date of applications - 2 November 2026**

The Programme Coordinator (PC) leads the overall implementation of The MENTOR Initiative's programmes in Mozambique, with a particular focus on Water, Sanitation and Hygiene (WASH), ensuring that objectives are achieved on time while identifying needs and opportunities and shaping strategic and operational responses.

The PC provides in-country leadership and representation, with overall responsibility for fundraising, financial and grant management, human resources, technical programme support and logistics.

The PC coordinates the different programmes to ensure consistent, high-quality, accountable and transparent delivery across them all.

**Requirements for the role:**

- Background in programme management in humanitarian settings is essential, with a strong focus on WASH (Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene) and its integration with public health interventions.
- Extensive experience in in-country operational leadership, including security management in volatile environments, HR supervision, financial management, and logistics.
- Proven track record in grant management and donor relations, including proposal writing, budget tracking, and high-quality reporting to institutional donors.
- Demonstrable experience managing multicultural teams and coordinating across multiple field bases in conflict or crisis-affected regions.
- Familiarity with local labour and tax regulations, legal compliance, and standard NGO operating procedures (Experience working in Mozambique, particularly Cabo Delgado, is a strong advantage).
- Strong understanding of safeguarding and PSEAH policies, with experience in incident reporting, case management and promoting a culture of zero tolerance.
- Highly organised with strong strategic planning, analytical and data management skills, using project log frames as strategic implementation tools.
- Excellent communication, networking and representation skills for active engagement with Health and WASH Clusters, local authorities and donors.
- Fluent in Portuguese and English (both written and spoken, essential).

**The main responsibilities of this post include the following:**

**1. Security Management**

Working closely with the HQ Programme Manager, the PC is responsible for overall security management in a potentially insecure and unstable context:

- Maintain strong networks and regularly collect and analyse information on the security situation.
- Organise regular security updates with MENTOR field bases and report to MENTOR HQ.
- Ensure security-related logistical support is adequate and functional.
- Keep security guidelines current and pragmatic, including evacuation and hibernation plans for all bases.
- Ensure all MENTOR team members strictly follow security rules.
- Provide thorough security briefings to new expatriate team members on arrival.

**2. Programme Management**

- Lead the implementation of MENTOR programmes, in particular water supply, sanitation and hygiene promotion (WASH) activities and their integration with other public health interventions.
- Ensure an efficient data collection and analysis system that meets the reporting needs of all grants.
- Use project log frames as a tool for strategic planning and implementation.
- Work closely with the coordination team to ensure activities are delivered on plan, on objective, and within security constraints.
- Represent MENTOR to external meetings with Clusters (WASH, Health), Authorities, donors, etc.
- Oversee delivery of existing programmes and supervise, develop and support the team.
- Coordinate strategic planning for programme development.
- Ensure quality monthly, quarterly and annual reports are submitted to HQ on time.

**3. Donor Management**

- Oversee grant management, including appropriate expenditure and timely reporting to HQ ahead of donor submission.
- Coordinate and finalise field drafts of donor progress reports for HQ review within required deadlines.
- Carry out exploratory field missions, with HQ, to assess and report on potential new intervention areas.
- Liaise with current and prospective donors, in consultation with HQ, to advance programme ideas and secure funding and support.

**4. Financial and Administrative Management**

Working closely with the in-country Finance team and the HQ Grants Manager, the PC is responsible for the financial integrity of the programme and the cost-effective use of resources in line with available budgets and MENTOR standard procedures:

- Ensure appropriate security precautions around cash management.
- Keep budget tracking for all grants up to date, in collaboration with the Finance Coordinator.
- Ensure monthly finance documents (expenditure reports, cash requests, payroll, budget plans) reach HQ on time.
- Ensure expenditure documentation meets MENTOR standard requirements.
- Ensure compliance with local taxation and labour regulations.
- Finalise and endorse official mission documentation (MOUs, contracts, agreements).
- Track proposal and administrative requirements relevant to the country context.
- Secure HQ authorisation for all new grants.

**5. Human Resource Management**

- Directly manage MENTOR Coordinators and oversee their management of programme and operational support staff.
- Participate in recruitment and final selection of consultant team members.
- Lead in-country briefings for incoming consultants and debriefings for those completing contracts.
- Ensure timely performance reviews for all consultant staff and conduct reviews for direct reports.
- Oversee and approve recruitment of national staff in line with national labour law.
- Review internal HR policies with the Finance and HR team, in line with national labour law.
- Ensure consistent application of national contract formats and per diem policies.
