- Lead weekly and ad hoc team meetings, and senior programme management meetings.
- Ensure contracts, the Code of Conduct, and MENTOR policies are respected by all staff.
- Implement MENTOR's Safeguarding/PSEAH policies, training and briefings for staff and volunteers.
- Support in-country Safeguarding Focal Points, in collaboration with the HQ Safeguarding focal point.
- Lead on safeguarding matters, ensuring effective support and appropriate case management.
- Ensure timely incident reporting to HQ on any policy or Code of Conduct violations and support ongoing cases.

**6. Logistics**

Working closely with the logistics team:

- Ensure adequate logistical support for security management.
- Oversee timely procurement in line with budgets, programme needs and guidelines.
- Oversee stock management of assets, WASH materials, medicines and prevention materials.
- Maintain logistical filing systems, including equipment manuals, maintenance schedules and waybills.
- Oversee fleet renewal and maintenance per HQ instructions.
- Oversee procurement, maintenance and use of communications equipment (HF, VHF, satellite phone/internet).
- Coordinate daily transport activities by road and air.

**7. Communication**

**Internal**

- Ensure regular communication within programme teams and hold regular general team meetings.
- Organise regular management meetings for all coordinators.
- Produce regular internal situation reports.
- Brief HQ (PM and GM) regularly.

**External**

- Ensure MENTOR's participation in relevant external meetings.
- Organise and join technical meetings with health and WASH stakeholders.
- Maintain transparent, efficient data and information exchange with stakeholders.
- Build strong working relationships with partners, donors and stakeholders; identify development and emergency funding opportunities through forums and conferences.

**8. Other**

- Share best practice across the organisation as required.
- Undertake any other duties assigned by the HQ Programme Manager.

The MENTOR Initiative is an equal opportunity employer and values diversity in the organisation. We ensure constant non-discrimination throughout the recruitment process.

The MENTOR Initiative is committed to promoting diversity and gender equality and strongly encourages candidates from under-represented backgrounds to apply.

The MENTOR Initiative applies a zero-tolerance approach to sexual exploitation, abuse, mistreatment or harassment, and other types of unethical behaviour including fraud.

The MENTOR Initiative will contact previous employers of applicants to determine if they have any history of violating international standards and codes of conduct relating to such matters.

jobs.title: Responsable Analyse Médicale et Plaidoyer - Est de la RDC (h/f/x) - Médecins Sans Frontières
jobs.description:
**CONTEXTE**

En République Démocratique du Congo (RDC), Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) travaille en collaboration avec le Ministère de la Santé afin de fournir des soins médicaux aux victimes des conflits et des violences, aux personnes déplacées ainsi qu'aux personnes affectées par des épidémies ou pandémies telles que le VIH/SIDA, la tuberculose, le paludisme, la malnutrition, entre autres. Ces situations sont souvent associées à la faiblesse des institutions étatiques, aux capacités limitées du système de santé public et à une compréhension insuffisante des besoins et des lacunes réels sur le terrain. La contribution de MSF s'appuie sur ses projets réguliers ainsi que sur ses équipes de réponse d'urgence, prêtes à intervenir sur l'ensemble du territoire en cas d'épidémie, de catastrophe naturelle ou de conflit.

En 2023, face à l'intensification de la violence dans l'est de la RDC, qui a entraîné le déplacement d'un nombre record de civils, MSF a renforcé ses activités afin de répondre à l'augmentation des besoins humanitaires. Depuis l'année dernière, l'ensemble des missions MSF au Nord-Kivu est confronté à d'importants défis liés aux ruptures de stocks de médicaments contre la tuberculose, le VIH et le paludisme, ainsi qu'à des pénuries d'intrants médicaux (cartouches GeneXpert, tests VIH et paludisme, etc.) et à une capacité limitée de réponse face à l'augmentation des cas de violences sexuelles, de malnutrition et d'épidémies. Le nombre élevé de déplacements de population complique également l'accès aux soins de santé. Les réductions de financement du Fonds mondial ainsi que le conflit en cours dans l'est de la RDC contribuent à ces perturbations.

En tant que **Responsable Analyse Médicale et Plaidoyer - Est de la RDC**, vous êtes responsable de l’analyse médicale et du développement des activités de plaidoyer liées à l’accès aux soins et aux services de santé dans l’est du pays. Placé(e) sous la supervision hiérarchique du Représentant Médical du BALI (Bureau administratif et de liaison intersectionnel de MSF) et en lien fonctionnel et technique avec les Conseillers en politiques de santé suivant la RDC, vous contribuez à l’identification, la documentation et l’analyse des principaux obstacles à l’accès aux soins ainsi qu'à l'élaboration des positionnements et messages de plaidoyer de MSF. Vous travaillez en étroite collaboration avec les équipes projets et les Coordinateurs Médicaux des différentes sections MSF présentes au Nord-Kivu afin de collecter et consolider les informations issues du terrain. Vous collaborez également avec le Responsable Plaidoyer VIH/TB basé à Kinshasa afin de relayer les enjeux identifiés dans l'Est auprès des autorités nationales, des bailleurs et des autres acteurs de santé concernés. En tant que membre de l'équipe de coordination, vous assurez le lien entre les réalités opérationnelles observées dans les projets et les initiatives de plaidoyer menées aux niveaux provincial, national et international.

**RESPONSABILITES PRINCIPALES**

**Analyse des obstacles à l'accès aux soins**

- Collecter, centraliser et analyser les informations relatives aux barrières d'accès aux services de santé, notamment dans les domaines du VIH, de la tuberculose, du paludisme, de la vaccination, de la nutrition et de la prise en charge des violences sexuelles. Produire des analyses permettant de mieux comprendre les défis rencontrés par les populations et d'orienter le positionnement de MSF

**Suivi des financements et cartographie des acteurs**

- Assurer une veille sur les financements des programmes de santé et sur les évolutions du paysage humanitaire et sanitaire. Analyser l'impact des financements sur la disponibilité des services de santé et maintenir une cartographie actualisée des acteurs intervenant dans les zones couvertes par MSF

**Consolidation et analyse des données issues des projets**

- Consolider les données et informations remontées par les projets MSF concernant les ruptures de stocks, les difficultés d'accès aux traitements et diagnostics, les tendances épidémiologiques, la malnutrition ou les violences sexuelles. Transformer ces informations en analyses permettant d'identifier les principales lacunes et risques pour les populations

**Suivi de la disponibilité des intrants médicaux**

- En collaboration avec les équipes pharmacie et supply, suivre la disponibilité des médicaments, tests diagnostiques et autres intrants de santé essentiels. Participer aux mécanismes de coordination concernés et contribuer à l'identification précoce des risques de rupture ou de difficultés d'approvisionnement pouvant affecter les activités médicales

**Développement et mise en œuvre du plaidoyer**

- Contribuer à l'élaboration et à la mise en œuvre des stratégies de plaidoyer de MSF en documentant les besoins, les insuffisances de réponse et les conséquences pour les populations. Participer à la rédaction de messages clés, notes de briefing, analyses et autres documents destinés aux autorités, bailleurs de fonds et partenaires

**Coordination et collaboration intersectionnelle**

- Travailler en étroite collaboration avec les équipes médicales, opérationnelles et de plaidoyer des différentes sections MSF intervenant au Nord-Kivu. Participer aux discussions internes visant à développer des analyses communes, harmoniser les positionnements de MSF et renforcer la cohérence des actions de plaidoyer aux niveaux provincial, national et international

**PREREQUIS**

**Education & Expérience**

- Diplôme universitaire en santé publique, politiques de santé, sciences de la santé, affaires humanitaires ou dans un domaine connexe. Une spécialisation en plaidoyer, sciences politiques ou communication constitue un atout
- Minimum 2 ans d’expérience internationale dans différents contextes humanitaires ou de santé publique est requis
- Expérience du secteur de la santé publique ainsi qu’une bonne compréhension des mécanismes de financement de la santé et du fonctionnement des systèmes de santé est un atout important
- Une expérience au sein de MSF ou d’une autre INGO médicale est indispensable
- Une expérience en plaidoyer auprès des autorités sanitaires, des bailleurs de fonds ou d’autres acteurs de la santé constitue un atout
- Un intérêt marqué pour la région ainsi que pour les enjeux humanitaires est attendu

**Compétences**

- Capacité à analyser et à synthétiser des données médicales, épidémiologiques et opérationnelles
- Capacité démontrée de représentation, du réseautage, et de négociations
- Forte sensibilité interculturelle et aptitude à travailler dans des environnements multiculturels
- Résistance au stress
- Travail d’équipe et coopération
- Agilité et diplomatie
- Excellente maîtrise du Pack Office 365 est obligatoire

**Langues**

- Très bonne maitrise orale et écrite du **Français**
- Bonne connaissance d’Anglais est un atout

**CONDITIONS**

- Date de début : **Dès que possible**
- Localisation : **Béni**, Est de la RDC
- Mobilité : **mobilité importante dans les projets et les coordinations**
- Type de contrat : Contrat à durée déterminée – Temps plein
- Durée du contrat : **9 mois** (prolongeable)
- Salaire selon la grille salariale internationale de MSF
- Les termes contractuels, les conditions et le salaire seront établis en fonction de la résidence officielle des candidats sélectionnés et dans le respect des grilles standard de fonction et de salaire de MSF
- **Pas de poste en famille ou couple**
- ***Adhésion aux valeurs managériales de l’organisation : Respect, Transparence, Responsabilisation, Intégrité, Confiance, Autonomisation***
- ***Adhésion aux engagements pour un comportement responsable***

**Date limite pour postuler : 15th of November 2026**

***Les femmes sont encouragées à postuler.***

jobs.title: Project Manager
jobs.description:
**OB DESCRIPTION**

**PROJECT**

Integrated Shelter, Food Security and Livelihoods Support for Safe, Dignified and Sustainable Return in Abul Thohur (Idleb) and Madiq Castle (Hama)

**DUTY STATION**

Idlib, Syria, with regular field visits to project locations

**ABOUT THE PROJECT**

IHH is implementing an integrated humanitarian and early-recovery project funded by the OCHA Syria Humanitarian Fund (SHF), supporting safe, dignified and sustainable return in Abul Thohur, Idleb Governorate, and Madiq Castle, Hama Governorate.

The project combines shelter rehabilitation, winterization and Core NFI assistance, cash assistance for food, bakery rehabilitation and subsidized bread provision, and agricultural and irrigation-related interventions. Through these complementary activities, the project aims to address urgent household needs, restore essential infrastructure and support agricultural livelihoods and community recovery.

**JOB SUMMARY**

IHH is seeking an experienced Project Manager to lead the overall planning, implementation, monitoring and closure of the project, ensuring that all activities are delivered effectively, on time, within the approved budget, and in compliance with IHH policies and OCHA SHF requirements.

The Project Manager will oversee the implementation of integrated Shelter/NFI and Food Security and Agriculture/Livelihoods (FSAL) activities, providing leadership to the project team and ensuring effective coordination between technical teams, support departments, local authorities, community representatives and relevant humanitarian stakeholders.

The role requires strong project management and organizational skills, sound financial oversight, and the ability to manage multidisciplinary teams and address operational challenges in the Syrian humanitarian context. The successful candidate will ensure that project activities achieve their intended results while maintaining high standards of programme quality, accountability, safeguarding and donor compliance.

**KEY RESPONSIBILITIES**

**Project Planning and Implementation**

**·** Lead the planning, implementation and closure of the project in accordance with the approved proposal, logical framework, work plan, budget and donor requirements.

**·** Develop and regularly update detailed implementation plans, activity schedules, procurement plans and resource requirements in coordination with relevant technical and support teams.

**·** Oversee the implementation of shelter, NFI, food security, agriculture and livelihoods activities, ensuring that project outputs, targets and milestones are achieved within the approved timeframe.

**·** Monitor progress against the approved work plan and indicators, identify implementation delays and operational challenges, and implement appropriate corrective measures.

**·** Ensure effective integration and complementarity between project components to maximize impact and avoid duplication of assistance.

**·** Conduct regular field visits to assess implementation progress, verify the quality of activities, engage with project teams and communities, and address implementation challenges.

**·** Ensure that project documentation, implementation records and supporting evidence are complete, accurate and maintained in accordance with organizational and donor requirements.

**Technical Oversight and Programme Quality**

**·** Coordinate with engineering staff to ensure the effective implementation of shelter rehabilitation activities, including household assessments, preparation and review of Bills of Quantities (BoQs), contractor supervision, quality assurance and verification of completed works.

**·** Oversee winterization and Core NFI assistance, ensuring transparent beneficiary selection, appropriate verification, clear communication of assistance modalities and coordination between SHF-funded and IHH-funded caseloads.

**·** Supervise the implementation of cash assistance for food, bakery rehabilitation and subsidized bread activities, ensuring compliance with approved targeting criteria, delivery arrangements and monitoring requirements.

**·** Coordinate with agriculture and field teams to support the effective implementation and monitoring of agricultural assistance, irrigation-related interventions and activities supporting farming livelihoods.

**·** Ensure that project activities comply with approved technical specifications, implementation procedures and relevant quality standards.

**·** Work closely with technical staff to identify implementation gaps, address quality concerns and ensure that interventions respond to identified household and community needs.

**·** Promote coordination across technical components to ensure consistent implementation and efficient use of project resources.

**Team Leadership and Coordination**

**·** Provide day-to-day management, supervision and guidance to project staff, ensuring clear responsibilities, effective communication and accountability for results.

**·** Coordinate closely with engineering, FSAL, finance, procurement, logistics, monitoring and other relevant teams to ensure timely and effective project delivery.

**·** Monitor staff performance, identify capacity-building needs and support professional development and continuous improvement.

**·** Maintain effective working relationships with local authorities, community representatives, contractors, service providers and relevant humanitarian actors.

**·** Represent IHH in relevant coordination meetings and external engagements related to the project, as delegated by senior management.

**·** Organize regular project review meetings to assess progress, discuss challenges, agree on corrective actions and follow up on outstanding issues.

**·** Ensure that field teams receive the guidance, information and resources required to perform their responsibilities effectively.

**Budget Management and Donor Compliance**

**·** Monitor project expenditure against the approved budget and implementation plan in coordination with the finance team.

**·** Review budget utilization, expenditure forecasts and financial progress, identifying variances and proposing corrective actions when required.

**·** Coordinate with finance, procurement and logistics teams to ensure that project expenditures, procurement processes, contracts and payments comply with IHH procedures and donor requirements.

**·** Ensure that project activities and expenditures remain within the approved scope and budget and that any proposed changes follow established authorization procedures.

**·** Monitor financial and operational risks, identify potential overspending or implementation bottlenecks, and take timely action to address them.

**·** Ensure that financial and programme documentation is accurate, complete and available for internal reviews, audits and donor verification.

**·** Escalate significant financial, contractual, operational or compliance issues to senior management in a timely manner.

**Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Reporting**

**·** Ensure systematic monitoring of project implementation against approved indicators, targets, milestones and means of verification.

**·** Coordinate with monitoring and evaluation staff to support data quality, activity monitoring, post-distribution monitoring and other required assessments.

**·** Ensure that beneficiary selection, registration and verification processes are transparent, properly documented and consistent with approved eligibility criteria.

**·** Oversee household-level de-duplication and the separate tracking of SHF-funded and IHH-funded assistance, where applicable.

**·** Ensure that feedback and complaints mechanisms are accessible to affected communities and that feedback is documented, referred and addressed through established procedures.

**·** Prepare, review and submit timely, accurate and evidence-based donor reports, internal progress updates and other required project documentation.

**·** Maintain effective project management systems and ensure that implementation records and indicator-tracking tools are regularly updated.

**·** Document implementation challenges, lessons learned and good practices, using monitoring findings to improve programme quality and inform management decisions.

**Coordination and Stakeholder Engagement**

**·** Maintain effective coordination with relevant local authorities, community representatives, service providers and other stakeholders in the targeted locations.

**·** Coordinate with relevant humanitarian coordination mechanisms and sector actors to promote complementarity, information sharing and alignment with identified needs.

**·** Facilitate communication between field teams, technical specialists and support departments to resolve implementation challenges.

**·** Support coordination with relevant stakeholders involved in shelter rehabilitation, food security, agricultural livelihoods, bakery operations and irrigation-related activities.

**·** Ensure that community engagement is conducted transparently and that beneficiaries receive clear information about project objectives, eligibility criteria, assistance modalities and feedback channels.

**Protection, Safeguarding and Risk Management**

**·** Ensure that protection mainstreaming, gender sensitivity, disability inclusion, accountability to affected populations and the principle of do no harm are integrated throughout project implementation.

**·** Work with the designated GBV Programme Focal Point to identify and mitigate potential gender-based violence risks associated with project activities.

**·** Ensure compliance with IHH safeguarding policies, prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEA), the organizational code of conduct and relevant reporting procedures.

**·** Promote safe, dignified and non-discriminatory access to project assistance, with particular attention to vulnerable and marginalized groups.

**·** Identify and monitor operational, security, access, financial, procurement and implementation risks, and develop appropriate mitigation measures.

**·** Ensure that safeguarding concerns, protection risks and other incidents are reported and referred through established organizational channels.

**·** Promote a culture of accountability, integrity, transparency and responsible use of humanitarian resources.

**REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS AND EXPERIENCE**

**·** Bachelor's degree in engineering, agriculture, economics, business administration, project management, international development or another relevant discipline. A master's degree is an advantage.

**·** At least five years of progressively responsible experience in similar positions within the humanitarian sector, including project planning, implementation, team management, budget monitoring and donor reporting.

**·** Demonstrated experience in at least one of the following sectors: Shelter and Non-Food Items (SNFI) or Food Security and Agriculture/Livelihoods (FSAL). Experience in both sectors is highly preferred.

**·** Proven experience managing donor-funded humanitarian projects and ensuring compliance with organizational policies, approved budgets and donor requirements.

**·** Experience in work planning, indicator tracking, financial monitoring, risk management and preparation of donor reports.

**·** Demonstrated ability to supervise multidisciplinary teams and coordinate effectively with technical and support departments.

**·** Experience working with local authorities, community representatives, contractors, service providers and humanitarian coordination mechanisms in Syria.

**·** Experience with OCHA or the Syria Humanitarian Fund (SHF) is highly desirable.

**·** Familiarity with shelter rehabilitation, cash-based assistance, food security, agricultural livelihoods or early-recovery programming is an advantage.

**·** Strong organizational, analytical, leadership, communication and problem-solving skills.

**·** Proficiency in Microsoft Office, particularly Excel and Word. Familiarity with project monitoring and digital data-collection tools is an advantage.

**·** Fluency in Arabic and excellent proficiency in English, both written and spoken, are essential. Knowledge of Turkish is an advantage.

**CORE COMPETENCIES**

**·** Project planning, implementation and results-based management.

**·** Team leadership, staff supervision and multidisciplinary coordination.

**·** Budget monitoring, financial accountability and donor compliance.

**·** Analytical thinking, risk management and problem-solving.

**·** Effective communication, negotiation and stakeholder engagement.

**·** Monitoring, reporting and evidence-based decision-making.

**·** Accountability, integrity, confidentiality and commitment to humanitarian principles.

**·** Adaptability and the ability to manage competing priorities in a complex operational environment.

**WORKING CONDITIONS**

The position will be based at the IHH Idlib Office, with regular field visits to Abul Thohur, Idleb Governorate, and Madiq Castle, Hama Governorate, as required by project implementation needs. The successful candidate must be able to coordinate effectively with field teams and travel to project locations when required.

jobs.title: GRANT MANAGER, Bangui, CAR.
jobs.description:
## The Role

**Job Title:** Grants Manager

**Location:** Bangui, Central African Republic

**Position Type:** International or national position

**Contract Type and Duration:** 12-month renewable fixed-term contract, subject to a probationary period.

**Reporting Line:** Regional Director

**Supervision:** The role has no line-management responsibilities but will work closely with Support Services and Programme teams.

**Salary and Leave:** 3200-3600EUR before tax. 33 days of annual leave to include all public and religious holidays

### Roles and Responsibilities:

Under the supervision of the designated Regional Director and in close collaboration with the Country Managers, Regional Head of MEAL, and Programme Development Manager, the Grants Manager will be responsible for the following key areas:

### Grants Management and Compliance

- Maintain oversight of donor contracts and grant agreements throughout the grant lifecycle.
- Develop and maintain a grants and compliance tracker; communicate obligations, responsibilities and deadlines; coordinate follow-up with Programme, Finance, MEAL and partner teams; maintain complete records; and escalate significant risks, gaps or delays to the appropriate managers.
- Coordinate grant requirements at project kick-off, review and closeout, ensuring that staff understand approved plans, budgets, deliverables, compliance obligations and deadlines.
- Support Project Managers to monitor implementation, prepare and track justified amendment requests, manage authorised donor communication, complete closeout requirements and document lessons for future programme design.
- Proactively identify potential donor compliance issues, and work with the team to develop appropriate and timely responses.

### Donor Reporting and Information Management

- Together with the Regional Head of MEAL, lead the donor reporting process, maintaining a clear reporting calendar and coordinating timely inputs from Programme, Finance, MEAL and other teams.
- Develop and maintain appropriate templates for reporting and other donor documentation requirements.
- Review narrative and financial reports for accuracy, consistency, evidence, compliance and alignment with approved plans and results frameworks; secure required approvals; follow up on gaps or delays; archive final submissions and supporting evidence; and guide colleagues on donor reporting standards.
- Establish and maintain an organised system for managing grant-related documentation throughout the grant lifecycle.
- Ensure that grant agreements, approved proposals, budgets, amendments, donor reports, correspondence, monitoring reports, evaluations, and closeout documents are properly filed and archived in designated organisational systems.
- Conduct periodic reviews of project files to verify the completeness, accuracy, and accessibility of grant documentation.
- Coordinate with Project Managers and relevant colleagues to ensure that project documentation is uploaded and maintained in accordance with organisational procedures.

### Communication, Donor Engagement, and Visibility

- Coordinate with Programme and Communications colleagues to identify achievements, results and lessons for donor briefings, success stories, case studies and other communication products.
- Ensure that all materials meet donor visibility requirements and Concordis standards for safeguarding, confidentiality and approval, and maintain an accessible record of key donor communications and products.

### Capacity Building and Internal Coordination

- Provide practical guidance to Project Managers and Programme, Finance and MEAL colleagues on grants management, donor compliance, proposal development and reporting.
- Promote consistent systems and standards across the regional programme, address implementation or capacity gaps, share good practice and lessons, and maintain effective coordination with Country Managers, the Regional Director and relevant UK colleagues.

### Safeguarding, Conduct and Confidentiality

- Comply with Concordis safeguarding, anti-fraud, anti-corruption, conflict-of-interest and code-of-conduct requirements.
- Maintain strict confidentiality regarding staff, financial, supplier and organisational information.
- Immediately report safeguarding, fraud, corruption, exploitation, abuse or other serious concerns through the appropriate reporting mechanisms.
- Ensure administrative and logistical arrangements support safe and dignified participation of staff and programme participants.

### Other Duties and Responsibilities

- Contribute to the continuous improvement of grants management systems, tools, and procedures to strengthen efficiency, accountability, transparency, and compliance across the regional programme.
- Support the Regional Director, Country Managers, and Programme Development Manager in other grant-related activities that contribute to effective programme implementation, resource mobilisation, and organisational development.
- Perform other duties reasonably assigned by the Line Manager that are consistent with the objectives and scope of the position.
- Ensure a comprehensive and timely handover of outstanding responsibilities, grant documentation, reporting deadlines, contractual obligations, and pending actions before the end of the assignment.

### Required Qualifications and Competencies

#### 1. Education and Qualifications

- Bachelor or Master’s degree in International Development, International Cooperation, Economics, Social Sciences, Project Management, or another relevant field.
- Additional professional training or certifications in grants management, project cycle management, fundraising, compliance, or donor reporting will be an advantage.
- Professional qualifications in accounting, finance, or related fields will be an asset.

#### 2. Professional Experience

- At least four (4) years of relevant professional experience in international cooperation, international development, humanitarian assistance, or peacebuilding programmes.
- At least three (3) years of demonstrated experience in grants management or a similar position.
- Proven experience independently coordinating proposal development, donor reporting, and grant compliance processes, including consolidating contributions from multiple stakeholders.
- Demonstrated experience working with institutional donors. Experience implementing European Union funded interventions is an advantage.
- Experience managing grants throughout the project cycle, including proposal development, contract management, reporting, grant amendments, compliance monitoring, and closeout.
- Experience preparing and reviewing narrative reports, financial reporting packages, proposals, budgets, and supporting documentation.
- Experience coordinating with Programme, Finance, Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL), and other support teams to ensure compliance with donor requirements.
- Previous experience working in conflict-affected, fragile, or complex operating environments will be an asset.

#### 3. Technical Competencies and Knowledge

- Strong knowledge of institutional donor regulations, contractual requirements, proposal development procedures, reporting standards, and compliance frameworks.
- Demonstrated ability to coordinate complex proposal development and donor reporting processes, ensuring quality, consistency, and timely submission.
- Good understanding of project cycle management, grant administration, budget monitoring, risk management, and donor compliance.
- Strong analytical, organisational, planning, and coordination skills, with attention to detail and the ability to manage multiple deadlines and competing priorities.
- Advanced practical knowledge of Microsoft Office applications, particularly Excel, Word, and Outlook, as well as online collaboration and document management tools such as SharePoint.
- Excellent writing, editing, reviewing, and information consolidation skills, particularly for donor proposals, narrative reports, and institutional communications.
- Ability to work independently while coordinating effectively with multidisciplinary and geographically dispersed teams.

#### 4. Languages

- **English:** Fluency in written and spoken English, with excellent report-writing, editing, and communication skills.
- **French:** Fluency in written and spoken French, with excellent report-writing, editing, and communication skills.

#### 5. Key Stakeholders

#### Internal Stakeholders

- Regional Director.
- Country Managers.
- Programme Development Manager.
- Project Managers and Programme teams across Cameroon, Chad, CAR, and Darfur in Sudan.
- Finance and Support Services teams.
- Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL) team.
- Communications teams.
- UK Team

#### External Stakeholders

- Institutional donors, including the European Union (EU) and other current or potential funding partners.
- Implementing partners and local organisations.
- External auditors and other relevant compliance or verification bodies.
- Other relevant stakeholders involved in programme implementation, donor coordination, and resource mobilisation.

jobs.description:
**Background:**

The International Rescue Committee (IRC) responds to the world's worst humanitarian crises and helps people to survive, recover, and gain control of their future.

We aim to make our programs a model for the highest global standards and to cultivate power and lasting change not just for our clients but for all people affected by humanitarian crises. To achieve that vision, the IRC’s Technical Excellence (TE) group, located within the Crisis Response, Recovery and Development (CRRD) Department, provides technical assistance to IRC’s country program staff and shares what we learn to influence policy and practice.

**Location:** This position is open to national candidates or candidates who have residency in either the U.S or UK.

**Internal Candidates:** Internal.staff from any other country that has an IRC Office, are welcome to apply and will be hosted in that country as a national staff if selected for the position.

**Languages:** Fluency in written & spoken English required. Fluency in Spanish, French, or Arabic a plus.

**Monitoring, Evaluation, Technology, Accountability, and Learning at the IRC**

The METAL Unit is responsible for supporting CRRD to have a culture of strong data and evidence use through stewardship of the Data & Performance Ecosystem, and for coordinating successful piloting and uptake of innovative technology solutions. The METAL Unit provides specialized support across four pillars to strengthen program effectiveness, improve decision-making, and enhance organizational learning:

- Global MEAL Practice: Global MEAL Practice works with the Technical Units to set and maintain the highest standards for measurement, analysis, and data use, promoting a culture of continuous improvement and learning.
- Technology for Programs: The T4Ppillar drives the identification and testing of cutting-edge technology for IRC’s programming areas, by focusing on advancing digital solutions that enhance program reach and impact. Leads T4P innovation and scaling for CRRD and coordinates between CRRD/IT/Signpost/Airbel.
- Data Systems and Analytics: The Data Systems and Analytics pillar ensures the widespread iteration, adoption, and sustainability of data systems, leading data governance for CRRD and coordinating between IT/others at an org level.
- Regional METAL Support: The Regional METAL Support team provides direct technical assistance to IRC Programs, ensuring programs meet MEAL maturity benchmarks and optimize data utilization. They also provide strategic support implementing and generating learning from MEAL systems and activities, providing regional leadership with data insights and informing global practice.

**Job Overview**

The Operations Manager, METAL provides dedicated administrative, knowledge management, and coordination support to METAL Unit leadership and the wider team. This role keeps the Unit organized to support uptake of key initiatives – maintaining shared knowledge products and resources, supporting meeting and event logistics, and supporting communications across all four pillars. The ideal candidate is highly organized, detail-oriented, and motivated by driving organizational change through strong communications and effective team operations.

**Major Responsibilities**

*Administrative and team support*

- Provide day-to-day administrative support to METAL pillar leads and the wider Unit, including invoice management.
- Plan and organize the Unit's team retreat, including venue research and booking, agenda coordination with pillar leads, travel logistics, budget tracking, and on-site/virtual materials
- Coordinate unit-wide meetings (e.g. all-staff calls, SMT meetings, pillar check-ins): scheduling, agenda preparation, notetaking, and follow-up on action items
- Support logistical planning of METAL-related events, workshops, and trainings
- Support onboarding logistics for new METAL Unit hires, including scheduling introductory meetings with pillar leads and colleagues, ensuring new hires have information and system access (i.e. Integra, Claude, WorkDay, etc.), and training staff on required systems

*Knowledge management*

- Collect, organize, and maintain knowledge products developed across the four METAL pillars (standards, guidance, templates, tools) in a well-organized, easy-to-navigate central repository
- Manage and maintain the Unit's Box folder structure, ensuring consistent naming conventions, version control, and appropriate access for all team members
- Maintain and update METAL's RescueNet pages and resource libraries on an ongoing basis, ensuring content stays current and easy to find in service to TechEx and CRRD at large
- Act as the Unit's knowledge management focal point, liaising with IT and other platform owners on folder structure, taxonomy, and content organization
- Maintain shared trackers and issue logs used by the Unit, ensuring they remain current and accessible to relevant stakeholders
- Maintain the organizational chart and keep a staff roster list (with TTA tracking) and sharing information with TechEx FinOps team

*Communications support*

- Support internal communications for the Unit: update shared trackers, standard presentations, and resource pages with current information
- Support department-wide communications for the Unit: gathering inputs for the CRRD newsletter,
- Maintain METAL distribution email list

*Other*

- Provide additional administrative and coordination support to METAL Unit leadership as needed
- Support in data inputs, data clean up, or data analyses as per request of TechEx
- Other duties as requested

**Key Working Relationships**

Position Reports to: Senior Director, METAL

This position works closely with the leads and teams of all four METAL pillars (MEAL Global Practice, Regional METAL Support, Technology for Programs, and CRRD Data & Analytics), as well as IT and other platform administrators, as needed.

**Job Requirements**

*Essential*

- Bachelor's degree, or equivalent combination of education and experience (e.g. in library science, information/knowledge management, or business administration)
- Minimum 2–4 years of experience in an administrative, knowledge management, or team coordination role; experience in a nonprofit or international development context a plus
- Experience planning and coordinating meetings, workshops, or team events, including logistics, scheduling, and materials preparation
- Proficiency with Microsoft 365 tools (SharePoint, Teams, Outlook, Excel) and file management/storage platforms (e.g. Box)
- Exceptionally well-organized, with strong attention to detail and a proven track record of managing multiple priorities and deadlines
- Strong written and verbal communication skills; able to produce clear, user-friendly documentation and reference materials
- Strong interpersonal skills, with a collegial, service-oriented approach to supporting colleagues and leadership across a distributed team
- Excellent spoken and written English

*Desirable*

- Experience with SharePoint site administration, document taxonomy, or metadata management
- Working knowledge of Arabic, French, and/or Spanish
- Experience supporting humanitarian or international development program teams

***This is a remote position open to internal candidates based in countries where IRC operates who have the right to work in their location. Successful candidates will be hired on a local employment contract and according to local salary scale.***

***This role is open to candidates located and with the right to work in United Kingdom and United States of America.***

**Compensation:** (UK Pay Rate: £41,767 - 49,599/yr; US Pay Rate: $73,000 - $85,000/yr). Ranges are based on various factors including the labor market, job type, internal equity, and budget. Exact offers are calibrated by work location, individual candidate experience and skills relative to the defined job requirements.

**Equal Opportunity Employer:** IRC is an Equal Opportunity Employer. IRC considers all applicants on the basis of merit without regard to race, sex, color, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, disability or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

**Professional Standards:** All International Rescue Committee workers must adhere to the core values and principles outlined in IRC Way - Standards for Professional Conduct. Our Standards are Integrity, Service, Equality and Accountability. In accordance with these values, the IRC operates and enforces policies on Safeguarding, Conflicts of Interest, Fiscal Integrity, and Reporting Wrongdoing and Protection from Retaliation. IRC is committed to take all necessary preventive measures and create an environment where people feel safe, and to take all necessary actions and corrective measures when harm occurs. IRC builds teams of professionals who promote critical reflection, power sharing, debate, and objectivity to deliver the best possible services to our clients.

**US Benefits:** We offer a comprehensive and highly competitive set of benefits. In the US, these include: 10 sick days, 10 US holidays, 20-25 paid time off days depending on role and tenure, medical insurance starting at $163 per month, dental starting at $6.50 per month, and vision starting at $5 per month, FSA for healthcare and commuter costs, a 403b retirement savings plans with immediately vested matching, disability & life insurance, and an Employee Assistance Program which is available to our staff and their families to support counseling and care in times of crisis and mental health struggles.

jobs.title: Medical coordinator (F/M) - Sudan
jobs.description:
For more than 40 years, Médecins du Monde (MdM), a campaigning medical organisation committed to international solidarity, has been caring for the most vulnerable populations here and abroad. It has continued to bear witness to obstacles that exist in accessing healthcare and has secured sustainable improvements in health-for-all policies.

Those working for this independent organisation do not solely dispense care and treatment but condemn violations of human dignity and rights and fight to improve matters for populations living in precarious situations.

MdM France currently works in 30 countries across all continents to facilitate access to healthcare through 6 political battles:

- Sexual and Reproductive Health Rights
- Migration, Exile, Human Rights and Health
- Harm Reduction
- Environment and Health
- Humanitarian Space
- Healthcare systems and rights

**MdM in Sudan**

MdM maintained a presence in Jebel Marra until 2011. Mid-December 2025, MdM decided to launch an exploratory mission in West Darfur and allocated core funds to provide medicines, recruit an exploratory team composed of a head of mission, a medical coordinator and a logistics coordinator, and start activities in Darfur.

Since end of April 2026, MdM is managing a clinic in the Dar Omo camp in Feina (South Darfur) hosting approximately 25.000 displaced persons.

Since August 2026, 2 mobile clinics are operating around Feina and mid-September 2026, MdM has launched a response to a cholera outbreak in North Darfur.

MdM France has decided to register itself and consolidate its presence in East Sudan to have a balanced presence in all Sudan and be able to answer humanitarian needs in this part of the country.

**About the role**

You are in charge of designing, planning, implementing, adapting and monitoring health activities. You directly manage the medical team.

**What you’ll do**

- Participate in the definition of the country strategy led by the general coordinator and drive the medical and technical aspects in the development of this strategy
- Design, plan, implement, adapt and monitor the programme’s health activities
- Ensure the quality and relevance of health activities, supervise the collection and analysis of medical data
- Recruit, manage, train, and motivate the medical team
- Ensure the management of pharmaceutical products
- Carry out health needs assessments and evaluations of medical partners
- Monitor, analyse and share health and epidemiological data and assess needs and contribute to medical response planning and emergency preparedness for epidemics and mass displacement
- Cooperate with the administration team regarding budgeting and supervise the medical purchase process
- Represent MdM with authorities, partners and other NGOs on health issues
- Participate in the writing of proposals and reports

**Who you’ll work with**

You work under the supervision of the general coordinator of the mission (based in El Geneina) and in collaboration with the health advisor, the MHPSS advisor and the pharmacy officer based at HQ. You manage directly the activity manager and the pharmacy officer. In Feina, the medical team is composed of a medical team supervisor and a midwife supervisor.

**You are the right match if you:**

- Have a medical degree (medical doctor, nurse, midwife)
- Have a minimum 4 years of experience in the humanitarian sector in a similar position
- Have experience in emergency responses, outbreak management, nutrition, health assessments and medical programme start-up
- Demonstrate experience working in complex, politically sensitive or rapidly evolving environments
- Are able to work in high security context
- Have solid background in team leadership, capacity building and technical supervision
- Have strong communication, negotiation and diplomacy skills
- Have strong ability to work collaboratively with diverse teams and multicultural stakeholders
- Have excellent organisational and time-management skills
- Have mapping skills with Google Earth or ArcGIS
- Have strong proficiency in Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint)
- Are fluent in English (spoken and written); knowledge of Arabic is an asset

**This role may not suit you if you:**

- Are not aligned with MdM’s values
- Don't have experience in volatile security environments

**Recruitment process**

If shortlisted, you will first meet with our HR team. Technical and managerial interviews, which may include practical case studies, will follow.

Please note: as part of our anti–money laundering and counter-terrorism policy, international background checks may be conducted. Data is processed confidentially and securely. More info: [https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/](https://www.medecinsdumonde.org/en/working-internationally/)
All successful candidates must provide a criminal record extract (B3).

**Ready to apply?**

We only need your CV and a cover letter.
If this role sounds like the right fit for you, apply now – we’d love to hear from you!

**Employment conditions**

Contract & status:

- Gross monthly salary: 3 663 €
- Fixed-term contract starting as soon as possible and for 6 months
- Single posting

Work environment:

- Position based in El Geneina , West Darfur, with regular field visits

Benefits:

- 13th month salary (paid in 2 installments after 6 months of service)
- Expatriation allowance: 10% of gross monthly salary
- Coverage of travel (home – mission), visas, and vaccinations
- Guesthouse
- Health insurance (50% covered by MdM and 50% by the employee)
- Repatriation insurance
- MdM promotes training and internal mobility

Essentials:

- 5 weeks paid leave + 22.5 RTT days per year
- Strong commitment to inclusion and fighting all forms of discrimination
- More info: [https://www.medecinsdumondeh.org/en/working-internationally/](https://www.medecinsdumondeh.org/en/working-internationally/)

**Our commitment to diversity and inclusion**

MdM is committed to the inclusion of people with disabilities and to fighting all forms of discrimination.
If you are officially recognized as a person with a disability and/or require workplace accommodations, please let us know

jobs.title: MERL Assistant
jobs.description:
**Aperçu de l'organisation**

Tostan is a 501(c)(3) nonprofit organization headquartered in Dakar, Senegal, and currently operating in five West African countries. Strategically, the organization is committed to further developing its core competency—education-based empowerment—and to documenting and scaling up the sustainable impact it creates across a range of issues. Tostan’s flagship model, the three-year Community Capacity-Building Program (CCBP), has already reached thousands of communities in West and East Africa since 1991. Results in the areas of governance, education, health, economic empowerment, and the environment are currently being tracked, and Tostan is particularly proud to have played a significant role in the large-scale empowerment of women and girls and in the community’s abandonment of harmful practices such as female genital mutilation and child marriage. As part of its plan d'engagement stratégique 2023-2030, Tostan is focusing on strategic scaling. The organization is developing new implementation strategies to support community leadership by driving systemic change on a larger scale at the regional level. It is also creating new models to share and replicate its programs with other development partners and is expanding its capacity to share Tostan’s comprehensive approach to support and influence a range of local and global audiences. For more information, please visit: [www.tostan.org](http://www.tostan.org)

**Department overview**

The Monitoring, Evaluation, Research, and Learning (MERL) team is an integral part of Tostan’s Program Department. Its mission is to coordinate and support the program monitoring and evaluation system in the countries where Tostan operates, as well as research and learning. Through this team, Tostan continuously monitors performance in partner communities and conducts internal evaluations, including baseline studies, midterm evaluations, and final evaluations.

**Roles and responsabilities**

Under the direct technical supervision of the MERL Focal Person and the TI MERL team, and the administrative supervision of the National Coordinator, the MERL Assistant will be responsible for supporting the MERL Country Responsible in ensuring the strict implementation of all monitoring and evaluation activities within the national coordination office.

***She/He will have as mission to :***

➔ Support the MERL Focal Person in supporting and coordinating the monitoring and evaluation strategies and activities implemented by SERA at the national coordination level

➔ Support the ERL Focal Person in overseeing the monitoring forms

jobs.title: Engineering and Shelter Team leader
jobs.description:
DRC Uganda is currently looking for a highly qualified and motivated individual to join our dynamic team as an Engineering and Shelter Team Leader.

**The overall purpose of the role:**

The Engineering and Shelter Team Leader will be responsible for providing overall technical leadership and oversight for shelter and infrastructure activities across Bidibidi, Rhino Camp and Imvepi refugee settlements. He/she will oversee cash-for-shelter assistance, renovation and construction works, ensuring quality and compliance with required technical standards. The position holder will also supervise Engineering Assistants and work closely with programme teams, Supply Chain, contractors and relevant stakeholders to ensure timely and effective implementation of shelter activities.

**Please note that this position is contingent upon confirmation of funding.**

**Your main duties and responsibilities will be:**

**Technical leadership and programme implementation**

- Provide overall technical leadership and oversight for shelter, renovation and construction activities across Bidibidi, Rhino Camp and Imvepi.
- Lead planning and implementation of shelter activities and ensure that agreed targets, timelines and technical standards are achieved.
- Review and approve technical assessments, Bill of Quantities (BOQs), cost estimates, specifications and other technical documentation prepared by Engineering Assistants before implementation.
- Provide technical guidance on appropriate shelter repair solutions, materials, designs and construction approaches, ensuring value for money, safety and suitability to the operational context.
- Ensure shelter and infrastructure interventions comply with approved project designs, organizational procedures and applicable humanitarian and technical standards.
- Ensure timely technical verification and documentation of completed household shelter repairs and follow-up of identified quality or safety concerns.
- Work closely with Protection, Cash and MEAL teams to ensure effective referral, assessment, monitoring and accountability throughout the cash-for-shelter assistance cycle.

**Renovation, construction and contractor management**

- Lead technical assessments and development/review of BOQs, drawings, specifications and cost estimates for project-supported renovation and construction works.
- Work closely with Supply Chain during procurement processes, including providing technical input into solicitation documents, technical evaluation of bids and clarification of technical requirements.
- Coordinate and monitor contractors during implementation to ensure compliance with approved BOQs, specifications, work plans, timelines and contractual requirements.
- Review progress and completed works and provide technical verification/certification to support acceptance and payment processes in accordance with organizational procedures.
- Identify construction defects, delays, variations and other technical risks and ensure appropriate corrective measures are agreed upon and followed through.

**Budget and resource management**

- Monitor expenditure against planned shelter activities and provide timely input into budget forecasts, spending plans and Budget Versus Actual (BVA) reviews.
- Track planned procurements, works and cash-for-shelter requirements to identify potential underspending, overspending or implementation delays and recommend corrective actions.
- Ensure BOQs and cost estimates are realistic, technically justified and provide value for money.
- Work closely with Finance, Supply Chain and the Project Manager to ensure timely procurement and utilization of resources required for shelter activities.

**Team management and capacity building**

- Provide day-to-day supervision and technical guidance to Engineering Assistants, including allocation of tasks, review of deliverables and monitoring of performance.
- Conduct regular field monitoring and provide coaching, mentoring and technical support to team members.
- Identify capacity-building needs and facilitate technical orientation and on-the-job training for shelter staff and other relevant project personnel.
- Promote effective teamwork, accountability and communication within the shelter team and with other programme and support departments.

**Coordination and stakeholder engagement**

- Represent the project on shelter and infrastructure matters in relevant coordination meetings, technical working groups and engagements as delegated by the Project Manager.
- Maintain effective working relationships with the Office of the Prime Minister (OPM), United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), district/local government authorities, settlement leadership, communities, implementing partners and other relevant stakeholders.
- Coordinate closely with community structures and assisted households to promote participation, accountability and ownership throughout implementation.
- Liaise with contractors, suppliers and relevant technical stakeholders to address implementation challenges and ensure timely delivery of works.
- Ensure effective internal coordination with Protection, Cash, MEAL, Finance and Supply Chain teams.

**About you**

To be successful in this role, you must have a minimum of 5 years of relevant professional experience in civil/building engineering, shelter, construction or infrastructure programming, preferably within humanitarian or development contexts. Moreover, we also expect the following.

**Required**

- Bachelor's degree in civil engineering, Building Engineering, Construction Management or another relevant engineering field.
- Experience in using design software like AutoCAD, ArchiCAD, Revit, QGIS software etc.
- Demonstrated experience in supervising construction, renovation and/or shelter programmes, including preparation and review of BOQs, drawings, specifications and cost estimates.
- Strong understanding of construction quality assurance, site supervision, occupational safety, and relevant engineering standards
- Experience working with refugees and host communities.
- Ability to ride a motorcycle with valid class “A” permit

**Desirable**

- A relevant postgraduate degree in Civil Engineering, Building Engineering, Construction Management or another relevant engineering field.
- Knowledge of one or more languages commonly spoken in the operational areas.
- Experience with cash-based shelter programming or household-level shelter repair assistance

In this position, you are expected to demonstrate DRC’s five core competencies:

**Striving for excellence:** You focus on reaching results while ensuring an efficient process.

**Collaborating:** You involve relevant parties and encourage feedback.

**Taking the lead:** You take ownership and initiative while aiming for innovation.

**Communicating:** You listen and speak effectively and honestly.

**Demonstrating integrity:** You uphold and promote the highest standards of ethical and professional conduct in relation to our values and Code of Conduct, including safeguarding against sexual exploitation, abuse and harassment.

**We offer**

- Contract length: 10 months
- Band: MG 2
- Designation of Duty Station: Bidibidi
- Start date: November 2026

Salary and conditions will be in accordance with Danish Refugee Council’s Terms of Employment for national employees; please refer to [our website](https://drc.ngo/about-drc/vacancies).

jobs.title: Case Manager Bangladesh
jobs.description:
**Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) is an international, independent medical humanitarian organization. As a non-profit, self-governed movement of over 63,000 dedicated professionals, we provide life-saving medical assistance to people affected by armed conflict, natural disasters, disease outbreaks, and exclusion from healthcare.**

**Our work is guided by medical ethics and the principles of impartiality, independence, and neutrality. We act based on need, and when we witness injustice, we speak out. Our commitment to professionalism and humanity can mean the difference between life and death.**

**People are our priority. At Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF)/ Artsen zonder Grenzen, we are committed to an inclusive culture that encourages and supports the diverse voices of our employees. We encourage diverse applicants including individuals of all gender identities, ages, sexual orientations, nationalities, ethnic background, religions, beliefs, social and marital status, people with different abilities and all other diversity characteristics and how they intersect together.**

With immediate effect, for our Country Programme in Bangladesh we are looking for:

## **Case Manager Bangladesh**

*(12 month assignment based in Bangladesh. This role is not based in Amsterdam)*

**Objectives of the position**

Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) OCA is seeking an experienced Safeguarding and Code of Conduct (CoC) Case Manager for the Kutupalong Project in Bangladesh. The role will support safeguarding initiatives and case management related to staff, patients, and communities in a context serving more than 1.1 million Rohingya refugees.

Reporting directly to the Project Coordinator and functionally to the Hospital Director in Bangladesh with technical support from the Safeguarding Case Management Advisor, the Case Manager will lead administrative investigations into misconduct, Coc violations, and safeguarding concerns, including complex and high-risk cases. The post holder will receive, triage, and manage subsequent complaint and investigation processes, ensure confidential case management and documentation, and serve as the primary focal point for patient and community safeguarding concerns in Kutupalong Hospital and other outreach facilities.

This position plays a key role in strengthening accountability, protecting vulnerable populations, and upholding MSF's safeguarding standards and ethical principles.

**Main responsibilities**

- Ensure proper handling of all misconduct complaints, including safe and confidential reception, timely acknowledgment, triage, and immediate reporting of high-risk allegations to the Safeguarding Unit and compliance with Intersectional Platform on Behaviour Standards for Case Management.
- Provide technical advice and support to all actors involved in case management and ensure risk-mitigation and referral measures for complainants. - subjects of complaints and witnesses, including protection, medical, psychosocial and legal referrals when appropriate.
- Conduct and lead case triage, risk assessments, and investigations, including evidence gathering, interviews, analysis, and recommendations.
- Manage investigation documentation, including archiving, minute-taking, coordination of meetings/interviews, and preparation of final reports.
- Build capacity of country programme teams by training and supporting staff involved in complaint handling and misconduct investigations.
- Propose improvements to protocols and guidelines on case management based on country programme realities.
- Ensure quality, confidentiality, and data protection in case management processes, including managing complaint databases and reporting statistics.
- Coordinate internal and external collaboration, maintain communication with the Safeguarding Unit, engage in relevant forums, and coordinate external investigation experts where necessary.

**Candidate Profile**

- BSc in law, social or organizational sciences, gender studies, social work, behavioural sciences, human rights, psychology, nursing or related field that deals with interpersonal behaviour and administrative fact-findings.
- Minimum 2 years of experience in identifying and addressing safeguarding concerns in a humanitarian setting, preferably a hospital setting with MSF or similar INGO. The 2 years of experience must include addressing concerns hands-on such as directly managing complaints, managing projects and staff, or treating patients.
- Experience working in low-resource contexts in countries of operation in the humanitarian, health, or development sector is highly desired.
- Strong analytical and advisory skills, with the ability to handle complex, sensitive, and high-risk cases independently.
- Excellent verbal communication skills, including the ability to deliver difficult information sensitively and appropriately.
- Excellent written communication skills, including the ability to draft investigation reports and present cases to senior management succinctly.
- Excellent intercultural communication skills, including the ability to work with qualified translators.
- Demonstrated commitment to confidentiality, survivor-centred practice, and fair process.
- Fluency in English, both speaking and writing, is mandatory. Bangla or Rohingya desirable.
- Ability to develop case strategies, conduct investigative interviews and deliver investigation reports of high quality and within prescribed deadlines.
- Certification as investigator highly desirable (CHS Tier 3, CFE/ CFF/ CPA/CCEP or equivalent)

**What we offer**

- Annual gross salary range: 33,500€ - 36,850€ depending on prior relevant experience. This is a level 15 of the new Program Function Grid.
- 25 annual holidays.
- Private Health Insurance for the duration of the assignment + 3 months post-assignment.
- Accommodation & utilities.
- Travel costs are covered, except for personal holidays.
- An international and multicultural work environment

jobs.description:
**Org. Setting and Reporting**

This position is located in the Financing and Outreach Division (FOD) of the Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA). OCHA's mission is to mobilize and coordinate effective and principled humanitarian action in partnership with national and international actors in order to alleviate human suffering in disasters and emergencies; advocate the rights of people in need; promote preparedness and prevention and facilitate sustainable solutions. The Financing and Outreach Division (FOD) leads in mobilizing and allocating resources for a coordinated and principled humanitarian response, while driving innovative humanitarian financing approaches and elevating the visibility and communication of OCHA’s mission and mandate. Within FOD, The Chief of Service, Communications is responsible for developing, implementing and evaluating communications strategies and services aligned with organizational objectives and priorities. The role includes providing vision, direction, support and implementation of the main functions of communications.. This position-specific job opening is advertised for the position of Chief of Communications in New York at UNHQ. The incumbent reports directly to the Director of the Financing and Outreach Division (FOD).

**Responsibilities**

Within delegated authority, the Chief of Communications will be responsible for the following duties: • Lead and strategically guide the activities of the communication sections and units to ensure strategic alignment and effective delivery of the organization’s objectives. • Provide the vision and leadership to develop and implement the communications strategy to strengthen understanding of organizational objectives, activities and impact, drive engagement, and build support with target audiences. • Guide and manage different communications workstreams bringing them together under shared objectives, such as digital communications, media relations, outreach, campaigns, and partnerships. Convene and coordinate with other UN entities and partners, as appropriate. • Chair and lead the Inter-Agency Standing Committee communications group, alongside an IASC member on a rotating basis. • Work to review OCHA's global communications workforce and identify how best to make it fit for purpose. • Advise senior management on strategic communications, crisis communications and reputational risk. • Oversee and lead the implementation of strategic communications policy, guidance and training for staff. • Advise and oversee internal communications, as appropriate, including messaging and content creation, and in crisis situations. • Lead and coordinate the creation of content, such as narratives and key messages, including on complex, sensitive, and crisis-driven issues. • Oversee the management and coordination of communications teams in the entity, including hiring, budgeting, reporting, recruitment, and training, in compliance with UN rules and regulations. • Provide guidance to team members to promote professional development and a positive team culture. • Oversee monitoring and analysis of communications strategies, approaches, and activities to assess performance and impact. • Maintain confidentiality and integrity in information management, and handle sensitive information with discretion, ensuring compliance with the UN data privacy, policies, security requirements, and standards. • Provide vision, targets and strategy for developing and delivering impactful offline and online campaigns through appropriate channels. • Lead collaboration with internal and external stakeholders to develop and deliver joint outreach and advocacy activities and campaigns to target key audiences and advance UN priorities. • Lead the development of engagement strategies to build and enhance the Organization's brand utilizing collaborations, partnerships and existing and emerging channels and content, as appropriate. • Oversee and guide the monitoring of media and developing events to identify emerging crises and reputational risks and provide early response warning and strategic advice to senior management. • Lead and oversee the Organization's proactive interaction with local, regional and international media and partners, promote outreach activities, and implement crisis communication responses and interactions with the media. • Oversee policy development and implementation to strengthen information integrity, and the coordination of efforts to address related threats at the regional and country levels, ensuring alignment with UN global priorities • Oversee efforts to strengthen information integrity, including research, risk and response work, coalition building and policy development. • Promote organizational understanding and adoption of technology, data, and innovation initiatives by leading communications related to digital transformation, enterprise platforms, cybersecurity, information governance, and business intelligence, ensuring alignment with organizational standards, policies, and strategic priorities.

**Competencies**

Professionalism: Knowledge of the substantive field of work in general and of specific areas being supervised. Skills to communicate complex and technical matters to diverse audiences. Exhibits strategic thinking and critical thinking skills. Knowledge of risks to information integrity - misinformation, disinformation, hate speech, and threats in fragile, post conflict, and crisis environments. Ability to build and maintain partnerships. Shows pride in work and in achievements; demonstrates professional competence and mastery of subject matter; is conscientious and efficient in meeting commitments, observing deadlines and achieving results; is motivated by professional rather than personal concerns; shows persistence when faced with difficult problems or challenges; remains calm in stressful situations. Client Orientation: Considers all those to whom services are provided to be “clients” and seeks to see things from clients’ point of view; Establishes and maintains productive partnerships with clients by gaining their trust and respect; Identifies clients’ needs and matches them to appropriate solutions; Monitors ongoing developments inside and outside the clients’ environment to keep; informed and anticipate problems; Keeps clients informed of progress or setbacks in projects; Meets timeline for delivery of products or services to client. Creativity: Actively seeks to improve programmes or services; Offers new and different options to solve problems or meet client needs;Promotes and persuades others to consider new ideas;Takes calculated risks on new and unusual ideas; thinks "outside the box"; Takes an interest in new ideas and new ways of doing things; Is not bound by current thinking or traditional approaches. Managerial Competencies: Leadership: Serves as a role model that other people want to follow; Empowers others to translate vision into results; Is proactive in developing strategies to accomplish objectives; Establishes and maintains relationships with a broad range of people to understand needs and gain support; Anticipates and resolves conflicts by pursuing mutually agreeable solutions; Drives for change and improvement; does not accept the status quo; Shows the courage to take unpopular stands; Provides leadership and takes responsibility for incorporating gender perspectives and ensuring the equal participation of women and men in all areas. Demonstrates knowledge of strategies and commitment to the goal of gender balance in staffing. Managing Performance: Delegates the appropriate responsibility, accountability and decision-making authority; Makes sure that roles, responsibilities and reporting lines are clear to each staff member; Accurately judges the amount of time and resources needed to accomplish a task and matches task to skills; Monitors progress against milestones and deadlines;Regularly discusses performance and provides feedback and coaching to staff; Encourages risk-taking and supports creativity and initiative; Actively supports the development and career aspirations of staff; Appraises performance fairly.

**Education**

Advanced university degree (Master’s degree or equivalent) in communications, journalism, international relations, digital communications or related field. A first-level university degree in combination with two additional years of qualifying experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree.

**Job - Specific Qualification**

Not available.

**Work Experience**

A minimum of fifteen (15) years of progressively responsible experience in communications, international relations, or other relevant areas is required. Knowledge of current and emerging digital media platforms, their principles and technologies is required. Knowledge of strategic communications principles and practices is required. Skills to lead teams, guide and mentor staff, and oversee their work to ensure successful completion of projects is required. A minimum of three (3) years of experience in crisis communication in a humanitarian, development or peacekeeping setting is desirable. Ability to identify trends and provide insights, to develop and implement communications strategies and to draft and tailor clear messages for diverse audiences is desirable. Skills to communicate complex and technical matters to diverse audiences is desirable.

**Languages**

English and French are the working languages of the United Nations Secretariat. For this job opening, English is required. Either French **or** Arabic is desirable. The table below shows the minimum required level for each skill in these languages, according to the UN Language Framework (please consult [https://languages.un.org](https://languages.un.org/) for details).

Staff members are subject to the authority of the Secretary-general and to assignment by him or her. In this context, all staff are expected to move periodically to new functions in their careers by established rules and procedures. Staff members of the United Nations Secretariat must fulfill the lateral or geographical move requirements to be eligible to apply for this vacancy. Staff members are requested to indicate all qualifying lateral or geographical moves in their Candidate Profile (CP) and motivation statement. At the United Nations, the paramount consideration in the recruitment and employment of staff is the necessity of securing the highest standards of efficiency, competence and integrity, with due regard to geographic diversity. All employment decisions are made on the basis of qualifications and organizational needs. The United Nations is committed to creating a diverse and inclusive environment of mutual respect. The United Nations recruits and employs staff regardless of gender identity, sexual orientation, race, religious, cultural and ethnic backgrounds or disabilities. The United Nations Secretariat is committed to achieving a 50/50 gender balance in its staff. Female candidates are strongly encouraged to apply for this position. An impeccable record of integrity and professional ethical standards is essential.

**United Nations Considerations**

According to article 101, paragraph 3, of the Charter of the United Nations, the paramount consideration in the employment of the staff is the necessity of securing the highest standards of efficiency, competence, and integrity. Candidates will not be considered for employment with the United Nations if they have committed violations of international human rights law, violations of international humanitarian law, sexual exploitation, sexual abuse, or sexual harassment, or if there are reasonable grounds to believe that they have been involved in the commission of any of these acts. The term “sexual exploitation” means any actual or attempted abuse of a position of vulnerability, differential power, or trust, for sexual purposes, including, but not limited to, profiting monetarily, socially or politically from the sexual exploitation of another. The term “sexual abuse” means the actual or threatened physical intrusion of a sexual nature, whether by force or under unequal or coercive conditions. The term “sexual harassment” means any unwelcome conduct of a sexual nature that might reasonably be expected or be perceived to cause offence or humiliation, when such conduct interferes with work, is made a condition of employment or creates an intimidating, hostile or offensive work environment, and when the gravity of the conduct warrants the termination of the perpetrator’s working relationship. Further, staff members in the Professional and higher category up to and including the D-2 level and the Field Service category are normally required to move periodically to discharge functions in different duty stations under conditions established in ST/AI/2023/3 on Mobility, as may be amended or revised. This condition of service applies to all position specific job openings and does not apply to temporary positions.
