- Ensure smooth handover of MEL framework, plans, and tools to the permanent team.
- Assist team members with information, tools, and resources to improve performance and reach objectives.
- Promote accountability, communicate expectations, and provide constructive feedback informally and formally via regular one-on-ones and performance reviews.
- Create and sustain a work environment of mutual respect where team members strive to achieve excellence.
- Play an active role in hiring, orienting, and leading team members as necessary.

### SAFEGUARDING RESPONSIBILITIES

- Actively learns safeguarding and integrates it into their work, including safeguarding risks and mitigations related to their area of work.
- Practices the values of Mercy Corps, including respecting the dignity and well-being of participants and fellow team members.
- Encourages openness and communication in their team; encourages team members to submit reports if they have any concerns using reporting mechanisms, e.g., Integrity Hotline and other options.

**Supervisory Responsibility**

MEL Programme managers and Advisors. Mentorship and support to local partner MEL teams

**Accountability**

### **Reports Directly To:** COP Programs

### **Works Directly With:** Country Director, Country MEL Manager, Director of Programmes, MSD Lead, Climate Director, GESI Director, HQ/ Regional MEL Team

**Accountability to Participants and Stakeholders**

Mercy Corps team members are expected to support all efforts toward accountability, specifically to our program participants, community partners, other stakeholders, and to international standards guiding international relief and development work. We are committed to actively engaging communities as equal partners in the design, monitoring, and evaluation of our field projects.

- Advanced degree/s in Statistics, Data Science, Economics, Public Policy, International Development, Organizational Learning, Information Systems, Social Sciences, or a related discipline.
- Minimum of 10 years of international experience in progressively senior leadership roles, including Director-level or above responsibilities in Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEL), Evidence and Learning, Data and Analytics, Program Performance, Impact Measurement, or Performance Management for large, complex development portfolios.
- Proven experience designing and leading enterprise-scale evidence, learning, impact, and performance ecosystems that enable data-driven decision-making, adaptive management, accountability, and organizational performance improvement.
- Demonstrated success in transforming data and evidence into strategic insights that influence program direction, executive decision-making, donor investments, policy engagement, and systems change.
- Strong experience leading the development and deployment of digital and technology-enabled performance management systems, including data analytics, business intelligence, visualization platforms, automation, artificial intelligence, and real-time decision-support tools.
- Proven track record of leading portfolio-wide learning agendas, evaluations, research, impact measurement, knowledge management, and adaptive management processes for large-scale development investments.
- Experience providing strategic advisory support to senior leadership teams and serving as a thought partner on portfolio performance, impact, innovation, and organizational learning.
- Demonstrated ability to build and lead high-performing teams and strengthen the capacity of organizations and partners to generate, interpret, and use evidence to improve performance and results.
- Strong understanding of market systems development, youth employment, economic inclusion, climate-smart agriculture, resilience, and systems-change programming in Africa.
- Outstanding communication, facilitation, and influencing skills, with the ability to effectively engage senior leaders, donors, governments, research institutions, private sector actors, and ecosystem partners.
- Experience working with major international donors, foundations, or large-scale development investments; experience with Mastercard Foundation-funded programs would be a strong advantage.

***Success Factors***

The ideal candidate will have a strong curiosity for understanding and working effectively within the complex cultural, political, security, and social environment of Nigeria. They will be excellent communicators, multi-tasker, and able to work in ambiguous situations. They will be tolerant and flexible individual able to work in difficult and stressful environments and follow procedures. The successful candidate will be focused on team building and capacity-building of national staff; be a strategic thinker, and have strong skills in design, monitoring and evaluation of development programmes.

**Living Conditions / Environmental Conditions**

The Director - Evidence Learning & Impact will be based in Abuja, Nigeria. This position requires at least 40% of time traveling by flight or road to field offices in areas with varying degrees of insecurity.

Mercy Corps team members represent the agency both during and outside work hours when deployed in a field posting or on a visit/TDY to a field posting. Team members are expected to conduct themselves in a professional manner and respect local laws, customs, and Mercy Corps’ policies, procedures, and values at all times and in all in-country venues.

**Accountability to Participants and Stakeholders**

Mercy Corps team members are expected to support all efforts toward accountability, specifically to our program participants, community partners, other stakeholders, and to international standards guiding international relief and development work. We are committed to actively engaging communities as equal partners in the design, monitoring, and evaluation of our field projects.

**Ongoing Learning**

In support of our belief that learning organizations are more effective, efficient, and relevant to the communities we serve, we empower all team members to dedicate 5% of their time to learning activities that further their personal and/or professional growth and development

**Team Efficiency and Effectiveness**

Achieving our mission starts with how we build our team and collaborate. By bringing together individuals with a variety of experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives, we strengthen our ability to solve complex challenges and drive innovation. We foster a culture of trust and respect, where every team member is valued for their contributions, empowered to reach their full potential, and motivated to do their best work.

We recognize that building a strong and effective team is an ongoing process, and we remain committed to learning, improving, and growing together.

**Equal Employment Opportunity**

Mercy Corps is an equal opportunity employer that does not tolerate discrimination on any basis. We actively seek out different backgrounds, perspectives, and skills so that we can be collectively stronger and have sustained global impact.

We are committed to providing an environment of respect and psychological safety where equal employment opportunities are available to all. We do not engage in or tolerate discrimination based on race, color, gender identity, gender expression, religion, age, sexual orientation, national or ethnic origin, disability (including HIV/AIDS status), marital status, military veteran status or any other protected group in the locations where we work.

**Safeguarding & Ethics**

Mercy Corps is committed to ensuring that all individuals we come into contact with through our work, whether team members, community members, program participants or others, are treated with respect and dignity. We are committed to the core principles regarding the prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse laid out by the UN Secretary-General and IASC **and have signed on to the** [**Interagency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme**](https://www.schr.info/the-misconduct-disclosure-scheme)**.** We will not tolerate child abuse, sexual exploitation, abuse, or harassment by or of our team members. As part of our commitment to a safe and inclusive work environment, team members are expected to conduct themselves professionally, respect local laws and customs, and to adhere to [Mercy Corps Code of Conduct Policies](https://www.mercycorps.org/who-we-are/ethics-policies) and values at all times. Team members are required to complete mandatory Code of Conduct e-learning courses upon hire and on an annual basis.

As an applicant, if you witness or experience any form of sexual misconduct during the recruitment process, please report this to Mercy Corps Integrity Hotline (integrityhotline@mercycorps.org).

jobs.title: 23495 Legal Officer (Head, Contract Law Division, Manila Unit) (P)
jobs.description:
The Office of Legal Affairs (LEG) provides legal advice to the Director General, the Deputy Directors General, Regional Offices, Country Offices, and other Departments and Offices of the Organization. The Office provides support to ensure that the activities and operations of the Organization are carried out in accordance with the legal framework governing IOM, including the IOM Constitution, decisions of the governing bodies of IOM, the Unified Staff Regulations and Rules, the Financial Regulations and Rules, IOM internal governance and administrative instruments and international law.

The Office of Legal Affairs is comprised of the Office of the Legal Counsel, the Institutional Law and Programme Support Division (LEGPS), the Contract Law Division (LEGCR), the General and Administrative Law Division (LEGGL), as well as Regional Legal Hubs. The Legal Counsel and Director of the Office is responsible for managing the Office and providing strategic direction for the work of the Office, as well as providing legal advice to Senior Management, reporting directly to the Director General.

The Contract Law Division (LEGCR) is responsible for:

- Providing legal advice on all types of contracts necessary for IOM’s operations and activities, including public and private donor funding agreements, contracts for the purchase of goods and services, project implementation agreements and cooperation agreements with partners and Governments;
- Reviewing contracts that deviate from the Organization’s standard terms and conditions, advising colleagues worldwide on the relevant implications, legal risks and suggested mitigation;
- Reviewing internal administrative instruments and policies related to contracting and otherwise raising contract law issues;
- Assisting colleagues worldwide to structure contractual arrangements for projects, including cash-based initiatives and public-private partnerships;
- Advising on privileges and immunities matters related to contracts and appropriate legal protections in complex areas such as funding conditions, intellectual property, confidentiality, liability and settlement of disputes;
- Representing the Organization as needed in contractual negotiations and disputes. Preparing legal advice on issues of breach of contract and contractual termination; and,
- Developing and maintaining a repository of contract templates for the Organization.

Under the direct supervision of the Head of the Contract Law Division, the Legal Officer (Unit Head, Manila Unit, Contract Law Division) will be accountable and responsible for the following activities.

**Responsibilities**

1. Oversee, supervise, and manage the day-to-day work of LEGCR Manila Unit, Contract Law Division (LEGCR) and guide and supervise the work of the Legal Officers within the Unit.
2. Review and approve various types of contracts and agreements necessary for the development and implementation of IOM projects in a timely manner with limited supervision, taking into account IOM's legal status, IOM's contract templates and the organizational policies, regulations and rules.
3. Revise and update IOM contract templates, including identifying the needs of developing new templates and revising existing templates.
4. Provide timely and pertinent legal advice to contract related (potential) disputes and other problems, including proposing the best actions in response to court summons or invitation to conciliation or arbitration.
5. Review and provide comments to various organizational policies related to the work of LEGCR, including in the areas of funding and operations,
6. Conduct trainings on concluding contracts and agreements for IOM staff for the English-speaking regions.
7. Participate in negotiating legal terms of contracts and agreements and undertake consultations with internal and external entities, as required.
8. Work on a variety of in-house legal issues concerning contractual matters, including drafting or reviewing research papers.
9. Follow up on meetings and international conferences (mainly in the English-speaking regions) relevant to the Office of Legal Affairs regarding issues related to the work of LEGCR.
10. Represent LEGCR in the internal meetings in absence of the Division Head and assist the Division Head in leading the functions of LEGCR.
11. Perform such other duties as may be assigned.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Master’s degree in Law from an accredited academic institution with five years of relevant professional experience; or,
- University degree in Law with seven years of relevant professional experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

**Experience**

- A minimum of five years of relevant professional legal experience:
- At least two years of practicing contract law in the Legal Department of an international organization or private sector entity, or law firm;
- Demonstrated experience with contractual negotiation and disputes; and,
- Experience managing the work of a team is an advantage.

**Skills**

- Proven legal research and contract review skills;
- Membership of a national bar or equivalent professional legal qualification; and,
- Knowledge of the privileges and immunities of international organizations is an advantage.

**Languages**

For this position, fluency in English is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of another official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, Russian, Spanish, and French) is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

jobs.title: 23520 Regional Data Analyst (P)
jobs.description:
Under the overall supervision of the Deputy Regional Director (DRD) for Operations, the direct supervision of the Regional Thematic Specialist (Data and Research), and the guidance of the Chief Migration and Displacement Data and Research Analytics Division in the Department of Data, Insights and Policy, the Regional Data Analyst will focus on generating and communicating analyses and insights in support of decision-making processes. The Regional Data Analyst is responsible for leading Regional Data Hub (RDH) work on migration data analysis, focusing on migration and human mobility dynamics, including mixed migration movements, drivers, trends, and characteristics across the region.

The Regional Data Analyst will work within the RDH Team to pursue its core objective to enhance, strengthen, and promote the regional evidence base on migration and human mobility, including by addressing existing primary data gaps through innovation, insight generation, foresight and scenario building, and consolidating primary and secondary data and analysis work in the region covering migration, displacement, and human mobility.

**Responsibilities**

**Data Processing and Data Use:**

- Locate and define new data analysis process improvement opportunities.
- Identify appropriate data sources for analytics projects.
- Ensure accurate and reliable data centralization to support analytical work.
- Collaborate with Data Engineers and Data Scientists in Headquarters (HQ) or other Missions as available and needed to improve data flows, data quality, etc.
- Coordinate the development and implementation of databases, data collection systems, data analytics and other strategies that optimize statistical efficiency and quality.

**Data Analysis and Reporting:**

- Conduct and coordinate regional, sub-regional, geographic and thematic analyses and reports on issues of relevance to the current human mobility and migration dynamics in the region, paying attention to routes, trends, and patterns which may necessitate additional analysis.
- Identify gaps in migration and human mobility data, specific data needs for local, national, regional, sub-regional and global policymaking, and capacities of relevant actors on migration and human mobility data. Respond to queries on gaps identified by thematic experts. Coordinate the development of tools and mechanisms to complete data gaps, in close alignment with international approaches and standards and existing IOM-supported global mechanisms.
- Support the analysis and validation of internal, cross-border, and international migration and human mobility data collected at various points along the migration journey - at departure, en route, in destination, and upon return- stranded or in need of assistance, voluntary and forced, humanitarian evacuations, support to migrants on socioeconomic inclusion and reintegration, and strengthening their development contributions to societies.
- Use existing IOM data from global, regional, sub-regional and national projects and initiatives for data triangulation to enhance cross-thematic data analysis for regional and national reporting within the region and to strengthen evidence-based policy formulation, national and regional humanitarian and development planning and operations. Coordinate and support cross-regional analysis where relevant.
- Coordinate and support desk reviews and carry out extensive and in-depth analysis of data sources identified under the desk review.
- Identify, analyze, and interpret trends or patterns, using basic machine learning techniques, qualitative, visualization, narrative, and statistical methods to identify relevant features and variables in structured and unstructured sources of information and data.
- Coordinate the development and implementation of various analysis, reporting and quality control capabilities.
- Provide analytical support to Country Offices in the Region as needed.

**Good Data Practice, Knowledge Management and Dissemination:**

- Ensure timely preparation and generation of information products.
- Adhere to IOM data protection, governance, and security standards.
- Consider ethical data collection, use, sharing, and dissemination.
- Participate in working groups and provide strategic input on behalf of IOM.

**Cross-Cutting Issues:**

- Evaluate new applications related to information systems, to new technologies, and processes to manage information in response to RDH needs.
- Ensure the integration of disaggregated data analysis to inform gender-responsive programming, including for specific needs of people such as pregnant women, persons with disabilities, the elderly, children, as well as other highly vulnerable groups within all emergency and transition activities.
- Perform other duties as may be assigned.

**Required Qualifications and Experience**

**Education**

- Master’s degree in Migration Studies, Demography, Political or Social Science, Statistics, Econometrics, Public Health, Sustainability Science, Data Science, or a related field from an accredited academic institution with five years of relevant professional experience; or,
- University degree in the above fields with seven years of relevant professional experience.

Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database.

**Experience**

- Experience in information management, reporting, coordination, and analysis of data triangulation and analysis from multiple large and complex information systems;
- Data analysis experience (including field experience) in the area of demographic and population studies, human mobility, internal and international migration, and refugees/IDPs in developed and developing countries; remote sensing and/or Geographic Information Systems (GIS) analysis experience is also an advantage;
- Practical field experience and analysis expertise in geographic (region and/or specific countries) and thematic (displacement, migration) relevant domain;
- Experience in data collection, data processing (incl. cleaning), data analysis for research, policy, and report writing;
- Experience in internal and/or international mixed migration data analyses is required;
- Self-service analytics and data visualization applications (MS Power BI, Qlik, Tableau or similar), or business intelligence tools (SAP Business Objects, etc.) are desirable;
- Experience with database or programming languages (SQL, Python, R) is desirable; other data analysis software may be advantageous (e.g., STATA, QGIS);
- Professional experience in coordinating multi-cultural teams and field-based staff;
- Experience in survey and questionnaire design and sampling is an advantage; and,
- Knowledge of IOM data, analytical methodologies and standards is an advantage.

**Skills**

- Excellent drafting skills; Proven skills to analyse statistical information;
- Ability to formulate IM-related technical requirements and operating procedures;
- Ability to translate planning specifications into technical briefs for data capture and analysis, and vice versa;
- Ability to compile and holistically analyse diverse datasets;
- Demonstrated team-building and information management skills; and,
- Demonstrated understanding of different data analysis methodologies.

**Languages**

For this position, fluency in English is required (oral and written).

Working knowledge of another official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian, and Spanish) is an advantage.

Proficiency of language(s) required will be specifically evaluated during the selection process, which may include written and/or oral assessments.

Nigeria is Africa's most populous country, and its influence spreads across the continent. Yet, inequality and insecurity have consistently undermined Nigeria's development. S/he will be responsible for leading the implementation of gender integration strategies aimed at ensuring that program activities result in positive outcomes for male and female participants of different age groups. The Gender, Social and Inclusion Director will work closely with other team members to ensure the effective and timely execution of activities related to gender and age-based access to opportunities. GESI Director will conduct a gender analysis to inform and guide program implementation and to ensure that men, women, girls and boys have equitable opportunities to engage in and benefit from program activities. - Provide strategic leadership and vision for the integration of Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI), youth empowerment, and safeguarding across the Mercy Corps Nigerian Programs.
- Lead the development and implementation of program-wide GESI and Safeguarding strategies, ensuring alignment with Mercy Corps standards, donor requirements, and national frameworks.
- Ensure gender-transformative, youth-centered, disability-inclusive, and safeguarding approaches are embedded throughout the program lifecycle, from design and partner onboarding through implementation, adaptation, learning, and closeout.
- Serve as the principal advisor to program leadership and implementing partners on GESI, youth inclusion, protection, and safeguarding priorities, risks, and opportunities.
- Drive the development of strategies that increase equitable access to economic, social, and development opportunities for women, youth, persons with disabilities, and other marginalized group
- Provide technical leadership to ensure safeguarding considerations are incorporated into program design, implementation plans, partnership agreements, participant engagement approaches, and monitoring systems.
- Lead the identification, assessment, and mitigation of gender, inclusion, protection, and safeguarding risks across program activities and partnerships.
- Establish program-wide standards, tools, indicators, and accountability mechanisms to measure and track GESI, youth empowerment, and safeguarding outcomes.
- Collaborate with technical leads and implementing partners to ensure GESI, youth, and safeguarding commitments are reflected in annual work plans, budgets, learning agendas, and performance targets.
- Promote evidence-based decision-making by leveraging data, research, participant feedback, and learning to continuously strengthen inclusive and safeguarding-centered programming.
- Champion a culture of inclusion, safeguarding, accountability, and participant-centered programming across all program teams, partners, and stakeholders
- Represent the program externally on GESI, youth empowerment, and safeguarding matters with government institutions, private sector actors, technical working groups, and other key stakeholders.
- Ensure that safeguarding, inclusion, and participant well-being remain central to program strategy and decision-making, enabling equitable participation and access to opportunities for all participants

### **PROGRAM MANAGEMENT**

- Develop targeted GESI capacity building interventions for program staff.
- Support program team in the delivery of training and capacity building on key gender and social inclusion topics to project participants.
- Conduct periodic monitoring of field activities; ensure quality delivery of GESI interventions and coach/mentor staff technically on this.
- Document processes and achievements to ensure impact and best practices are captured and disseminated. This will include the continual re-evaluation of program activities and information, with resulting activity adjustments in keeping with new insights.

**REPRESENTATION**

- Develop relationships and linkages with organizations implementing other donor-funded programs focused on GESI in Nigeria.
- Conduct regular community consultations to ensure programming remains GESI sensitive and on track.
- Collect and share learnings and best practices from this program both internally and externally.
- Identify, build and manage collaborative partnerships with implementing partners, donors, local governments, civil society organizations, private sector actors, and other stakeholders
- Communicate effectively to ensure overall program targets and donor obligations are met.

**SECURITY AND RISK MANAGEMENT**

- Collaborate with country leadership to support preparedness and response to major disruptive events.
- Work closely with the country team’s security focal point to develop and maintain systems that promote the safety and security of all team members.
- Ensure that activities are designed and implemented with a clear analysis and understanding of security.

#### Safeguarding Responsibilities

- Actively learns about safeguarding and integrates it into their work, including safeguarding risks and mitigations related to their area of work.
- Practices the values of Prosper Global including respecting the dignity and well-being of participants and fellow team members.
- Encourages openness and communication in their team; encourages team members to submit reports if they have any concerns using reporting mechanisms e.g., Integrity Hotline and other options.

## **Supervisory Responsibility**

- Supervise Mercy Corps GESI and safeguarding team members and provide technical guidance, mentorship, and capacity strengthening support to partner organizations

## **Accountability**

**Reports Directly To:** Chief of Party / Program Director

**Works Directly With:** Program leadership team, technical leads, MEL team, finance and operations teams, partner organizations, regional teams, and HQ technical advisors

## **Minimum Qualification & Transferable Skills**

- MA/S or equivalent experience in development studies, international relations, women’s studies, gender studies, sociology or other social science discipline.
- At least seven years’ experience in gender, youth and social dynamics development work at the community level.
- Experience developing and conducting gender training, gender/youth/social dynamics mainstreaming and engaging in gender advocacy.
- 10 plus years in Senior Program level positions
- Understanding of donor regulations, compliance requirements, and program management systems for large development programs.
- Demonstrated experience in gender equality, safeguarding, social inclusion, women's empowerment, youth development, protection, or related technical leadership roles
- Experience supporting gender equality, social inclusion, youth empowerment, safeguarding, protection, economic development, resilience, or community development programs.
- Demonstrated capacity to lead the collection, analysis and utilization of information from a broad range of sources to ensure effective integration of gender and youth concerns throughout the program’s duration.
- In-depth understanding of gender, age and other locally significant socio-cultural factors in the context of food and nutrition security and resilience programming.
- Skills in participatory learning and facilitating collaborative problem-solving.
- Prior humanitarian and/or development experience working in a context similar to Nigeria.
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English.
- Excellent computer skills (especially Microsoft office applications) and ability to use information technology as a tool and resource.

**Success Factors**

The successful candidate will be a strategic and collaborative leader with a strong commitment to gender equality, social inclusion, safeguarding, and participant-centered programming. They will possess strong technical expertise and the ability to influence diverse stakeholders to ensure that inclusive and equitable approaches are integrated across all aspects of program implementation.

The ideal candidate will demonstrate excellent relationship-building, communication, and facilitation skills and be capable of working effectively with communities, government institutions, private sector actors, donors, and implementing partners. They will foster a culture of accountability, learning, and continuous improvement while ensuring that safeguarding, inclusion, and participant well-being remain central to program design, implementation, monitoring, and decision-making.

They will be an effective mentor and capacity builder, strengthening the ability of teams and partners to deliver high-quality, inclusive programming that contributes to sustainable and meaningful outcomes for participants and communities.

## **Living Conditions / Environmental Conditions**

The GESI Director will be based in Abuja Nigeria. This position requires at least 40% of time traveling by flight or road to field offices in areas with varying degrees of insecurity.

Mercy Corps team members represent the agency both during and outside work hours when deployed in a field posting or on a visit/TDY to a field posting. Team members are expected to conduct themselves in a professional manner and respect local laws, customs, and Mercy Corps’ policies, procedures, and values at all times and in all in-country venues.

## **Accountability to Participants and Stakeholders**

Mercy Corps team members are expected to support all efforts toward accountability, specifically to our program participants, community partners, other stakeholders, and to international standards guiding international relief and development work. We are committed to actively engaging communities as equal partners in the design, monitoring, and evaluation of our field projects.

## **Ongoing Learning**

In support of our belief that learning organizations are more effective, efficient, and relevant to the communities we serve, we empower all team members to dedicate 5% of their time to learning activities that further their personal and/or professional growth and development

## **Team Efficiency and Effectiveness**

Achieving our mission starts with how we build our team and collaborate. By bringing together individuals with a variety of experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives, we strengthen our ability to solve complex challenges and drive innovation. We foster a culture of trust and respect, where every team member is valued for their contributions, empowered to reach their full potential, and motivated to do their best work.

We recognize that building a strong and effective team is an ongoing process, and we remain committed to learning, improving, and growing together.

## **Equal Employment Opportunity**

Mercy Corps is an equal opportunity employer committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all employees and qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, sex, sexual orientation, religion or belief, national origin, age, disability, marital status, veteran status, or any other characteristics protected under applicable law.is an equal opportunity employer that does not tolerate discrimination on any basis. We actively seek out different backgrounds, perspectives, and skills so that we can be collectively stronger and have sustained global impact.

## **Safeguarding & Ethics**

Mercy Corps is committed to ensuring that all individuals we come into contact with through our work, whether team members, community members, program participants or others, are treated with respect and dignity. We are committed to the core principles regarding the prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse laid out by the UN Secretary-General and IASC **and have signed on to the** [**Interagency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme**](https://www.schr.info/the-misconduct-disclosure-scheme)**.** We will not tolerate child abuse, sexual exploitation, abuse, or harassment by or of our team members. As part of our commitment to a safe and inclusive work environment, team members are expected to conduct themselves professionally, respect local laws and customs, and to adhere to [Mercy Corps Code of Conduct Policies](https://www.mercycorps.org/who-we-are/ethics-policies) and values at all times. Team members are required to complete mandatory Code of Conduct e-learning courses upon hire and on an annual basis.

As an applicant, if you witness or experience any form of sexual misconduct during the recruitment process, please report this to Mercy Corps Integrity Hotline (integrityhotline@mercycorps.org).

jobs.title: Web Designer & Digital Communications Consultant (Only Ugandan Based Females) Previous applicants should not reapply.
jobs.description:
**About Bodmando Consulting Group**

Bodmando Consulting Group is a feminist international consulting firm registered in **Uganda** and **Kenya.** As a women-led social enterprise, Bodmando operates at the gender and climate nexus, driven by the vision of a world free from intergenerational poverty, gender inequality, and social injustice. Our work is anchored in intersectional analysis, systems thinking, and human-centred design, ensuring that every solution we craft is both inclusive and transformative. With a multidisciplinary core team spanning Africa, South Asia, and the MENA region, we deliver high-impact research, evaluation, capacity strengthening and strategic advisory services that blend contextual understanding with global best practices.

We further leverage a global consultancy network of over 1,000 technical experts, allowing rapid mobilization of specialized skills for complex, multi-country assignments. Through thought leadership, north-south collaboration, and co-creation, Bodmando continues unlocking value and generating evidence-based, scalable solutions that advance equity, sustainability, and impact. To date, we have successfully implemented more than 65 projects across 31 countries, empowering governments, donors, civil society organizations, and communities to design, implement, and learn from transformative interventions. ***Learn more about our work at*** [***www.bodmando.org***](http://www.bodmando.org)***.***

**Back ground**
Bodmando Consulting Group is seeking a creative, technically competent and proactive Female Web Designer & Digital Communications consultant to manage and strengthen the organisation’s digital presence. The successful candidate will be responsible for ensuring that our website and social media platforms remain functional, current, professional and aligned with modern digital standards.

**Work location**

Kagoma, Wakiso district, Uganda

**Duties and Responsibilities**

The consultant will:

- Manage, maintain and regularly update the Bodmando Consulting Group website, including content, pages, images, project information, publications and other resources.
- Monitor website functionality, performance, security and user experience and promptly address technical issues.
- Continuously improve the website to ensure it remains modern, responsive, user-friendly and consistent with state-of-the-art web design practices.
- Manage and regularly update the organisation’s social media platforms, particularly **LinkedIn and X (formerly Twitter)**.
- Develop, design and publish professional digital content highlighting Bodmando’s projects, research, evaluations, achievements, opportunities and other organisational activities.
- Ensure consistent organisational branding and messaging across the website and social media platforms.
- Monitor digital engagement and periodically provide basic analytics on website and social media performance.
- Support the development of graphics, digital communication materials and other online content as required.
- Provide periodic support to research and consultancy assignments, including supporting field data collection, digital data management and related research activities when required.
- Undertake other reasonable duties assigned by management in support of the organisation’s operations and projects.

**Qualifications**

Applicants should have:

- A diploma or bachelor’s degree in Web Design, Information Technology, Computer Science, Digital Communications, Multimedia, Graphic Design or a related field.
- Demonstrated experience in website design, administration and maintenance.
- Experience managing professional social media accounts, particularly LinkedIn and X.
- Knowledge of WordPress.
- Basic graphic design and digital content development skills.
- Ability to troubleshoot website and digital platform issues.
- Strong written communication, organisation and attention-to-detail skills.
- Ability to work independently, meet deadlines and manage multiple assignments.
- Willingness to periodically participate in research and field data collection activities.
- Experience working with consulting, research, development or similar organisations will be an added advantage.

jobs.title: Coordinateur Logistique et Approvisionnement
jobs.description:
INTERSOS est une Organisation Humanitaire Non Gouvernementale, à but non lucratif, qui a pour objectif d’assister les victimes de désastres naturels et de conflits armés. INTERSOS base son action sur les valeurs de la solidarité, de la justice, de la dignité humaine, de l’égalité des droits et des opportunités pour tous les peuples, du respect des diversités, de la cohabitation, de l’attention aux groupes sociaux les plus vulnérables.

## **Termes de référence**

**Intitulé du poste** : Coordinateur Logistique et Approvisionnement

**Code :** SR-49-10326

**Pays :** RCA (République centrafricaine)

**Lieu d’affectation** : Bangui avec déplacements sur les zones opérationnelles.

**Date de prise de fonction** :15/11/2026

**Durée du contrat** : 6 mois renouvelable

**Sous la supervision de :** Chef de mission

**Supervision de :** Équipe logistique

**Lieu d'affectation:** sans famille

## **Contexte général du projet**

La République centrafricaine est confrontée depuis plus de deux décennies à des crises complexes et récurrentes, caractérisées par des dynamiques sécuritaires, sanitaires et climatiques.

Bien que des évolutions positives soient observées dans certaines zones, la situation reste fragile, avec des poches d’insécurité persistantes sur certains axes et localités, affectant l’accès aux services essentiels et les conditions de vie des populations.

Par ailleurs, le pays fait face à des chocs humanitaires récurrents, notamment des épidémies (dont le choléra), ainsi que des aléas climatiques tels que les inondations, qui aggravent la vulnérabilité des communautés.

Dans ce contexte, les besoins humanitaires demeurent élevés, en particulier dans les secteurs de l’accès à l’eau, de l’assainissement, de la santé et de la protection.

INTERSOS est présent en RCA depuis 2014 et met en œuvre des interventions humanitaires visant à répondre aux besoins des populations affectées, dans le respect des principes d’humanité, de neutralité, d’impartialité et d’indépendance.

L’organisation dispose d’un bureau de coordination à Bangui et d’une présence opérationnelle dans plusieurs préfectures, notamment la Kémo, Bamingui-Bangoran, Nana-Gribizi, Haute-Kotto, Ouham et Ouham-Pendé.

## **Objectif général de la position**

Définir et mettre en œuvre l'ensemble des stratégies d'approvisionnement, de logistique et de TIC et d'appui à la mission, en veillant à la pertinence et à la cohérence des systèmes logistiques et d'approvisionnement, à l'adéquation des moyens mis à disposition et au respect des normes, protocoles et procédures d'INTERSOS pour favoriser le développement de la mission et optimiser l'impact des projets.

Travailler en étroite collaboration avec le personnel du programme et de l'administration afin d'assurer l'établissement de rapports, le soutien et l'assistance complets à l'égard de toutes les activités d'INTERSOS.

Est responsable de la gestion logistique du logiciel IMP et fait partie de la mission Senior Management Team (SMT).

## **Principales responsabilités et tâches**

**Coordination et soutien**

- Participer activement à la définition et à la mise à jour de la planification et des budgets annuels des projets, en définissant des stratégies et en fournissant des conseils au chef de mission pour traduire les besoins identifiés en matière de logistique, d'approvisionnement et de TIC en objectifs, priorités et ressources nécessaires à la mission
- Est responsable du suivi de la mise en œuvre des activités de logistique, d'approvisionnement et de TIC dans la mission (construction et réhabilitation, stockage et fourniture de matériel non médical et médical, gestion de la flotte et transport, eau et assainissement, véhicules et moteurs, équipements/installations et infrastructures, règles de sécurité (mise en œuvre et application, TIC, biens, etc.)
- Assurer le respect des normes, protocoles et procédures d'INTERSOS, dans l'ensemble de la mission et conformément aux exigences des donateurs, y compris en matière d'approvisionnement. Rendre compte au chef de mission de l'élaboration des programmes en cours et proposer des stratégies de réorientation au besoin
- Est chargé d'assurer la référence technique et le soutien pour toutes les questions de logistique, d'approvisionnement et de TIC dans la mission, de fournir un encadrement au personnel logistique et de représenter INTERSOS lors de réunions avec les autorités, d'autres ONG et les réseaux de coordination pour les questions techniques et logistiques
- Assurer la production de SOP au niveau de la mission (si nécessaire) pour les besoins logistiques

**Gestion de l'information logistique**

- Fournir des rapports mensuels au chef de mission, au coordonnateur régional de la logistique et de l'approvisionnement (par l'intermédiaire du PGI) et aux personnes concernées sur l'évolution des projets et des missions du point de vue technique et logistique, et proposer des corrections si nécessaire.
- S'assurer que les données remontées dans le logiciel INTERSOS Logistics (Intersos Management Platform - IMP) sont correctement utilisées et exactes. Assurer la formation du personnel de la mission si nécessaire et soutenir la mise en œuvre du logiciel INTERSOS Logistics dans les missions

**Gestion de la chaîne d'approvisionnement et approvisionnement**

- Suivi de la performance globale de l'approvisionnement pour la mission. Assurer une planification efficace et rentable de l'approvisionnement en assurant la liaison avec le personnel technique, le coordonnateur sur le terrain et/ou les chefs de projet. Veiller à ce que les plans d'approvisionnement en ligne soient créés sur IMP et à jour, tout en garantissant le respect à tout moment des politiques et procédures d'approvisionnement d'INTERSOS et des bailleurs de fonds. Recherche pour déterminer les meilleurs produits et fournisseurs en termes de meilleur rapport qualité-prix, délais de livraison et qualité
- Assurer la coordination avec le département de l'administration et des finances pour s'assurer que les processus de paiement aux fournisseurs sont effectués à temps et dans le respect des systèmes financiers.
- Planifier et effectuer des vérifications sur le terrain pour s'assurer de l'uniformité du processus, de l'application et du maintien de la documentation et du classement appropriés.
- Élaborer et mettre en œuvre des instructions, des politiques et des procédures de gestion des contrats de service. Examiner et réévaluer les contrats de service existants et superviser les loyers réguliers, les paiements de services publics (c'est-à-dire l'électricité, l'eau, le gaz, etc.), les contrats d'entretien des bureaux et des maisons d'hôtes et les procédures relatives aux coûts de fonctionnement. Veiller à ce qu'ils soient correctement pris en charge par l'officier de la logistique et de l'approvisionnement et les assistants, l'administration et/ou les points focaux.
- Aperçu du fait que le gestionnaire de l'approvisionnement/adjoint et le coordonnateur sur le terrain (agent(e) de la logistique et de l'approvisionnement tiennent à jour une liste de fournisseurs préqualifiés par base
- Est responsable d'assurer le bon stockage de tous les matériaux du projet dans l'entrepôt/stock, dans le respect des SOP d'approvisionnement d'INTERSOS et des contrôles d'inventaire réguliers tous les trimestres
- Vérifier et coordonner avec le personnel logistique que les livraisons de marchandises sont effectuées comme prévu et correctement stockées
- Préparer et lancer les documents d'appel d'offres en coordination avec l'équipe d'approvisionnement

**Gestion des transports**

- S'assurer que le modèle de gestion de flotte d'INTERSOS, les protocoles de sécurité des mouvements et le manuel d'identité de la marque sont appliqués dans les missions - la flotte est vérifiée et régulièrement entretenue, les véhicules sont assurés et les taxes sont payées.
- Assurer le suivi de la surveillance adéquate de la consommation de carburant et de l'utilisation du carnet de bord des véhicules, du carnet d'entretien, du carnet d'huile et d'autres formats et modèles de flotte par le personnel logistique du coordonnateur sur le terrain. S'assurer que la documentation appropriée des véhicules (c.-à-d. location, assurance, inspection mécanique, etc.) est correctement gérée par le personnel de la logistique.
- Contribuer à l'élaboration d'approches durables en matière de gestion des transports en rationalisant la politique environnementale d'INTERSOS et les suggestions des bureaux régionaux.

**Gestion des installations et des communications**

- Superviser l'installation et l'entretien d'espaces de bureaux fonctionnels et d'installations de maisons d'hôtes avec des conditions de vie adéquates et conformément aux normes minimales et au manuel d'identité de marque d'INTERSOS. S'assurer de l'application des mesures de sûreté et de sécurité définies et effectuer des visites d'inspection pour évaluer les besoins de réhabilitation des installations
- Veiller à ce que les installations disposent d'une infrastructure et d'un équipement informatiques et de communication appropriés pour assurer la maintenance des plates-formes logicielles INTERSOS et conformément aux politiques et procédures - permettant une communication permanente entre les immobilisations, les projets, les bases et le siège et une bonne gestion des bases. S'assurer que tous les membres du personnel de la mission reçoivent une formation adéquate sur l'utilisation de l'équipement de communication disponible (p. ex., téléphones satellites, radios HF/VHF, ordinateurs, etc.)
- Contribuer à l'élaboration d'approches durables en matière de gestion des installations en rationalisant la politique environnementale d'INTERSOS et les suggestions des bureaux régionaux.

**Gestion d'actifs**

- Superviser l'achat, l'utilisation et l'entretien des actifs informatiques, de l'équipement de bureau et de projet, ainsi que des outils de communication, tout en veillant à ce que tous les actifs de la mission enregistrés dans le PGI soient documentés, qu'ils reçoivent des numéros d'actifs INTERSOS uniques, qu'ils soient étiquetés et enregistrés conformément aux politiques et procédures de gestion des actifs.
- Rapportez la liste des actifs à la fin du projet et supervisez le transfert des actifs en fonction de la destination définie avec le service des programmes
- Superviser la vérification régulière des immobilisations tous les trimestres

**Gestion des ressources humaines**

- Coordonner l'équipe logistique et participer aux processus RH (recrutement, formation, briefing/débriefing, évaluation, potentiel, détection, développement du personnel et communication interne) afin d'assurer à la fois le dimensionnement et la quantité de connaissances requises pour les activités dont il est responsable

**Sécurité appliquée**

- En collaboration avec le Chef de Mission et le Coordonnateur de la Sécurité (le cas échéant), il est chargé de co-définir et de suivre les aspects techniques de la politique de réduction des risques, du transport, de la communication, de la protection, de l'identification et de la préparation des aspects techniques de la politique et des directives de sécurité de la mission, du plan d'évacuation et du plan d'urgence, du suivi quotidien des règles de sécurité et du signalement au Chef de Mission de tout problème. À cette fin, en l'absence d'un point focal dédié à la sécurité, le coordonnateur logistique doit créer un environnement approprié pour faciliter l'échange d'informations sur les situations de sécurité. Il s'agit de la sauvegarde de sécurité en l'absence du chef de mission.

## **Profil requis**

**Education**

- Diplôme essentiel et spécialisation en logistique et/ou gestion de la chaîne d'approvisionnement

**Expérience Professionnelle**

- Essentiellement, au moins quatre ans d'expérience professionnelle dans des postes logistiques pertinents et une expérience humanitaire antérieure avec des ONG dans des pays en développement. Expérience préalable souhaitable dans le domaine des situations d'urgence

**Exigences Professionnelles**

- Connaissances essentielles en informatique (Word, Excel et Internet)

**Langues**

- Français essentiel
- La maîtrise de l'anglais sera un atout.

**Exigences personnelles**

- Vision stratégique
- Leadership
- Gestion et perfectionnement du personnel
- Orientation vers le service
- Flexibilité comportementale
- Orientation vers les résultats et la qualité
- Gestion du stress
- Engagement envers les principes d'INTERSOS

### **Conditions générales et avantages :**

- **Fourchette de salaire :** 12 - 3.690€ - 4.245€ monthly gross
- **Rémunération**: La rémunération mensuelle pour chaque poste est définie conformément à la grille salariale et à la grille de fonctions standard internationales d'INTERSOS, en tenant compte de l'expérience du candidat sélectionné. Elle est communiquée lors de l'entretien avec les ressources humaines, ou en tout état de cause lors de la première étape du processus de sélection.
- **Hébergement :** Shared Guesthouse
- **R&R :** Le personnel d'INTERSOS tenu de travailler pendant des périodes prolongées dans des lieux d'affectation soumis à des conditions périlleuses, stressantes et difficiles bénéficie d'une période régulière et obligatoire de repos et de récupération (R&R). Cette mesure vise à protéger sa santé et son bien-être et à garantir une performance de travail optimale lors de la reprise de ses fonctions, tout en préservant la capacité opérationnelle de l'Organisation. Les avantages liés au R&R ne constituent pas une compensation financière pour le degré de pénibilité et d'insécurité d'un lieu d'affectation. **Admissibilité :** Les membres du personnel recrutés en tant que personnel international de terrain dont le contrat indique un lieu d'affectation R&R comme lieu d'affectation principal et dont la durée du contrat est égale ou supérieure à 4 mois civils. R&R : il consiste en 7 jours de récupération psychophysique toutes les 8/10/12 semaines, selon le lieu d'affectation. Une indemnité de 1 000 € y est associée.
- **Congés annuels :** 2,5 jours par mois
- **Assurance médicale:** Assurance accidents et décès ; assurance responsabilité civile ; remboursement des vaccins, du certificat médical et du test PCR pour le déploiement ; soutien psychosocial sur demande pour le travailleur humanitaire.
- **Transport:** Vols A/R pour l'humanitaire. Pour toute mission d'une durée d'au moins 9 mois, un billet d'avion supplémentaire vers le pays de résidence et le retour sur le lieu de mission est pris en charge par l'Organisation pour le travailleur humanitaire.
- **Visa:** INTERSOS prend en charge les frais et l'assistance pour l'obtention du visa pour le travailleur humanitaire.
- **Formation d’intégration :** Cours d'orientation en ligne : chaque nouveau membre du personnel reçoit une formation préparatoire avant le départ, adéquate pour fournir les informations nécessaires relatives à la structure d'INTERSOS et aux principaux processus décisionnels et outils de travail, afin de faciliter son intégration au sein de l'Organisation.
- **Remarque 1 :** INTERSOS applique une « politique d'apprentissage et de développement » (Learning & Development Policy) qui inclut la possibilité de bénéficier de formations et de participer à des formations internes et externes. La priorité sera accordée au personnel travaillant pour INTERSOS depuis plus de deux ans.
- **Remarque 2 :** La classification des lieux d'affectation avec accompagnement, R&R et sans accompagnement est soumise à des critères de sécurité, d'accès aux services de santé et d'éducation, et n'est pas négociable.

jobs.title: Finance Manager
jobs.description:
INTERSOS is an independent humanitarian organization that assists the victims of natural disasters, armed conflicts and exclusion. Its activities are based on the principles of solidarity, justice, human dignity, equality of rights and opportunities, respect for diversity and coexistence, paying special attention to the most vulnerable people.

## **Terms of reference**

**Job Title:** Finance Manager

**Code**: SR-49-10322

**Duty station:** Maiduguri

**Starting date:** 16/11/2026

**Contract duration:** 11 months

**Reporting to:** Finance Coordinator

**Supervision of:** Finance Officer

**Type of duty station:** Non-family duty station

## **General context of the project**

With over a decade of conflict, there have been devastating humanitarian consequences across the Northeast (Borno, Adamawa, and Yobe (BAY) states) and the Northwest of Nigeria. According to the Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan 2025, an estimated 7.8 million women, men, and children need some form of humanitarian and protection assistance. 2.3 million people have been forced to flee their homes due to persistent violence and remain internally displaced. Food insecurity and malnutrition are exacerbated by inflation, poverty, and restricted access due to insecurity, which impedes livelihood opportunities. 5.1 million are projected to be acutely food insecure during the 2025 lean season, with 2.5 million children malnourished. Gender-based violence (GBV) has been a significant protection concern faced by IDP women and girls in the area. Numerous basic infrastructure facilities, such as hospitals, clinics, and water supplies are damaged, posing constraints on essential service provision. Epidemics like cholera arising from flooding and overcrowded settings put extra stress on the already vulnerable communities.

In support to the coordinated humanitarian response in Nigeria, INTERSOS has been delivering multi-sectoral interventions addressing critical gaps in protection, health and nutrition, WASH, food security & livelihoods, and Camp Coordination and Camp Management for the most vulnerable communities in both Northeast and Northwest Nigeria, with funding support from OCHA, ECHO, WFP, SV, etc.

## **General purpose of the position**

Manage and supervise the economic and financial management of the mission (accounting, treasury, audit procedures, etc.) in compliance with legal obligations and INTERSOS standards and protocols in order to provide quality, reliable, and transparent information on the use and allocation of resources in the mission.

## **Main responsibilities and tasks**

**Accounting and budget**

- In case there is no Accounting Manager in the mission, they are responsible for quality and timely accounting for the whole mission, e.g. cash procedures, bank account transactions, receipts and supporting administrative and financial documents, electronic data entry, consolidation of overall mission accounting, grants, monthly closing process, bank reconciliation and documents, ensuring strict respect of deadlines and compliance with INTERSOS and donors' guidelines, financial standards and procedures
- Is the technical reference for any financial management-related issue: budgeting, direct and indirect cost allocation, donors' financial reporting, tax compliance, statutory annual audit, and donors’ audit.
- In collaboration with the Finance Coordinator, supports the preparation of the annual budget of the mission in line with financial and economic forecasts and INTERSOS applicable requirements (protocols, guidelines, SoPs…), ensuring the collaboration
- Support the Project / Programme Manager in preparing no-cost extension and budget revision
- Supervise the liquidity level of the mission (cash and bank) and report promptly cash-book discrepancies to the Country Finance Coordinator

**Compliance**

- Is responsible for supporting the Country Finance Coordinator in monitoring the economic and financial KPIs of the mission.

INTERSOS is an independent humanitarian organization that assists the victims of natural disasters, armed conflicts and exclusion. Its activities are based on the principles of solidarity, justice, human dignity, equality of rights and opportunities, respect for diversity and coexistence, paying special attention to the most vulnerable people.

## **Terms of reference**

**Job Title:** Medical Coordinator

**Code**: SR-28-10324

**Duty station:** Kabul, with field visits to other locations

**Starting date:** 15/01/2026

**Contract duration:** until31st May 2027

**Reporting to:** Head of Programme

**Functional Supervisor:** Medical Advisor/ Head of Medical Unit

**Supervision of:** Medical team

## **General context of the project**

Managing more than 50 health facilities, INTERSOS plays a prominent role in Afghanistan’s humanitarian health and nutrition response. Its comprehensive primary healthcare approach brings together outpatient care for communicable and non-communicable diseases, sexual and reproductive health, maternal and child healthcare, routine immunisation, screening and treatment of acute malnutrition, and mental health and psychosocial support. These services are complemented by health promotion, community engagement and referral to specialised care, supporting an integrated response to the needs of underserved communities.

## **General purpose of the position**

As Medical Coordinator, you will provide strategic and technical leadership to this extensive programme, with the opportunity to shape its development, strengthen multidisciplinary teams and improve the quality and accessibility of care. Working closely with the Country Director, Head of Programme and HQ Medical Unit, you will translate evolving health and nutrition needs into clear priorities, effective interventions and appropriate allocation of resources. Combining strategic leadership with direct engagement with field teams, you will drive improvements in clinical quality, patient safety and continuity of care, while helping shape the next stage of INTERSOS’ response in Afghanistan in line with humanitarian principles, medical ethics and national and international standards.

- Coordinate with the Medical Unit for the validation of the project proposals he/her designs to be submitted to international donors and private foundation
- Responsible for the supervision and monitoring of the medical technical aspects, humanitarian needs and in coordination with the Logistics and supply Coordinator, the material aspects of the programmes through regular field visits, analysing difficulties during the implementation and reporting deviations as they appear, in order to proactively provide the necessary solutions and achieve operational results

jobs.description:
**\*\*Contingent upon Donor Funding\*\***

**Location:** Abuja Nigeria

**Position Status:** Full-time, Exempt or Non-exempt, Regular

[**Risk Level:**](https://library.mercycorps.org/record/47705?ln=en) X **Level 3** ☐**Level 2** ☐**Level 1**

(Level 3: Frequent contact with participants, direct contact with children, access to sensitive data, and/or high level of accountability.

Level 2: Some contact with participants; unplanned non-direct contact with children.

Level 1: Likely to have no contact with participants or sensitive data)

## **About Mercy Corps**

Mercy Corps is a leading global organization powered by the belief that a better world is possible.

In disaster, in hardship, in more than 40 countries around the world, we partner to put bold solutions

into action — helping people triumph over adversity and build stronger communities from within.

Now, and for the future. Mercy Corps is transitioning to Prosper Global. Learn more [**here**](https://www.prosperglobal.org/mercy-corps). As the transition is being implemented by location, you may see the Mercy Corps and Prosper Global names used concurrently during this period. This is an administrative transition, and our teams, programs and commitments continue without interruption.

**The Program / Department / Team**

Nigeria is Africa's most populous country, and its influence spreads across the continent. Yet, inequality and insecurity have consistently undermined Nigeria's development. Mercy Corps Nigeria was established in 2012 to respond to these challenges. The Nigeria team is headquartered in Abuja, the Federal Capital Territory (FCT), and has programs across 16 states. Mercy Corps works with communities to build economic opportunities, enhance water security, drive peace and good governance, and ensure food security. Our activities aim to build resilience through an integrated approach, helping communities and the most marginalized within them cope, adapt, and thrive in the context of numerous shocks and stresses. With a strong and growing team, Mercy Corps works to achieve the vision of a Nigeria in which all people are empowered, engaged, resilient, and secure.

**The Position**

The Chief of Party (CoP) will lead implementation of Mercy Corps' market systems and youth employment vision in Nigeria, advancing sustainable pathways to work for young women and men through climate-smart agrifood systems and private sector engagement. As the senior-most leader of this flagship investment, the CoP will serve as the chief architect and strategic leader, driving systems change, strengthening agricultural market systems, and positioning the Program as a catalyst for inclusive economic growth and sustainable employment opportunities.

As the senior-most leader of the Program, the CoP will serve as an ecosystem builder, strategic influencer, and trusted thought partner to, government institutions, private sector leaders, financial institutions, and development stakeholders. The CoP will cultivate high-value partnerships, influence investment and sector priorities, and position the Program as a leading platform for innovation, learning, and systems change within Nigeria's agricultural ecosystem. The successful candidate will be a highly accomplished development leader with a demonstrated ability to steward large and complex investments, inspire high-performing teams, influence senior decisionmakers, and drive transformational change at scale while delivering lasting opportunities for young people, strengthened market systems, and sustainable impact beyond the life of the investment.

**Essential Responsibilities**

STRATEGY AND PLANNING

- Provide visionary leadership for Programs, setting the strategic direction for a flagship investment that advances systemic change, strengthens agricultural market systems, and enables large-scale, sustainable pathways to dignified and fulfilling work for young people across Nigeria.
- Serve as the principal steward of the Mercy Corps Program, shaping Program strategy, influencing investment decisions, and ensuring alignment between donor ambitions, partner contributions, market opportunities, and long-term impact objectives.
- Lead and inspire a diverse ecosystem of Program partners, government institutions, private sector actors, financial institutions, research organizations, and development stakeholders around a shared vision for youth employment, agricultural transformation, and inclusive economic growth.
- The CoP will be expected to identify and unlock opportunities for innovation, co-investment, strategic partnerships, and thought leadership that strengthen the Nigeria Program Program's contribution to national development priorities for transformational impact
- Drive innovation, adaptive management, and strategic learning across the Program, ensuring that evidence, emerging opportunities, and implementation insights continuously inform decision-making, Program evolution, and systems-level impact.
- Champion cross-cutting priorities including youth empowerment, gender equality, social inclusion, safeguarding, climate resilience, and locally led development, ensuring they are fully embedded across Program strategy, partnerships, investments, and results.
- Represent the Program and organization at the highest levels with donors, government leaders, industry stakeholders, and development partners, serving as a trusted thought leader and advocating for innovation, systems change, and inclusive economic opportunity.

PROGRAM MANAGEMENT

- Provide executive oversight of Program performance, ensuring delivery of transformative outcomes, achievement of strategic objectives, and responsible stewardship of program resources in alignment with Mercy Corps standards and commitments.
- Lead and strengthen a high-performing ecosystem of Program partners, fostering alignment, accountability, collaboration, and collective ownership of results while ensuring the Program functions as an integrated platform for learning, innovation, and impact.
- Drive the design and implementation of partnership, investment, and capacity-strengthening approaches that build the long-term sustainability, effectiveness, and leadership of Program partners and wider ecosystem actors.
- Ensure Program interventions are market-driven, evidence-informed, youth-centered, climate-smart, gender-transformative, safeguarding-focused, and responsive to emerging opportunities and challenges within the agricultural ecosystem.
- Champion a culture of performance, innovation, adaptive management, and continuous learning, leveraging evidence, technology, and real-time insights to inform strategic decisions and maximize impact at scale.
- Provide strategic oversight of operational, financial, compliance, safeguarding, and reputational risk management, ensuring that Program systems, resources, and support functions effectively enable implementation excellence and sustainable results.

EVIDENCE AND LEARNING

- Provide strategic oversight of Program learning and adaptive management processes, ensuring evidence, data, and stakeholder feedback are systematically used to inform decision-making, improve performance, and strengthen impact.
- Champion a culture of learning, innovation, and accountability across the Program, fostering collaboration among consortium partners to identify, document, and scale promising practices and lessons learned.
- Lead periodic Program reviews and reflection processes, using performance data, market insights, and implementation learning to adapt strategies, manage risks, and maximize opportunities for achieving sustainable outcomes.
- Ensure Nigeria Program’s generated evidence, results, and lessons learned are effectively communicated to partners, government stakeholders, and broader sector audiences to influence policy, practice, and systems-level change.

TEAM MANAGEMENT

- Build, lead, and inspire a high-performing multidisciplinary leadership team, fostering a culture of excellence, accountability, innovation, inclusion, and continuous learning across the Program.
- Provide strategic leadership and mentorship to senior Program staff, creating an enabling environment that empowers teams to perform, collaborate effectively, and deliver results at scale.
- Promote a culture of adaptive leadership, evidence-based decision-making, and shared accountability, ensuring teams are equipped to navigate complexity, manage change, and respond to emerging opportunities and challenges.
- Foster strong collaboration and alignment across Program partners, technical teams, and support functions, ensuring collective ownership of results and effective coordination toward shared Program objectives.
- Champion talent development, succession planning, and leadership growth, strengthening the Program's long-term capacity and contributing to the development of future leaders within Mercy Corps and the wider ecosystem.

REPRESENTATION

- Serve as Mercy Corps' representative at strategic stakeholders’ platforms, building trusted partnerships and positioning the Mercy Corps as a leading contributor in youth employment and climate-smart agriculture.
- Cultivate and manage high-value relationships with government, private sector, financial institutions, development partners, and ecosystem actors to strengthen collaboration, influence priorities, and unlock opportunities for scale and sustainability.
- Represent the Nigeria Programs at national, regional, and global forums, leveraging Program evidence, learning, and partnerships to drive thought leadership, policy influence, and systems-level impact.
- Foster collaboration across Nigeria Program partners and complementary initiatives to maximize collective impact, accelerate learning, and advance long-term change within Nigeria's agricultural ecosystem.

FINANCE AND COMPLIANCE

- Ensure compliance with the Mercy Corps’ regulations.
- Create and maintain systems to ensure effective and transparent use of financial resources for timely and informative reporting in line with program, donor, and Mercy Corps’ needs.
- Ensure sound financial management, including programmatic budgeting, spending projections, and monitoring of payments in compliance with the donor standards.

SECURITY AND RISK MANAGEMENT

- Collaborate with country leadership to support preparedness and response to major disruptive events.
- Work closely with the country team’s security focal point to develop and maintain systems that promote the safety and security of all team members.
- Ensure that activities are designed and implemented with a clear analysis and understanding of security.

**Supervisory Responsibility**

- Program team Managers and Specialist

**Accountability**

**Reports Directly To:** Mercy Corps Nigeria Country Director

**Works Directly With:** Mercy Corps Nigeria Director of Programs, other COPs / Program Directors, HR, Finance and Operations teams, Regional Programs and Technical Teams, and HQ Technical Resources and Quality Unit

**Minimum Qualification & Transferable Skills**

- Advanced degree in Management, Leadership, agriculture, economics, business administration, or related field.
- At least 10 years of international experience in Senior Leadership positions, including being a Chief of Party for large complex programs (preferably $30 million and above).
- Demonstrated experience in market systems development, food security and economic growth, livelihood, agricultural development activities, and/or food systems programming in the African context preferred.
- Proven experience of leading consortiums with both international and national partners and building their capacity and creating an enabling environment for collaboration
- Experience in supporting multiple countries and harmonizing program quality and performance
- Strong interpersonal and communication skills, and a proven ability to network and maintain effective working relationships with diverse actors.
- Experience leading diverse teams in dispersed geographic locations, including inspiring staff and developing a shared vision with staff and stakeholders.
- Knowledge of Nigeria’s governance and conflict dynamics preferred.
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English.

**Success Factors**

The successful candidate will be a strategic and collaborative leader with the ability to provide vision, direction, and oversight for complex Programs. They will possess strong relationship management and influencing skills, with the ability to effectively engage donors, government institutions, private sector actors, implementing partners, and internal stakeholders at senior levels. The candidate will demonstrate a proven ability to lead diverse and geographically dispersed teams, foster collaboration across consortium members, and build an enabling environment for high performance and shared accountability.

They will be adept at navigating complexity, balancing strategic priorities with operational realities, and making sound decisions in dynamic environments. The successful candidate will have strong programmatic and business acumen, with the ability to drive program quality, harmonize approaches across partners and countries, and ensure delivery of results at scale. They will also demonstrate exceptional communication, representation, and networking skills, coupled with the emotional intelligence and adaptability required to build trust, manage competing priorities, and sustain productive partnerships.

The most successful candidate will be entrepreneurial, solutions-oriented, and committed to empowering teams and partners to achieve lasting impact for young people through inclusive, market-driven and locally led development approaches.

**Living Conditions / Environmental Conditions**

The CoP is based in Abuja. This position requires at least 40% of time traveling by flight or road to field offices in areas with varying degrees of insecurity.

Mercy Corps team members represent the agency both during and outside work hours when deployed in a field posting or on a visit/TDY to a field posting. Team members are expected to conduct themselves in a professional manner and respect local laws, customs, and Mercy Corps’ policies, procedures, and values at all times and in all in-country venues.

**Accountability to Participants and Stakeholders**

Mercy Corps team members are expected to support all efforts toward accountability, specifically to our program participants, community partners, other stakeholders, and to international standards guiding international relief and development work. We are committed to actively engaging communities as equal partners in the design, monitoring, and evaluation of our field projects.

**Ongoing Learning**

In support of our belief that learning organizations are more effective, efficient, and relevant to the communities we serve, we empower all team members to dedicate 5% of their time to learning activities that further their personal and/or professional growth and development

**Team Efficiency and Effectiveness**

Achieving our mission starts with how we build our team and collaborate. By bringing together individuals with a variety of experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives, we strengthen our ability to solve complex challenges and drive innovation. We foster a culture of trust and respect, where every team member is valued for their contributions, empowered to reach their full potential, and motivated to do their best work.

We recognize that building a strong and effective team is an ongoing process, and we remain committed to learning, improving, and growing together.

**Equal Employment Opportunity**

Mercy Corps is an equal opportunity employer that does not tolerate discrimination on any basis. We actively seek out different backgrounds, perspectives, and skills so that we can be collectively stronger and have sustained global impact.

We are committed to providing an environment of respect and psychological safety where equal employment opportunities are available to all. We do not engage in or tolerate discrimination based on race, color, gender identity, gender expression, religion, age, sexual orientation, national or ethnic origin, disability (including HIV/AIDS status), marital status, military veteran status or any other protected group in the locations where we work.

**Safeguarding & Ethics**

Mercy Corps is committed to ensuring that all individuals we come into contact with through our work, whether team members, community members, program participants or others, are treated with respect and dignity. We are committed to the core principles regarding the prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse laid out by the UN Secretary-General and IASC **and have signed on to the** [**Interagency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme**](https://www.schr.info/the-misconduct-disclosure-scheme)**.** We will not tolerate child abuse, sexual exploitation, abuse, or harassment by or of our team members. As part of our commitment to a safe and inclusive work environment, team members are expected to conduct themselves professionally, respect local laws and customs, and to adhere to [Mercy Corps Code of Conduct Policies](https://www.mercycorps.org/who-we-are/ethics-policies) and values at all times. Team members are required to complete mandatory Code of Conduct e-learning courses upon hire and on an annual basis.

As an applicant, if you witness or experience any form of sexual misconduct during the recruitment process, please report this to Mercy Corps Integrity Hotline (integrityhotline@mercycorps.org).

jobs.title: 23674 Emergency Officer (Humanitarian Response and Recovery (HRR)) (P)
jobs.description:
Under the overall supervision of the Chief of Mission and direct supervision of the Programmes Coordinator (Humanitarian Response and Recovery (HRR)), N'Djamena, and the administrative supervision of the Head of Sub Office, the Emergency Officer (HRR) will be responsible and accountable for supporting the implementation and management of the portfolio of Emergency Operations in the relevant Region of Chad.

**Responsibilities**

1.
