**Job Title:** Safety & Security Officer (Ukrainian nationals)

**Department:** Safety & Security

**Division:** Operations

**Duty Station:** Mykolaiv, Ukraine

**Line Manager:** Safety & Security Manager

**Line Management Responsibility:** N/A

**Position Type:** Full-time

**Overview:**

Nonviolent Peaceforce (NP) is a dynamic, international non-governmental organisation. We work with people affected by violent conflicts to enhance their security and dignity through Unarmed Civilian Protection (UCP). We work to reduce violence, protect civilians in countries affected by violent conflict and its aftermath, and help transform the world’s response to conflict situations.

NP first established a presence in Ukraine in 2014/2015 working on peacebuilding and conflict mediation. NP has had a sustained presence in Ukraine since April 2022. NP occupies a unique space in the protection response in Ukraine; simultaneously providing direct protection to at-risk civilians and providing hands-on support to front-line volunteer collectives to directly contribute to the sustainability and safety of their actions.

**Job Summary:**

The Safety and Security Officer works directly with the Head of Operations and Security to contribute to the safety and security of NP staff in Ukraine. The position will support with analysis and security inputs and will engage directly with programmes teams for security monitoring and guidance. The position contributes to making sure effective safety and security arrangements are in place for NP staff.

The ideal candidate will bring security expertise developed through experience working in the security and/or humanitarian sector. They are focused and driven by a keen interest and personal commitment to civilian protection – the core of NP’s work.

**Key Responsibilities:**

**Safety & Security Management**

- Implement and uphold NP safety and security policies, procedures, SOPs, and contingency plans at field and office level.
- Conduct regular security and risk assessments to identify threats, vulnerabilities, and mitigation measures.
- Support the operationalisation of security plans including travel management, incident response, emergency communications, evacuation, relocation, and hibernation procedures.
- Ensure offices, guesthouses, and programme sites meet minimum physical security standards through regular infrastructure and security audits.
- Immediately report and document all security incidents, breaches, threats, or near-misses affecting staff, assets, or operations.

**Operational Support & Staff Movement**

- Provide real-time tracking, monitoring, and oversight of staff and vehicle movements in line with established procedures.
- Ensure vehicles, communications equipment, and personal protective equipment are available, functional, and compliant with minimum standards.
- Work closely with Logistics to identify, procure, and maintain safety and security equipment and resources.

**Information Management & Analysis**

- Collect, verify, analyze, and disseminate security-related information from formal and informal sources.
- Maintain up-to-date records of security incidents, trends, and contextual developments.
- Provide timely security briefings, updates, and advisories to staff and management in response to changes in context.
- Contribute to weekly and monthly security reports relevant to NP areas of operation.

**Training & Capacity Building**

- Deliver regular security briefings, inductions, and awareness sessions for staff.
- Identify security capacity-building needs and support the design and delivery of relevant trainings.
- Train, mentor, and support designated Security Focal Points across field offices.
- Supervise, train, and develop security staff at office or area level where applicable.

**Coordination, Liaison & Access**

- Maintain strong working relationships with NGOs, UN agencies, INSO, security providers, and relevant coordination platforms.
- Liaise with local authorities, community leaders, and other relevant stakeholders to support safe access and programme implementation, in line with humanitarian principles.
- Participate in security coordination forums and inter-agency meetings as required.
- Support access analysis and security input for programme planning and expansion into new areas of operation.

**Assessments & Compliance**

- Participate in security assessments for new locations and evolving operational areas.
- Ensure adherence to NP security risk management standards and country-specific SOPs.
- Support senior management in internal security reviews and audits.

**Safeguarding & Conduct**

- Comply with and uphold NP safeguarding policies, including child protection, prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse (PSEA), and policies on bullying and harassment.
- Act in accordance with NP Codes of Conduct at all times.

**Critical Interfaces**

- All NP staff and departments.
- Senior Management Team.
- Programme and Operations teams.
- Logistics and Administration.
- External coordination and security actors.

**Qualifications:**

- Post-secondary education in a related field with at least 2 years related work experience or equivalent in work experience.
- Relevant security experience in humanitarian settings / previous experience working with security providers, law enforcement entities, and/or intelligence resources and utilizing information to create and deploy actionable security plans and programs.
- Understanding of current security management good practice.
- Good grasp of various communications technologies commonly used, including VHF radio systems, satellite phones, cell phones, Power Bi, etc.
- Excellent interpersonal, representation and negotiation skills, with the ability to influence, build consensus and develop partnerships.
- Ability to work well under pressure in unstable and frequently changing security environments.
- Training and facilitator skills; ability to support training sessions is a plus.
- Commitment to and understanding of NP’s methodologies, core values and mission.
- Advanced proficiency in written and spoken English, Ukrainian and Russian.
- Computer literacy, particularly in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, databases.
- Valid Ukrainian driving license.
- Knowledge of and commitment to safeguarding, whistleblowing, PSEA and anti-corruption.

**Skills and Competencies:**

**Independent Judgment/Analytical:**

- Ability to set priorities, solve problems and analyse data.
- Ability to manage information with discretion.
- Identify safety and security issues and propose solutions.

**Interpersonal:**

- Ability to communicate effectively with individuals and motivate and provide leadership to team and to work and live in a multi-cultural environment.
- Ability to exert solutions-focused, creative behaviour.
- Proven ability to build relationships with the full range of actors including government, military, police and non-state actors.

**Job Title:** Policy & Advocacy Assistant

**Department:** Advocacy

**Technical Line Manager:** U.S. Policy and Advocacy Manager

**Line Management Responsibility:** N/A

**Position Type:** Part-time, non-exempt

**OVERVIEW**

Nonviolent Peaceforce (NP) reimagines security and civilian protection in areas most impacted by conflict by working alongside communities to interrupt and prevent violence. NP is a global civil society organization that works with people affected by violent conflicts to enhance their security and dignity through Unarmed Civilian Protection (UCP) and by helping to transform the world’s response to conflict situations.

Since 2020, NP has worked alongside local communities in the U.S. to interrupt cycles of violence and build bridges across polarized communities. Responsive to community needs, NP builds relationships with community members, leaders, and organizations to identify risks to safety and ways to work together to keep communities safe through nonviolent strategies. These strategies include protective presence, training, safety planning, and rapid response. This work takes us to demonstrations, marches, courts, voting centers, health facilities, pantries, and other public spaces where people may face violence and intimidation. In partnership with local organizations we help build stronger protection networks, coordinate responses to emerging risks and advance the practice of nonviolent community-led approaches to protection in communities across the country.

**JOB SUMMARY**

Nonviolent Peaceforce U.S. (NPUS) is seeking a Policy and Advocacy Assistant to support NP's Advocacy team within the External Engagement function. The Policy and Advocacy Assistant will support NP’s advocacy to the U.S. government and the broader work of the global Policy and Advocacy team, with a special focus on the federal appropriations process. Under the supervision of the U.S. Policy and Advocacy Manager the Policy and Advocacy Assistant will represent NP in coalition meetings, submit congressional appropriations requests, and meet with congressional staffers to educate on the importance of key foreign assistance funds. jobs.title: Oficial de Gestión de Casos de Protección (PCM) - Carúpano
jobs.description:
El Consejo Dánes para refugiados es una de las ONG humanitarias líderes en el mundo, que trabaja en más de 40 países para brindar asistencia y protección adecuadas a refugiados, solicitantes de asilo, desplazados internos, retornados, personas en movimiento y población local vulnerable/comunidades de acogida. Actualmente, DRC está buscando un **Oficial de Gestión de Casos de Protección** altamente calificado con sede en **Carúpano, Edo. Sucre.**

**Acerca del trabajo:**

DRC está administrando sus operaciones en Venezuela, bajo la dirección de la oficina de país en Caracas y cuatro oficinas de campo ubicadas en los estados de Sucre, Apure, La Guaira y Zulia. DRC Venezuela está implementando actividades como monitoreo de protección, asistencia legal, asistencia de protección individual para PWSN, sesiones informativas para PoC, prevención de trata de personas, rehabilitación de infraestructura de salud y seguridad alimentaria.

**Descripción del cargo:**

Evaluar los casos remitidos por actores externos u otros sectores internos del DRC para la previsión de servicios de asistencia humanitaria complementaria de protección, EcRec y Ayuda Legal. Ser responsable por el desempeño eficaz y profesional de las actividades del proyecto. Con labores en oficina base Carúpano con misiones frecuentes entre las parroquias de los municipios de implementación.

- Bajo la supervisión del Líder de Equipo de Gestión de Casos de Protección, el/la Oficial de Gestión de Casos será responsable de recibir, evaluar, gestionar, acompañar y remitir casos con necesidades especifica de protección (salud, medicamentos de emergencia, apoyo psicosocial, transporte humanitario, alojamiento de emergencia, artículos en especie y ayuda legal).
- Transferir casos con criterios de VBG a otros actores especializados y continuar la respuesta de ser necesario con el resto de los miembros expuestos a otros riesgos de protección.
- Desarrollará y mantendrá buenas relaciones con las personas de interés, las partes interesadas relevantes y otros actores humanitarios, para facilitar la implementación y coordinación adecuadas de las actividades del proyecto de DRC-Carúpano.
- Apoyar al Líder de Equipo de Gestión de Casos de Protección en garantizar la calidad de la planificación, implementación, seguimiento de las actividades de protección, dando cumplimento a los planes de acción construidos y priorizados en conjunto con las personas de interés.

**RESPONSABILIDADES:**

**Implementación del Proyecto de Protección.**

- Recibir remisiones externas e internas de casos de personas con necesidades específicas de protección, asignadas por la TL de manera equitativa a cada oficial y proceder con la evaluación de riesgo y gestión de casos una vez sean analizados los perfiles de protección según los criterios fijados por DRC.
- Coordinar con otras unidades del DRC, actores externos y organizaciones humanitarias para la respuesta integral de la gestión de los casos.
- Asegurar el consentimiento informado del beneficiario la asistencia humanitaria necesaria para abordar las necesidades de protección identificadas.
- Garantizar una escucha activa de los beneficiarios con el objetivo de identificar el servicio de asistencia humanitaria más apropiado para abordar las necesidades de protección identificadas.
- Registrar los casos recibidos y aceptados en las carpetas correspondientes y bases de datos de la organización.
- Mantener actualizada constantemente la información contenida en las herramientas de gestión de casos.
- Manejar la información confidencial de manera correcta, gestionando los archivos físicos y digitales de protección de manera precisa, correcta y completa.
- Desarrollar planes de acción para abordar las necesidades específicas identificadas procediendo a entregar la asistencia humanitaria, incluidos los servicios médicos, agua, saneamiento e higiene, educación, alojamiento de emergencia, de transporte para reunificación familiar y entrega de artículos en especie.
- Asegurar la entrega de la asistencia humanitaria identificada manejando solicitudes de compras y, por ende, estableciendo articulación con el equipo de soporte quien será el encargado de articular con los proveedores de servicios.
- Asegurar la correcta legalización de los gastos efectuados para la provisión de servicios de asistencia humanitaria.
- Asegurar el seguimiento de los casos averiguando la satisfacción de los beneficiarios en la recepción de servicios.
- Asegurar el cierre de casos en un tiempo adecuado al marco de emergencia en el cual se implementa.
- Proporcionar información para informes semanales, mensuales, trimestrales y anuales según requerido por la Líder de Gestión de Casos de Protección o Gerente de Protección.
- Asegurar la más alta calidad de las intervenciones de gestión de casos y la coherencia entre todos los proyectos en curso y propuestos, de acuerdo con la estrategia general;
- Seguir los planes de trabajo y las directrices del proyecto manteniendo los principios de confidencialidad.

**Programación y Operaciones**

- Asegurar la implementación eficiente y efectiva del proyecto mientras sigue el plan de trabajo.
- Participar en la preparación de informes y presupuestos mensuales.
- Participar en la implementación de actividades generales de protección de acuerdo con los objetivos acordados.
- Monitorear y documentar continuamente las necesidades de las personas de interés en los formatos de seguimientos, además del desarrollo de planes de acción en un tiempo oportuno según sea el nivel de riesgo.
- Llevar a cabo tareas básicas dentro del área de protección, incluyendo recolección de datos, identificación de patrones y tendencias, como llegadas / salidas / nuevos flujos de personas de interés en el área, etc.
- Apoyar en otras actividades de programa y de los equipos multidisciplinarios del DRC base Carúpano.

**Experiencia y competencias:**

- Mínimo 1-2 años de experiencia relevante en protección humanitaria, de preferencia Gestión de Casos de Protección, trabajo social, derechos humanos u otro trabajo similar de terreno, relacionado a una ONG u otra organización sin fines de lucro.
- Experiencia de terreno y de trabajo con perfiles de personas refugiadas, migrantes, desplazados internos o comunidad de acogida expuesta a situaciones de violencia.
- Experiencia y habilidades demostradas en protección humanitaria y un enfoque diferencial en respuestas de protección.
- Experiencia en apoyo psicosocial o primeros auxilios psicológicos.
- Experiencia en solicitudes de compras y relación con proveedores de servicios.
- Optimas habilidades para trabajar con tabletas y computadores.
- Optimas habilidades en MS Word y Excel.
- Voluntad y habilidad de aprendizaje a corto plazo.
- Optimas habilidades blandas para desarrollar trabajo con equipos multidisciplinarios.

**Deseable**

- De profesión: Psicología, Trabajo Social, Sociología, Derecho, DDHH y carreras afines.
- Experiencia en manejo de casos en contextos de migración mixta y gestión de casos.
- De carácter tranquilo y diplomático.
- Buen trabajo en equipo; habilidad para crear buen ambiente.
- Dominio de inglés es una ventaja.

**Nivel educativo:**

- Título profesional pertinente (por ejemplo; Psicología, Trabajo social, Abogados, Sociólogos, DDHH, entre otros).

**Competencias Básicas de DRC:**

- Luchar por la excelencia: centrarse en alcanzar resultados al tiempo que garantiza procesos eficientes.
- Colaboración: Involucrar a las partes relevantes y alentar la retroalimentación.
- Tomar la iniciativa: Tomar posesión e iniciativa al tiempo que apunta a la innovación.
- Comunicar: Escuchar y hablar con eficacia y honestidad.
- Demostrar integridad: Actuar de acuerdo con la visión y valores de DRC.

**DRC como empleador**
Al trabajar en DRC, te unirás a una fuerza laboral global de alrededor de 6000 empleados en 30 países. Nos enorgullecemos de nuestro:

- Profesionalismo, impacto y experiencia
- Enfoque humanitario y el trabajo que realizamos
- Propósito, significado y contribución personal
- Cultura, valores y liderazgo sólido
- Compensación justa y desarrollo continuo

jobs.title: Oficial de Seguridad y Acceso Humanitario
jobs.description:
**DATOS GENERALES**

- ***Sede del Puesto:** Caracas, Venezuela*
- ***Duración del Contrato:** 5 meses inicialmente*
- ***Supervisor***\*\*:\*\* *Director de proyecto MIHR*

**DESCRIPCIÓN GENERAL DEL PROGRAMA:**

VENGOAL está implementando un programa multianual para apoyar y fortalecer la capacidad de las ONG locales en Venezuela para brindar servicios de salud materna, neonatal e infantil (MNCH) de calidad y mejorar el conocimiento, las prácticas y los resultados de la salud MNCH, incluyendo en comunidades indígenas, mineras y/o afectadas por la minería. Este cargo está abierto solo a residentes y ciudadanos venezolanos.

**PROPÓSITO DEL PUESTO:**

El Punto Focal de Seguridad y Acceso Humanitario de MIHR ELLA - VENGOAL es responsable de facilitar y garantizar un entorno seguro y el acceso sin obstáculos para las operaciones humanitarias en el proyecto MIHR ELLA. Esto incluye monitorear el contexto de seguridad, analizar riesgos, desarrollar estrategias de mitigación y mantener relaciones clave con actores relevantes para asegurar la entrega efectiva de asistencia humanitaria a las poblaciones necesitadas.

Además, MIHR ELLA - VENGOAL reconoce que los pueblos indígenas son titulares de derechos colectivos, poseen sistemas de conocimiento propios, estructuras de gobierno y cosmovisiones que deben ser respetados y comprendidos para establecer cualquier tipo de colaboración. En el marco de presencia en el país, es fundamental garantizar que todas las acciones se realicen con el consentimiento libre, previo e informado (CLPI) de los pueblos indígenas involucrados, asegurando la pertinencia cultural y el respeto a sus derechos y autonomía.

**RESPONSABILIDADES CLAVE**

**Análisis y Monitoreo de Seguridad:**

- Monitorear y analizar continuamente el contexto de seguridad y acceso humanitario en el país, incluyendo tendencias políticas, sociales, económicas y de conflicto.
- Apoyar al Asesor expatriado de Seguridad y Acceso Humanitario de VENGOAL en la producción de informes regulares y análisis de riesgo para informar la toma de decisiones estratégicas y operativas.
- Mantenerse al tanto del derecho internacional humanitario y los derechos humanos, y su impacto diferenciado en las poblaciones afectadas.
- Actuar como punto focal de comunicación principal entre la organización y las autoridades, líderes y miembros de las comunidades indígenas.
- Asesorar al equipo del proyecto sobre protocolos culturales, tiempos y formas adecuadas para el relacionamiento y la toma de decisiones según los usos y costumbres locales.
- Participar en el diseño e implementación de un sistema de monitoreo y evaluación participativo que incorpore indicadores y métodos culturalmente pertinentes.

**Estrategia y Gestión de Seguridad:**

- Desarrollar, implementar y actualizar planes y procedimientos de seguridad y acceso adaptados al contexto local.
- Asesorar a la dirección del país y al personal sobre las mejores prácticas de seguridad y acceso.
- Coordinar la respuesta a incidentes de seguridad y garantizar la gestión adecuada de la información.
- Facilitar y fortalecer la relación de confianza, comunicación y colaboración efectiva entre el Proyecto MIHR ELLA - VENGOAL y los pueblos, comunidades y/u organizaciones indígenas en el área de influencia del proyecto, asegurando que los principios de respeto, interculturalidad y pertinencia cultural guíen todas las fases del proyecto (diseño, implementación, monitoreo y evaluación).

**Coordinación y Enlace:**

- Establecer y mantener una red de contactos con autoridades locales, actores armados (cuando sea apropiado y seguro), líderes comunitarios, organizaciones humanitarias y otras partes interesadas.
- Participar activamente en foros de seguridad y acceso humanitario a nivel nacional y subnacional.
- Promover la concientización sobre los principios humanitarios (humanidad, imparcialidad, neutralidad e independencia) entre todos los actores relevantes.
- Apoyar en la mediación y resolución de posibles conflictos o malentendidos que puedan surgir, siempre desde un enfoque de respeto y construcción de consensos.
- Facilitar procesos de diálogo intercultural, asegurando que los mensajes se transmitan de manera clara, respetuosa y en los idiomas pertinentes (cuando sea posible).
- Alertar al equipo sobre posibles riesgos culturales, sociales o espirituales asociados a las intervenciones y proponer medidas de mitigación adecuadas.

**Capacitación y Desarrollo:**

- Identificar las necesidades de capacitación en seguridad y acceso para el personal MIHR ELLA y para los socios locales
- Organizar y facilitar sesiones de capacitación y talleres sobre seguridad y acceso humanitario.

**Reporte:**

- Elaborar informes periódicos sobre la situación de seguridad y acceso, incidentes y acciones tomadas.
- Contribuir a los informes internos y externos según sea necesario.

**PERFIL MÍNIMO REQUERIDO**

- Nacional Venezolano

***Formación Profesional:***

- Título universitario en seguridad, estudios de conflicto, relaciones internacionales, ciencias políticas, desarrollo o un campo relacionado.

***Experiencia Profesional***

- Mínimo de 2 años de experiencia relevante en seguridad y acceso humanitario, preferiblemente en contextos complejos o de emergencia.

***Habilidades:***

- Excelentes habilidades de análisis, comunicación y negociación.
- Capacidad probada para trabajar bajo presión y tomar decisiones rápidas.
- Conocimiento profundo de los principios humanitarios y el derecho internacional humanitario.
- Conocimiento profundo del enfoque sensible al conflicto, acción sin daño, enfoque diferencial y edad.
- Fluidez en español oral y escrito. Dominio del inglés será altamente apreciado.
- Habilidades informáticas avanzadas (MS Office, herramientas de mapeo, etc.).

***Competencias:***

- Liderazgo y trabajo en equipo.
- Comunicación efectiva.
- Planificación y organización.
- Toma de decisiones y resolución de problemas.
- Adaptabilidad y flexibilidad.
- Sensibilidad cultural.

***Condiciones de Trabajo:***

- El puesto puede requerir viajes frecuentes a áreas de alto riesgo dentro del país.
- Disponibilidad para trabajar fuera del horario laboral habitual en situaciones de emergencia.

**COORDINACIÓN**

El profesional reportará al Director de Proyecto MIHR ELLA, y coordinará con el Asesor de Seguridad y Acceso.

**SALVAGUARDIA**

Los niños, niñas y los adultos en situación de vulnerabilidad deben estar protegidos en la mayor medida posible de acciones deliberadas o inadvertidas y fallas que los ponen en riesgo de abuso, explotación sexual, lesiones y cualquier otro daño. Una de las formas en que VENGOAL muestra este compromiso continuo con la protección es incluir rigurosos antecedentes y verificaciones de referencia en el proceso de selección para todos los candidatos.

**RESPONSABILIDAD DENTRO DE VENGOAL**

Junto con nuestra política de protección, VENGOAL es un empleador que ofrece igualdad de oportunidades y tiene un conjunto de políticas de integridad. Se espera que cualquier candidato que ofrezca un trabajo con VENGOAL se adhiera a las siguientes áreas clave de responsabilidad:

- Cumplir con las políticas y procedimientos de VENGOAL con respecto a la protección, el Código de Conducta, la salud y la seguridad, la protección de datos y la confidencialidad, los principios de no dañar y los protocolos de comportamiento inaceptables.
- Informar cualquier inquietud sobre el bienestar de un niño o adulto en situación de vulnerabilidad, o cualquier irregularidad dentro de nuestra área de programación.
- Informar cualquier inquietud sobre el comportamiento inapropiado de un personal o socio de VENGOAL.

jobs.title: Associate Programme Management Officer, P2
jobs.description: Org. Setting and Reporting The United Nations Office of Counter-Terrorism (UNOCT) was established by the General Assembly in June 2017. The Office has five main functions: (a) provide leadership on the General Assembly counter-terrorism mandates across the United Nations System; (b) enhance coordination and coherence across the 38 Counter-Terrorism Implementation Task Force entities to ensure the balanced implementation of the four pillars of the Strategy; (c) strengthen the delivery of United Nations counter-terrorism capacity-building assistance to Member States; (d) improve visibility, advocacy and resource mobilization for United Nations counter-terrorism efforts; and (e) ensure that due priority is given to counter-terrorism across the United Nations System and that the important work on preventing violent extremism is firmly rooted in the Strategy. The United Nations Counter-Terrorism Centre (UNCCT) is part of UNOCT and promotes the delivery of United Nations capacity building assistance to Member States. This position is located in the United Nations Counter-Terrorism Centre (UNCCT) within the Office of Counter-Terrorism (UNOCT) premises in Nairobi. The Associate Programme Management Officer will serve within the Unit on Countering Terrorist Use of Weapons, in UNCCT’s Countering Terrorism Section, and will report to the Head of the unit, under the overall supervision of the Chief of the Section. The focus of this job is to support the implementation of the UNCCT Global Programme on Countering Terrorist Use of Weapons, with a special focus on the project on “Supporting Eastern Africa in countering terrorist use of improvised explosive devices (IEDs)”, as well as the operations and other activities in the assigned functional areas. Responsibilities Within delegated authority, the Associate Programme Management Officer will be responsible for the following duties: • Supports the development, implementation and coordination of assigned Weapons Unit’s programme/projects relating to countering terrorist acquisition and use of weapons, with a specific focus on IEDs, etc. • Reviews relevant documents and reports; identifies problems and issues to be addressed and proposes corrective actions. • Supports provision of technical assistance to Member States on issues related to countering terrorist acquisition and use of weapons, including weapons of mass destruction, chemical, biological, radiological, and nuclear materials, small arms and light weapons, IEDs, and unmanned aircraft systems. • Carries out basic research on selected aspects of programmes/project, operations and other activities, etc., to include collecting, analyzing and presenting statistical data and other information gathered from diverse sources. • Provides substantive support for policy coordination and evaluation functions, including the review and analysis of emerging issues and trends in countering terrorist use of weapons, with a special focus on IEDs. • Assists in performing consulting assignments, in collaboration with Member States, International Organizations and UN entities, by planning and facilitating capacity building and awareness raising activities. • Contributes to the preparation of various written outputs, e.g. draft background papers, analytical notes, sections of reports and studies, inputs to Secretary General reports, senior management statements and talking points, publications that relate to countering terrorist use of weapons, etc. • Provides administrative and substantive support to consultative and other meetings, conferences, etc., to include proposing agenda topics, identifying and proposed participants, preparation of background documents and presentations, handling logistics, etc. • Undertakes outreach activities; participates in the development of training workshops, seminars, etc.; participates in and makes presentations on assigned topics/activities. • Participates in field missions, including provision of substantive and administrative support, data collection, etc. • Coordinates activities related to budget funding (programme/project preparation and submissions, progress reports, financial statements, etc.) and preparation of related documents/reports (pledging, work programme, programme budget, etc.). • Performs other duties as required. Competencies PROFESSIONALISM: Knowledge and understanding of a range of issues related to counter-terrorism, and countering terrorist acquisition and use of conventional and non-conventional weapons, weapons of mass destruction, chemical, biological, radiological and nuclear materials, small arms and light weapons, IEDs and unmanned aircraft systems, non-proliferation and disarmament affairs, as well as regional dynamics in Eastern Africa, Ability to identify issues, analyze and participate in the resolution of issues/problems. Ability to assist with data collection using various methods. Conceptual analytical and evaluative skills to conduct independent research and analysis, including familiarity with and experience in the use of various research sources, including electronic sources on the internet, intranet and other databases. Ability to apply judgment in the context of assignments given, plan own work and manage conflicting priorities. Shows pride in work and in achievements; demonstrates professional competence and mastery of subject matter; is conscientious and efficient in meeting commitments, observing deadlines and achieving results; is motivated by professional rather than personal concerns; shows persistence when faced with difficult problems or challenges; remains calm in stressful situations. Takes responsibility for incorporating gender perspectives and ensuring the equal participation of women and men in all areas of work. TEAMWORK: Works collaboratively with colleagues to achieve organizational goals; solicits input by genuinely valuing others’ ideas and expertise; is willing to learn from others; places team agenda before personal agenda; supports and acts in accordance with final group decision, even when such decisions may not entirely reflect own position; shares credit for team accomplishments and accepts joint responsibility for team shortcomings. PLANNING & ORGANIZING: Develops clear goals that are consistent with agreed strategies; identifies priority activities and assignments; adjusts priorities as required; allocates appropriate amount of time and resources for completing work; foresees risks and allows for contingencies when planning; monitors and adjusts plans and actions as necessary; uses time efficiently. Education Advanced university degree (Master’s degree or equivalent) in international relations, law, business administration, management, economics or a related field is required. A first-level university degree in combination with two additional years of qualifying experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree. Job - Specific Qualification Not available. Work Experience A minimum of two years of progressively responsible experience in project/programme management, administration or related area is required. No experience is needed for candidates who have passed the United Nations Young Professionals Programme Examination (YPP) or the G to P Examination (G to P). Experience in dealing with counter-terrorism issues and countering terrorist use of weapons is required. Experience working in international organizations is required. Experience in countering terrorist use of IEDs is desirable. Languages English and French are the working languages of the United Nations Secretariat. For this job opening, English is required. The table below shows the minimum required level for each skill in these languages, according to the UN Language Framework (please consult https://languages.un.org for details). Setting and Reporting The United Nations Department of Safety and Security (UNDSS) is responsible for providing leadership, operational support and oversight of the United Nations Security Management System (UNSMS) globally. As a global leader in security risk management principles, UNDSS enables the safe and effective delivery of United Nations System programmes and activities in the most complex and challenging environments, while maximizing resources. To this end, the work of the Department is aligned under a clear mission, to enable United Nations system operations through trusted security leadership and solutions. This is a unique opportunity to join a diverse, dynamic and exciting organization gaining valuable experience where security provides great value. Besides the opportunity to gain new skills and further advance security expertise, this position offers a fulfilling environment that gives you satisfaction by contributing directly or indirectly to peace and security, human rights, and achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Together, we will make the world a better place. For more information on the Department, and how we make an impact on the world in enabling the achievement of SDGs, visit: https://www.un.org/undss/ This position is located in Gaza, within the UNDSS Israel and Occupied Palestinian Territory (IOPT) Office. Using analytical techniques and collaborative team research, supports planning and ensure awareness of the current trends to enhance or adjust security programmes. • Supports the development of risk management strategies and drives planning using situational awareness, critical thinking, and logic to detect and interpret early signals, emerging trends and analysis of multi-dimensional threats that may impact security. Identifies the strengths and weaknesses of different solutions, conclusions, or approaches to problems. • Prepares, reviews, implements, and supports security planning, security risk management documents and risk management-based security solutions through innovation and creativity. Provides written analysis of security trends and reporting of incidents. Participates in meetings, committees, and task forces, prepares papers on security issues, delivers briefings provides responses, as needed. • Supports the management of security-related projects, prioritizing work to meet deadlines and following defined processes, policies, procedures and guidance, fostering alignment with colleagues and across organizations. • Monitors and contributes to activities that relate to the implementation and evaluation of preparedness and compliance; drives results that help support efficiency and effectiveness of operations. • Enhances communication and trust through active collaboration, consultation and exchanges with agencies, funds, and programmes and other stakeholders, for information sharing, coordination of responses, provision of security briefings, taking into account operational activities and risks. • Strengthens awareness and capacity of relevant personnel by supporting the development, updates and delivery of contextually relevant security training and advice. • Assesses prevailing local security conditions, identifying security trends and advising UN staff, project personnel and dependents on potential security problems., such as, kidnapping, armed attacks, arrest and detention. • Conducts security surveys and assessments, creatively leveraging tools and processes, identifying and recommending the simplest, reasonable, effective and efficient security measures, including when there is incomplete, contradictory and/or fluid information. • Supports organizational resilience and contingency planning, crisis decision-making, and the development of disaster recovery and business continuity plans, by providing information and analysis including situational monitoring and updates. Assists with internally relocating personnel and assets in a conflict zone or supporting the development and implementation of evacuation plans from a country. • Maintains an ongoing evaluation of air, land and all evacuation routes and resources for use in emergencies, ensuring the availability of vehicles, aircraft, vessels, fuel supply and assessable roads. • Provides support to establishing and maintaining a functioning Security Communication System making periodic checks to determine if system is functioning properly; arranges for necessary repairs or adjustments. • Leads after action and fact-finding reviews on security-related incidents involving UN staff members, project personnel or eligible dependent as well as accidents involving UN vehicles and prepares report of findings. • Actively implements departmental approaches to mainstreaming gender, diversity and inclusion into all aspects of the work as well as ensuring the implementation of people-centred security risk management approaches considering specific threats or vulnerabilities of personnel and adapting practices and measures in support of diversity and inclusion. • Performs other functions as may be assigned by the PSA and/or Chief SIOC. Takes responsibility for incorporating different perspectives and ensuring the equal participation of women and men in all areas of work. Contributes to an environment in which others can talk and act without fear of repercussion; places confidence in and builds trust with colleagues and stakeholders. Demonstrates effective interpersonal skills and emotional intelligence, including self-awareness and contextual intelligence. Shows openness to learning and commitment to self-development. Identifies issues, researches, collects data, demonstrates situational awareness, conceptual analytical and evaluative skills and participates in the resolution of issues/problems demonstrating critical thinking, perceptiveness, judgement and decision-making. Demonstrates an ability to implement policies. Ability to make quick decisions in emergencies or when rapid response is needed. Communicates complex concepts effectively both verbally and in writing. Shows pride in work and in achievements. Demonstrates professional competence and mastery of subject matter. Is conscientious and efficient in meeting commitments, observing deadlines and achieving results. Shows ability to prioritize, manage, and implement multiple high-level projects in a timely manner, even in fast-changing contexts. Is motivated by professional rather than personal concerns. Takes ownership of accountability and supports strategies to ensure compliance with all security risk management decisions and regulations. Shows persistence when faced with difficult problems or challenges; remains calm in stressful situations; Takes responsibility for incorporating gender perspectives and ensuring the equal participation of women and men in all areas of work. Able to analyze and interpret data in support of decision-making and convey resulting information to management. Communication: Speaks and writes clearly and effectively; listens to others, correctly interprets messages from others and responds appropriately; asks questions to clarify and exhibits interest in having two-way communication; tailors language, tone, style and format to match audience; demonstrates openness in sharing information and keeping people informed. Client Orientation: Considers all those to whom services are provided to be “clients” and seeks to see things from clients’ point of view; establishes and maintains productive partnerships with clients by gaining their trust and respect; identifies clients’ needs and matches them to appropriate solutions; monitors ongoing developments inside and outside the clients’ environment to keep informed and anticipate problems; keeps clients informed of progress or setbacks in projects; meets timeline for delivery of products or services to client. Education Advanced university degree (Master’s degree or equivalent) in business or public administration, political/social science, psychology, criminal justice, law, international relations, security management or a related field is required. A relevant first-level university degree in combination with two years of qualifying experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree. A first-level university degree may be substituted with a diploma from a police or military education institution, college or academy obtained over a minimum of a three-year period. Job - Specific Qualification Not available. Work Experience A minimum of five years of progressively responsible experience in international relations, disarmament affairs, conflict resolution, crime or terrorism prevention, security, risk or disaster or emergency management and preparedness in the public or private sector areas responsible for responding to emergency situations that directly impact security is required. One year of experience in the last three in leading the drafting of security plans including Relocation Plans, Evacuation Plans, Incident Response Plans and CASEVAC & MEDEVAC Plans in a conflict environment is required. Experience in operational coordination and security support to UN entities, including Agencies, Funds and Programmes, and to INGOs or Saving Lives Together partner organizations to enable humanitarian operations in a conflict environment is required. Experience in using applied analytical, information management to advance decisions, strategies and execution is required. At least two (2) years of experience in the last five years working within the UN Common System or comparable international organization or nongovernmental organization in a conflict or post-conflict environment, out of which one year at the international level is desirable. Experience in stakeholder consultations for security planning, security operations, production of security risk assessments or analysis is desirable. This is a unique opportunity to join a diverse, dynamic and exciting organization gaining unique and valuable experience where security provides great value. Experience maintaining and coordinating a database and digital archives and production of data-driven incident reporting is required. Experience in substantive engagement, information-sharing and/or coordination and liaison with the United Nations or similar international organization and International Non-Governmental Organization (INGO) is required. Experience in using applied analytical, information management to advance decisions, strategies and execution is required. Experience with conducting risk analysis and providing assessments of conflict dynamics in the Middle East-North Africa (MENA) region is desirable. Experience, in the last three years, in contributing to design and planning of risk mitigation strategies, including area security plans, Standard Operating Practices, or security risk management (SRM) for humanitarian operations is desirable. Takes responsibility for incorporating different perspectives and ensuring the equal participation of women and men in all areas of work. jobs.title: Programme Management Officer (One Portfolio Investment Model Enhancement), P4
jobs.description: Org. Setting and Reporting The United Nations Secretary-General is responsible for the investment of the assets of the United Nations Joint Staff Pension Fund (UNJSPF). The RSG heads the Office of Investment Management (OIM), which manages a $100+ billion multi-asset class, global investment portfolio, about 85% of which is actively managed in-house. Asset classes under management comprise global equities, fixed income, foreign exchange, private equity, real estate, infrastructure, timber and commodities. OIM's staff are all based in New York but come from over 40 countries. For more information, please visit OIM's website at https://oim.unjspf.org/. Ability to analyze complex issues, identify practical solutions and produce clear, audit-ready documentation. Ability to conduct data collection using various methods. Conceptual analytical and evaluative skills to conduct independent research and analysis, including familiarity with and experience in the use of various research sources, including electronic sources on the internet, intranet and other databases. Ability to apply judgment in the context of assignments given, plan own work and manage conflicting priorities. Shows pride in work and in achievements; demonstrates professional competence and mastery of subject matter; is conscientious and efficient in meeting commitments, observing deadlines and achieving results; is motivated by professional rather than personal concerns; shows persistence when faced with difficult problems or challenges; remains calm in stressful situations. Takes responsibility for incorporating gender perspectives and ensuring the equal participation of women and men in all areas of work. Able to analyze and interpret data in support of decision-making and convey resulting information to management. • Teamwork: Works collaboratively with colleagues to achieve organizational goals; solicits input by genuinely valuing others’ ideas and expertise; is willing to learn from others; places team agenda before personal agenda; supports and acts in accordance with final group decision, even when such decisions may not entirely reflect own position; shares credit for team accomplishments and accepts joint responsibility for team shortcomings. • Planning& Organizing: Develops clear goals that are consistent with agreed strategies; identifies priority activities and assignments; adjusts priorities as required; allocates appropriate amount of time and resources for completing work; foresees risks and allows for contingencies when planning; monitors and adjusts plans and actions as necessary; uses time efficiently. A first-level university degree in combination with qualifying experience may be accepted in lieu of the advanced university degree. Job - Specific Qualification Not available. Work Experience A minimum of seven years of progressively responsible experience in project or programme management, investment, organizational change, governance or a related area is required. Experience delivering organizational or governance transformation in institutional or client engagements is required. Listens to others, correctly interprets messages from others and responds appropriately. Asks questions to clarify, and exhibits interest in having two-way communication. Tailors language, tone, style and format to match the audience. Demonstrates openness in sharing information and keeping people informed. Education Advanced university degree (Master’s degree or equivalent) in human rights, law, political science, international relations, social sciences, economics, public policy, sustainable development, humanitarian affairs or related field. At least 5 years of demonstrated knowledge of human rights monitoring, documentation, analysis, research and reporting methodologies, including planning, coordinating and conducting field missions is required. Skills in drafting human rights reports, policy and other documents is required. At least 5 years of demonstrated knowledge of international human rights law, norms, and standards is desirable. Knowledge of international humanitarian law and its application is desirable. Knowledge of Sexual and Gender-Based Violence (SGBV) and related frameworks is desirable. For this job opening, English is required.
