jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

General Assembly Resolution 2186 (XXI) decided to “bring into operations the United Nations Capital Development Fund as an organ of the General Assembly which shall function as an autonomous organization of the United Nations. The UN Capital Development Fund (UNCDF) assists developing countries, especially least developing countries, in the development of their economies by supplementing existing sources of capital assistance by means of grants, loans, and guarantees. UNCDFs vision is to help mobilize and catalyze an increase of capital flows for SDG impactful investments to Member States to address the most pressing development challenges facing vulnerable communities in these countries and thereby contribute to sustainable economic growth and equitable prosperity.

As a Flagship Catalytic Blended Financing platform of the UN, UNCDF utilizes its unique capability in the UN system to deploy grants, loans and guarantees to crowd-in finance for the scaling of development impact. UNCDF focuses on where the needs are greatest, a deliberate focus and capability rooted in UNCDF’s unique investment mandate to support the achievement of the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development and the realization of the Doha Programme of Action for the least developed countries, 2022–2031.

As per its Strategic Framework, UNCDF works to deploy its functions as a hybrid development organization and development finance institution. UNCDF responds to Member States requests for assistance by providing targeted technical and financial advisory services on investments for development outcomes, designing bespoke financial structuring solutions, undertaking financial derisking of investments, and enhancing investment readiness of SDG aligned projects in partnership with private sector, UNOs, International and Local Finance Institutions, Development Finance Institutions as well as Foundations and Philanthropy, among others. UNCDF works to develop local financial systems, new markets and mobilize and crowd in capital from public and private sources. UNCDF is driven by a partnership mindset which enables it to deploy its different capital capabilities in highly tailored and responsive ways in order to mobilize investments flows from other sources, in particular from the private sector. By structuring transactions which are highly impactful, but also recognize the need for multiplying the impact of its own capital, UNCDF seeks to position itself as a preferred partner for different stakeholders. UNCDF’s work is focused on three priority areas, including:

• SME Finance

• Sub-National Finance

• Digital Finance

UNCDF’s organizational set up includes an Investment and Implementation Division (IID), Investment and Finance Oversight Division (IFOD), Operations and Oversight Division (OOD) and a Directorate of the Executive Office. UNCDF staff and personnel are located in regional hubs based in Dakar (Senegal), Nairobi (Kenya) and Bangkok (Thailand) with sub-regional presence in a number of locations in the Caribbean and Pacific Regions. UNCDF is led by an Executive Secretary based out of New York, USA. Pursuant to General Assembly resolution 2321(XXII, para 1.a), the Administrator of the UNDP performs the function of the Managing Director of UNCDF. UNCDF is overseen by an Executive Board comprised of UN Member States.

Duties and Responsibilities

Under the supervision of the Regional Investment Specialist for the Pacific and in close collaboration with programme, investment and operations colleagues, the Project Associate will provide operational, administrative and financial support for UNCDF ongoing initiatives implemented in the Pacific region. The Associate will support operational coordination, procurement, financial administration, logistics and partner coordination activities across project implementation in the Pacific countries.

1. Provide operational and administrative support for programme implementation

- Support day-to-day operational and administrative activities for the various initiatives in the Pacific region.

- Assist in the implementation of procurement plans, travel arrangements, and operational schedules.

- Provide administrative support for meetings, workshops, missions and programme events in a gender-sensitive manner, promoting inclusive participation, and addressing the specific needs of all genders.

- Coordinate travel logistics and related administrative requirements for programme personnel and consultants.

- Provide administrative and operational support to procurement activities, including supporting procurement planning, document preparation and initial review within requesting teams, vendor liaison for micro-purchasing cases where required, procurement tracking against plans, and records management, ensuring compliance with UNCDF and UNDP policies and procedures

- Maintain filing systems and documentation for operational and administrative records.

- Support asset management and inventory tracking related to programme activities.

- Follow up on operational requests, approvals and administrative actions required for programme implementation.

- Supports the travel and logistic arrangements, including travel transaction reconciliation as well as supplier registration and maintenance Collaborates and leads to ensure the continuity of office maintenance through related services providers.

2. Provide financial and compliance support for programme activities

- Support budget tracking and expenditure monitoring for UNCDF projects in the Pacific.

- Assist in preparation of financial reports and supporting documentation in line with UNCDF and donor requirements.

- Support processing payments, vendor invoices and financial transactions through corporate systems.

- Ensure operational and financial processes comply with UNCDF and donor rules and procedures.

- Support tracking and management of partner agreements, procurement contracts and related documentation.

- Support the review of project balances, cash availability, and other financial data; flag any discrepancies to the supervisor.

- Generate standard financial reports from corporate systems to support monitoring and planning.

- Support project and award management activities in Quantum.

- Support in budget revisions, project extensions and related financial actions.

- Support delivery rates, commitments and available balances to ensure efficient utilization of project resources

3. Support coordination and partnership engagement

- Support coordination with implementing partners, consultants, government counterparts and service providers on operational matters.

- Assist in organizing meetings, workshops and stakeholder consultations.

- Support preparation of meeting minutes, briefing materials and administrative correspondence.

- Coordinate with programme, finance and procurement teams to support timely implementation of activities.

- Provide administrative support for onboarding of consultants and project personnel.

- Support logistical arrangements for knowledge-sharing and learning activities.

4. Support operational reporting and documentation

- Maintain operational trackers, procurement monitoring tools and programme records for UNCDF projects in the Pacific.

- Support preparation of operational and administrative reports as required.

- Ensure proper filing, archiving and efficient retrieval of operational and financial documentation.

- Support consolidation of supporting documents for donor reporting and programme reviews.

- Assist in tracking procurement timelines and operational deliverables across the Pacific countries.

- Support continuous improvement of operational processes and administrative workflows where required.

- Provide administrative support during audits, programmatic reviews and verification exercises.

- Maintain accurate operational and financial records to support reporting and compliance requirements.

5. Support knowledge building, knowledge sharing and capacity building relevant to the project.

- Participate in training and organize briefings on internal procedures for the project personnel. Provide support to other capacity building activities, including to the design and delivery of tools, materials for workshops, or platforms that tap into the collective intelligence of communities and mobilize action.

- Provide support in the dissemination and sharing of relevant data and lessons learned within the CO and regionally. Keep pulse on emerging best practices nationally, regionally, and internationally that relate to the work of the assigned project.

- Make sound contributions to knowledge networks and communities of practice. Support compiling and systematizing project knowledge, products and tools as well as their wide distribution to partners.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

Institutional Arrangement

The Project Associate will carry out relevant duties under the guidance and direct supervision of the Regional Investment Specialist for the Pacific with matrix reporting to the Regional Operational Effectiveness and Assurance Specialist.

The Project Associate will have regular communication with the relevant staff via email and messaging apps, for coordination and guidance purposes, ensuring output quality and targets.

About Travel:

a) UNCDF will cover the cost of travel as required during the assignment

b) As per need, the incumbent will be required to travel to any of the countries in which UNCDF is implementing project activities in the Pacific.

Competencies

Core Competencies - UNDP Core Competencies can be found here.

Achieve Results:

LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline

Think Innovatively:

LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvement

Learn Continuously:

LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback

LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible

Accounting (General)

Financial reporting and analysis

Understands changes in regulatory, legal and ethical frameworks and standards for financial reporting in the public sector. Ability to extract, evaluate financial data, derive relevant findings and present them in a meaningful and coherent manner to facilitate effective decision making and performance monitoring. Understands the benefits of integrated reporting, including non-financial resources such as human, social and intellectual capital, and environmental and governance performance.

Finance

Banking and cash management

Ability to collect, handle, and manage cash, which involves assessing market liquidity, cash flow, and investments.

Finance

Management and cost accounting

Ability to produce periodic qualitative and quantitative performance reports to facilitate effective decision making and performance monitoring. Ability to use a range of costing techniques and analyses cost related data to provide quantitative information to the users of reports.

Business Management

Communicate in a clear, concise and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience.

Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media and other appropriate channels.

Business Management

Customer Satisfaction/Client Management

Ability to respond timey and appropriately with a sense of urgency, provide consistent solutions, and deliver timely and quality results and/or solutions to fulfil and understand the real customers' needs.

Provide inputs to the development of customer service strategy

requests. Ability to anticipate client's upcoming needs and concerns.

Required Skills and Experience

Experience:

Required skills and competencies:

Desired skills in addition to the competencies covered in the Competencies section:

- Experience in managing complex operations, financial and administrative processes within environment, natural resources, climate change and related projects, combined with ability to prepare high quality documentation on budgetary and financial matters, briefing notes, analytical summaries, and accounting spreadsheets.

jobs.title: Small Grants Programme Coordinator [Open to internal and external candidates]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

UNDP Eswatini is initiating Eswatini Country Programme 2026–2030. As part of this programme UNDP will concentrate on two mutually reinforcing priorities: (1) good governance and social cohesion—strengthening accountable, transparent and people-centered institutions, expanding access to justice and human rights, bolstering anti-corruption and oversight, and improving public service delivery (including through digitalization and citizen feedback); and (2) sustainable and resilient economic development—advancing inclusive, green and digital growth by supporting MSME development, entrepreneurship and decent jobs (especially for youth, women and vulnerable groups), while building climate and environmental resilience through nature-positive development, circular economy approaches and a just energy transition, alongside efforts to mobilize innovative financing for implementation. Within the Sustainable and resilient development portfolio, UNDP will be executing the Global Environment Facility (GEF) Small Grants Programme (SGP).

The Global Environment Facility (GEF) Small Grants Programme (SGP) is implemented by UNDP on behalf of the GEF Partnership. UNDP oversees the Small Grants Programme (SGP) through the Vertical Hub and the Nature Hub of Bureau for Policy and Programme Support (BPPS). Funded by the Global Environment Facility (GEF), the Small Grants Programme efficiently channels direct grants to non-governmental and community-based organizations to help them cope with climate change; conserve biodiversity; protect international waters; reduce the impact of Persistent Organic Pollutants; and prevent land degradation. Helping communities with their initiatives for sustainable livelihoods while generating global environmental benefits is the core inspiration of the Small Grants Programme.

Launched in 1992 as a corporate programme of the GEF, the GEF Small Grants Programme (GEF SGP) has supported local action for over thirty years to address global environmental concerns. SGP aims to deliver global environmental benefits in the GEF focal areas of biodiversity conservation, climate change mitigation, protection of international waters, prevention of land degradation, and elimination of persistent organic pollutants through community-based approaches. To date, SGP has funded over 29,000 community-based projects covering more than 120 countries. It has gained considerable experiences at the community level, including adapting to climate change while addressing issues of the GEF focal areas. Further information can be found at: https://sgp.undp.org/.

The SGP Programme in Eswatini has been implemented over the past 2 years under the oversight of UNOPS Regional Office, with 1 UNOPS contracted staff embedded within UNDP. As the Programme transitions to UNDP full oversight in 2026, UNDP Eswatini is recruiting a National Coordinator to coordinate the SGP in Eswatini.

Duties and Responsibilities

The National Coordinator will report through a matrixed structure to both the Deputy Resident Representative and the SGP Regional Programme Specialist. The coordinator will work on a day-to-day basis within the Sustainable Development Portfolio of UNDP under the oversight of the Sustainable Development Specialist to ensure synergies and coordination within the overall environment, climate and nature portfolio of UNDP. The Coordinator will be responsible for overseeing the implementation of the SGP at country level, while dedicating approximately 50% of their time to support implementation other country office locally-led initiative on adaptation and resilience, with particular focus on the grants element, including grant pipeline development, appraisal support, grantee capacity strengthening, milestone-based disbursement follow-up, grant monitoring, reporting and learning.

Ensure effective management of the SGP Country Programme team

- Liaise with the Sustainable Development/Environment Programme Assistant for administrative support in relation to SGP programming;

- Promote and maintain effective teamwork within the SGP Country Programme and wider Environment portfolio team, the National Steering Committee members, and with the UNDP CO team;

- Prepare and implement annual work plan, including strategic and/or innovative initiatives, with set delivery and co-financing targets; draft annual SGP Country Office administrative and project operational budget proposal;

- Set annual performance parameters and learning objectives for the SGP Country Programme team, assess their performance and provide feedback.

Ensure Programme/Portfolio Development and Management

- Keep abreast of national environmental concerns and priorities as well as the socio-economic conditions and trends as they relate to the SGP and assess their impact on SGP’s work and programme.

- Ensure formulation and implementation of the Country Programme Strategy (CPS), and its periodic review and update.

- Ensure the Country Programme Strategy (CPS) and annual workplans integrate gender analysis, clear gender equality actions, and measurable targets (including for women-led/women-benefiting initiatives), aligned to UNDP and national gender priorities.

- Manage the SGP grant allocations and country operating budget, maintain the financial integrity of the programme by ensuring adherence to SGP Standard Operating Procedures as well as UNDP rules and regulations, and ensure timely and effective use of SGP resources.

- Exercise quality control over the development of a portfolio of project ideas and concepts and closely monitor the programme implementation progress and results.

- Organize periodic stakeholder workshops and project development sessions for civil society organizations (CSOs) and local communities, and potential applicants and other stakeholders to inform about SGP and its Strategic Initiatives.

- Design and deliver capacity development and communications in gender-responsive ways (e.g., convenient timing/locations, accessible formats/languages, safe spaces), to enable meaningful participation of women and marginalized groups.

- Work closely with Civil Society Organizations (CSOs) and Community-based Organizations (CBOs) in preparation of project concepts and proposals to ensure that projects fit with the SGP Strategic Initiatives, Country Programme Strategy, and technical guidance notes;

- Authorize and manage project planning grants as required.

- Oversee ongoing SGP grant projects and conduct periodic project monitoring field visits and provide technical and operational support and guidance to SGP grantees as required.

- During monitoring visits, assess gender-related results and risks, support corrective actions, and document lessons on what works to advance gender equality in community-based environmental action.

- Plan and serve as secretary to the National Steering Committee meetings. Support and closely coordinate with the National Steering Committee and Technical Advisory Group where relevant, in the process of project proposal review, selection and approval, especially the initial appraisal of proposals and assessment of eligibility.

- Promote gender-responsive grantmaking by applying gender considerations in calls for proposals, appraisal tools and selection processes, and by advising the National Steering Committee on gender equality gaps, risks and opportunities in the portfolio.

- Foster programme, project, and policy linkages between the SGP and the full or medium-sized GEF projects, planned or underway in the country, as well as those of other government, donors and development partners.

- Report periodically to the Central Programme Management Team (CPMT) on programme implementation status, including annual monitoring reporting, financial reporting, audit, and update the relevant SGP databases.

- Undertake monitoring and evaluation of SGP Country Programme and projects, and grant maker initiatives, in coordination with National Steering Committee (NSC) and CPMT.

- Perform and coordinate administrative tasks (i.e. procurement, travel) adhering to SGP SOPs procurement rules and regulation, as required for programme implementation.

Support implementation of grassroot level adaptation interventions under the Environment Portfolio (50% level of effort)

- Support the Sustainable Development Specialist and UNDP Country Office in the effective in-country implementation of adaptation grants, ensuring complementarity between the SGP grant portfolio and the UNDP’s other country initiatives on adaptation, catchment resilience, and nature-based solutions objectives.

- Support coordination of the grants pipeline for country adaptation and resilience grant, including targeted outreach to eligible community-based organizations, civil society organizations, cooperatives and other local entities; support preparation of concept notes and proposals aligned to Catchment Investment Programme priorities and agreed grant criteria.

- Provide technical and operational support to the review, appraisal and documentation of grant proposals, ensuring consistency with partner/donor requirements, UNDP Low-Value Grant procedures, social and environmental safeguards, gender and inclusion standards, and fiduciary due diligence.

- Strengthen grantee capacities in project design, financial management, procurement planning, safeguards, gender-responsive implementation, monitoring, reporting and verification, with particular attention to women, youth and vulnerable groups participating in locally led adaptation initiatives.

- Conduct field monitoring and quality assurance visits for country office initiatives on adaptation, catchment resilience, and nature-based solutions, document progress against agreed outputs and indicators, identify implementation risks and lessons learned, and support adaptive management by grantees and catchment-level stakeholders.

- Prepare timely inputs for donor/partner reporting, audits, knowledge products and regional learning processes, including evidence on grant results, beneficiary reach, safeguards compliance, gender-responsive outcomes, co-financing and sustainability prospects.

Gender mainstreaming (cross-cutting responsibility)

- Integrate gender equality and women’s empowerment considerations across SGP and other locally led adaptation and resilience initiatives’ planning, grantmaking, implementation, monitoring and reporting, in line with UNDP gender policies and the SGP strategic framework.

- Identify and address gender-related barriers to accessing SGP and in other locally-led Adaptation resources (e.g., information, land/asset access, time burdens, mobility, digital access), including through targeted outreach and capacity support for women-led organizations and groups.

- Ensure SGP and Locally Led Adaptation processes and partner engagements are risk-informed and safeguarding-sensitive, including attention to prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse/sexual harassment (SEA/SH) and appropriate referral pathways in line with UNDP requirements.

Resource Mobilization and Partnerships

- Establish and maintain close working relationships with stakeholders as well as promote the value, comparative advantages, and ensure visibility of the SGP.

- Assess interest and priorities of key donors and other development partners and develop/update and implement the resource mobilization and partnership strategy to mobilize resources from and develop partnerships with the government, donors and other partners to best leverage SGP resources and develop programme level partnerships.

- Support SGP grantees in securing co-financing and project level partnerships and assist in identifying opportunities and resources for sustaining and scaling up projects.

- Mobilize resources and partnerships that explicitly support gender-responsive community climate and biodiversity solutions, including engagement with women’s organizations and gender machinery where relevant.

Facilitate Knowledge Management and Communication

- Document programme/project stories, lessons learned, and best practices in SGP programme/project development, implementation, and oversight.

- Access SGP and other global and regional knowledge, distill best practices and facilitate their dissemination and incorporation within SGP Country Programme and projects, UNDP CO, and to counterparts and partners;

- Support capacity building and networking of grantees to facilitate knowledge exchange, and promote uptake through Knowledge platforms, Knowledge fairs etc.

Office/Unit/Project Description

The Volunteer Services Centre (VSC), part of UNV’s Management Services, supports a growing global portfolio of over 15,000 UN Volunteers (2025), delivering timely and high-quality services across the full volunteer lifecycle. This includes recruitment, pre-assignment processing, contract administration, payroll, separation, and evacuation support for UN Volunteers serving with UN agencies, funds, programmes, and missions. With a presence in 13 locations worldwide, VSC ensures consistent and compliant service delivery across diverse operational contexts.

Under the guidance and supervision of the Operations Associate/Team Leader (G7) for the duty station, the Operations Associate supports the delivery of end-to-end volunteer lifecycle services within the VSC. The role contributes to timely onboarding, contract administration, and accurate management of benefits & entitlements, and lifecycle events.

The incumbent ensures the integrity, transparency, and accuracy of service delivery in line with the UN Volunteers Conditions of Service (COS), policies, and procedures, while maintaining high-quality outputs and consistency across multiple countries and stakeholders.

VSC collaborates closely with the Volunteer Solutions Section (VSS), headquarter units, Regional Offices, Field Units, the UNDP Global Shared Services Centre, and other UN partners to deliver coordinated services. The Operations Associate advises stakeholders on policies and procedures, promotes a collaborative and client-focused approach, and supports the timely implementation of the VSC work plan.

Scope of work

- Verify quality and consistency of Description of Assignments (DOAs), and provide guidance on designing DOAs to UN host entities, UNV Regional Offices and Field Units;

- Advertise relevant assignments in line with established processes;

- Identify suitable candidates for UN Volunteer assignments in diverse areas of expertise and for various host entities, as per corporate Key Performance Indicators, and according to DOA requirements and in compliance with UNV’s Recruitment and Selection policy;

- Alert supervisor about deficiencies or risks, liaise with Regional Offices and Field Units on exceptional situations and provide guidance on applicable regulations, rules and policies to ensure full compliance with accountability framework;

- Keep relevant parties updated on status of identification and negotiate adjustments when required;

- Contribute to a fair workload distribution by supporting the identification and submission of candidates for UN Volunteer assignments across regions when needed;

- Record actions and data in the volunteer management systems;

- Ensure accurate data management in official databases;

- Facilitate timely resolution of queries related to volunteer recruitment.

3.2 Outreach and support to talent acquisition

- Coordinate with the Volunteer Solutions Section, Regional Offices and Field Units to remain informed of evolving demand for UN Volunteer profiles;

- Use social media and other sourcing channels to identify candidates, identify gaps in the existing talent pool, and support regional and national outreach campaigns and networks of talent sources in coordination with the Talent Acquisition team and relevant communication colleagues;

- Manage communication with candidates as it relates to the outcome of their applications;

- Capture and share lessons learnt from candidate identification; contribute to knowledge networks and communities of practice; and provide input on recruitment policies, systems and processes to improve the timeliness and quality of VSC services;

Background

Job Purpose and Organizational Context

UNDP is the knowledge frontier organization for sustainable development in the UN Development System and serves as the integrator for collective action to realize the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). UNDP's policy work carried out at HQ, Regional and Country Office levels, forms a contiguous spectrum of deep local knowledge to cutting-edge global perspectives and advocacy. In this context, UNDP invests in the Global Policy Network (GPN), a network of field-based and global technical expertise across a wide range of knowledge domains and in support of the signature solutions and organizational capabilities envisioned in the Strategic Plan.

Within the GPN, the Bureau for Policy and Programme Support (BPPS) has the responsibility for developing all relevant policy and guidance to support the results of UNDP's Strategic Plan. BPPS's staff provides technical advice to Country Offices, advocates for UNDP corporate messages, represents UNDP at multi-stakeholder fora including public-private dialogues, government and civil society dialogues, and engages in UN inter-agency coordination in specific thematic areas. BPPS works closely with UNDP's Crisis Bureau (CB) to support emergency and crisis response. BPPS ensures that issues of risk are fully integrated into UNDP's development programmes. BPPS assists UNDP and partners to achieve higher quality development results through an integrated approach that links results-based management and performance monitoring with more effective and new ways of working. BPPS supports UNDP and partners to be more innovative, knowledge and data-driven including in its programme support efforts.

UNDP has achieved significant progress in making gender equality and women’s empowerment integral to its work on human development. It’s Gender Equality Strategy 2026-2029 builds on the lessons and achievements of previous gender equality strategies and advances gender equality as a core accelerator of human development. The Strategy aims to support governments in transforming the systems, institutions, and power structures that perpetuate gender inequalities by placing gender equality at the center of political, economic, and environmental decision-making.

The Gender Team (BPPS) has the leading role in the implementation of the Gender Equality Strategy 2026-2029. The Gender Equality Global Programme (GEGP) serves as a key vehicle for advancing this agenda, including Outcome 1: Economies are inclusive, and women are economically empowered. Under this outcome, UNDP supports countries in developing and implementing gender-responsive economic and fiscal policies, strengthening public finance systems, expanding investments in the care economy, and generating evidence on the impacts of taxation, public expenditure, and social protection policies on gender equality. Through research, policy advisory services, and capacity development, the Programme contributes to ensuring that public resources and fiscal reforms support more inclusive, equitable, and sustainable development outcomes for gender equality.

Duties and Responsibilities

The Econometrician, under the supervision of the Gender Specialist on Inclusive Economies, will:

- Ensure the application of econometric analysis and quantitative research to advance Inclusive Economies:

- Design and apply econometric and quantitative methods to assess impacts of economic, social and distributional outcomes related to inequality, care systems and gender equality.

- Conduct impact evaluations, causal inference studies, forecasting exercises, and scenario analyses to generate evidence on inclusive economic development.

- Contribute to the preparation of technical reports, policy briefs, research papers and knowledge products to support evidence-based policy making.

- Produce analytical reports, technical papers, policy briefs, visualizations, and presentations that translate complex quantitative findings into actionable policy recommendations

- Collaborate with national stakeholders and development partners to strengthen the use of data and evidence in advancing inclusive economies.

2. Ensure the application of quantitative models, data systems and analytical tools:

- Design and implement econometric models, simulations and statistical analyses to evaluate the effectiveness and distributional impacts of economic and social policies.

- Apply econometric methods to assess the effectiveness of public policies and investments aimed at reducing inequalities and promoting inclusive development outcomes.

- Develop analytical outputs, visualizations and technical documentation to communicate findings to policymakers and other stakeholders.

- Synthesize emerging evidence, global best practices, and lessons learned in feminist economics, care policy, economic inclusion, and social development.

3. Ensure the development of monitoring, evaluation and indicator frameworks:

- Support the design of indicators and measurement frameworks to assess progress on inclusive economic development, gender equality, care systems and crisis recovery.

- Develop statistical and econometric approaches for tracking policy outcomes, programme effectiveness, and socio-economic impacts across diverse populations.

- Support the development and implementation of monitoring and evaluation frameworks, methodologies, and results-based management systems.

- Contribute to the development of methodological guidance and tools for measuring economic inclusion, care outcomes, resilience, and social well-being.

4. Provide support for the implementation of the Gender Team’s priorities related to inclusive economies and gender equality and facilitate knowledge sharing

- Support the development of policy recommendations, technical guidance, and knowledge products to strengthen inclusive and equitable economic outcomes.

- Contribute to the development and tracking of indicators, data systems, and results frameworks to monitor progress and inform decision-making.

- Contribute to regional and global knowledge networks and communities of practice focused on inclusive economies.

- Participate in knowledge-sharing initiatives and support the dissemination of evidence, lessons learned, and good practices to advance inclusive economies.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization.

The Econometrician works under the general supervision of the Gender Specialist on Inclusive Economies.

jobs.description:
Aproximaci6n por Niveles (Tiered Approach)

De acuerdo con el compromiso de salvaguardar capacidad y apoyar al personal actual de la Organizaci6n, la mayoria de vacantes de PNUD/UNCDF/UNV se han anunciado utilizando un proceso de aplicaci6n por niveles (tiers) en donde:

- Nivel 1: Otro personal del PNUD/UNCDFNNU con nombramientos permanentes (PA) y de plazo fijo (FTA)

- Nivel 2: personal del PNUD/UNCDFNNU con nombramientos temporales (TA), personal con contratos PSA regulares y Voluntarios Expertos y Eespecialistas de las Naciones Unidas •

- Nivel 3 o 0 sin nivel indicado: todos los demás tipos de contratos del PNUD/UNCDF/VNU y de otros organismos, y demás candidatos externos Por favor tenga en cuenta del nivel(es) indicado(s) en el título de la vacante, si Io hay, y asegurese de que cumple con la elegibilidad para aplicar.

I. Descripción de la oficina/proyecto:

El PNUD es la principal organización de las Naciones Unidas en la lucha para poner fin a la injusticia de la pobreza, la desigualdad y el cambio climático. Trabajando con nuestra amplia red de expertos y socios en 170 países, ayudamos a las naciones a construir soluciones integradas y duraderas para las personas y el planeta.

El PNUD trabaja en más de 170 países y territorios, dando asistencia para desarrollar políticas, habilidades de liderazgo y asociación, capacidades institucionales y construcción de resiliencia, fomentando el desarrollo humano sostenible. En Panamá trabaja a nivel nacional, nivel municipal y comarcal. El PNUD hace parte de las Agencias, Fondos y Programas de las Naciones Unidas en Panamá aportando al logro del Marco de Cooperación de las Naciones Unidas para el Desarrollo Sostenible (UNSDCF en inglés).

Por más de 50 años, el Programa de las Naciones Unidas (PNUD) ha sido un aliado estratégico de Panamá, centrándose en soluciones integradas y alineadas con las prioridades nacionales, apoyando la gestión, implementación y ejecución de programas y proyectos en beneficio de las personas.

El PNUD en Panamá está organizado en tres grupos programáticos que coordinan más de 40 proyectos en todo el territorio nacional:

- Igualdad e inclusión social, económica y ambiental

- Gobernabilidad, paz y derechos humanos

- Cambio climático, gestión integral ambiental y reducción de riesgos y desastres

En el PNUD, la gestión basada en resultados, la igualdad de género, los derechos humanos, el enfoque multidimensional, el desarrollo territorial, la innovación, digitalización y el uso de nuevas tecnologías son transversales en todas nuestras áreas de trabajo y proyectos.

Dentro del Clúster de Igualdad e Inclusión Social, Económica y Ambiental, se brinda asistencia al Gobierno de Panamá en alineamiento con el Marco de Cooperación de las Naciones Unidas para el Desarrollo Sostenible en Panamá 2026-2030 y el Plan Estratégico del PNUD 2026-2030, los cuales destacan la necesidad de fortalecer el capital humano, reducir las desigualdades y apoyar la innovación y el crecimiento sostenible.

El proyecto “Latidos del Barrio: Cultura que Transforma Comunidades” es una iniciativa impulsada por el Ministerio de Cultura con apoyo del PNUD, orientada a fortalecer la inclusión social, la cohesión comunitaria, la participación ciudadana, el acceso a servicios culturales y formativos, la activación deportiva y la economía creativa en territorios priorizados. El proyecto operará mediante una Unidad Coordinadora del Proyecto, con enfoque territorial, gestión basada en resultados, articulación interinstitucional, acompañamiento comunitario y cumplimiento de los procedimientos aplicables del PNUD.

El/la candidato/a seleccionado/a para esta posición será contratado bajo la modalidad contractual "Acuerdo Nacional de Servicios de Personal (NPSA, por sus siglas en inglés), en el nivel NPSA 6. Este contrato es por 12 meses con posibilidades de extensión, según desempeño y duración del proyecto.

II. Alcance del trabajo:

Las actividades específicas incluyen:

1. Apoyo a la Gestión y seguimiento del proyecto:

• Apoyar a el/la Coordinador/a de Proyecto en la planificación, coordinación y seguimiento de la implementación de las actividades del proyecto.

• Apoyar a el/la Coordinador/a de Proyecto y a el/la Especialista de Monitoreo y Evaluación del PNUD y del proyecto en la coordinación de los procesos relacionados con el monitoreo, evaluación y la gestión de los recursos del proyecto.

• Apoyar en la elaboración de términos de referencia (TdR), especificaciones técnicas y otros documentos requeridos para la contratación de consultores, contratistas y servicios del proyecto.

• Gestionar y dar seguimiento a las solicitudes de viaje, procesos de adquisiciones, microcompras, contrataciones y demás procesos administrativos del proyecto, velando por el cumplimiento de los procedimientos del PNUD y los cronogramas establecidos.

• Coordinar con las áreas de operaciones y otras unidades de apoyo el procesamiento oportuno de las transacciones administrativas y operativas del proyecto.

• Consolidar la información requerida para la preparación de informes semestrales, anuales, planes operativos anuales y otros reportes de gestión del proyecto, asegurando la calidad, consistencia y oportunidad de la información presentada.

2. Gestión Documental y Aprendizaje:

• Velar por la integridad, actualización y disponibilidad de la documentación técnica y programática del proyecto, en coordinación con el personal de apoyo administrativo.

• Dar seguimiento al control y organización de la documentación técnica y administrativa del proyecto, asegurando que se encuentre completa y disponible para procesos de monitoreo, auditoría y rendición de cuentas.

• Recopilar las lecciones aprendidas durante la ejecución del proyecto.

3. Coordinación operativa para la implementación del proyecto:

• Coordinar los requerimientos administrativos y logísticos necesarios para la ejecución de las actividades del proyecto, asegurando el cumplimiento de los procedimientos institucionales y la oportuna realización de las actividades programadas.

• Dar seguimiento a la ejecución de las actividades programadas y coordinar con las áreas de apoyo correspondientes para asegurar su adecuada implementación.

4. Apoyar la creación, el intercambio y el fortalecimiento del conocimiento, así como el desarrollo de capacidades relevantes para el proyecto.

• Participar en capacitaciones y organizar sesiones informativas sobre procedimientos internos para el personal del proyecto. Brindar apoyo a otras actividades de fortalecimiento de capacidades, incluyendo el diseño y la entrega de herramientas, materiales para talleres o plataformas que aprovechen la inteligencia colectiva de las comunidades y movilicen la acción.

• Brindar apoyo en la difusión e intercambio de datos relevantes y lecciones aprendidas dentro de la oficina de país y a nivel regional. Mantenerse al tanto de las mejores prácticas emergentes a nivel nacional, regional e internacional relacionadas con el trabajo del proyecto asignado.

• Realizar contribuciones valiosas a redes de conocimiento y comunidades de práctica. Apoyar la recopilación y sistematización del conocimiento, los productos y las herramientas del proyecto, así como su amplia distribución a los socios.

III. Acuerdo Institucional:

El/La Asociado/a de Proyecto trabajará bajo la supervisión directa de el/la Coordinador/a de Proyecto.

Movilización: Esta posición estará basada en la sede del Ministerio de Cultura, Ciudad de Panamá.En caso de requerirse desplazamientos a los territorios priorizados (Centros Latidos del Barrio), los gastos de movilización, hospedaje y alimentación serán cubiertos por el proyecto conforme a los procedimientos aplicables.

jobs.title: Communications and Research Analyst (Home-based in Shenzhen, China) [Open to Tier 1 & 2 Applicants]
jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

- Tier 0 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.

- Tier 1 : Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments

- Tier 2 : UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers

- Tier 3 or no tier indicated : All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

UNDP provides integrated programmatic, policy and financing solutions to realize the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). In this context, UNDP has created a Global Policy Network (GPN), a network of field-based and global technical expertise across a wide range of knowledge domains and in support of the signature solutions and organizational capabilities envisioned in the Strategic Plan. The Bureau for Policy and Programme Support (BPPS) and the Crisis Bureau (CB) are the two anchor Bureau of the GPN.

In this context, the newly established Governance, Rule of Law, and Peacebuilding (GRP) Hub, a joint endeavor with the Bureau for Policy and Programme Support (BPPS), provides leadership and advisory services to enhance UNDP’s impact on governance and peacebuilding, ensuring the integration of democratic governance and human rights into crisis response and recovery. The Hub aims to build an integrated portfolio collaboratively between the CB and BPPS and establish partnerships with various stakeholders including the UN System, IFIs, civil society, and the private sector.

Through Local Action, the GRP Hub seeks to contribute to peace and development, achieving a visible impact on communities and improving lives by delivering integrated solutions that harness global expertise and partnerships. The Local Action Unit works closely with local and regional governments as key development players, highlighting their role as public service implementers, as drivers of innovation and the closest institution to people.

Local and regional governments are already responsible of over 65% of the SDG targets, most of them linked to basic service provision from water, sanitation, mobility, climate action, health or education. Cities and territories are playing a big part on the implementation of SDGs, that are becoming a new tool for strategic planning and budgeting in the mid to long-term. Since 2015, local governments and their associations have been increasingly active in promoting the SDGs through advocacy, working with their local population and partners in transposing the spirit of Agenda 2030 in cities and territories. Local Governments have also started to use SDGs as a strategic framework to deliver better and more innovative public services linked to SDG targets and indicators.

Within this context, the SDG Local Action project is seeking to recruit a Communications and Research Analyst to contribute to the design of contents and communications tools to highlight the role of local and regional governments in implementing Agenda 2030.

The Communications and Research Analyst will also support participant local and regional governments exchange on SDG implementation, contributing to generate knowledge and replication of successful experiences to implement Agenda 2030 at local level. Finally, the Analyst will also support the communication and research needs of the Mayors Challenge project.

Duties and Responsibilities

The Communications and Research Analyst will report to the Learning and Knowledge Generation Analyst, who works home based (CET time zone).

SDGs are genuinely interlinked with service provision at local level. To be able to deliver on Agenda 2030, local and regional governments are innovating on the way they plan, design and implement public policy. The Analyst will support UNDP cities and their partners to generate knowledge through the exchange of experiences, organizing international events and elaborating policy briefs and other communication materials. The Communications and Research Analyst will also liaise with the different UNDP project personnel globally to collect information, monitor and lessons learnt issued from the Mayors Challenge project.

The Communications and Research Analyst will support participant local and regional governments to communicate their stories, analyzing project data and providing narratives for targeted public segments: including local population, central governments and the international community.

Summary of functions:

1. Elaborate communications products for local and regional governments on SDG implementation solutions

- Draft and design content for the project and UNDP social platforms and project newsletter;

- Elaborate “SDG stories” about how local governments are implementing Agenda 2030;

- Elaborate content for learning exercises targeting the participating local governments.

2. Conduct research on innovative delivery of public services by local and regional governments

- Elaborate knowledge products on how local governments are contributing to SDGs by innovating public service delivery;

- Elaborate policy briefs and easy communicable knowledge materials on the lessons learnt by participating local governments;

- Promote exchange of experiences amongst local governments on how their peers are implementing the SDGs at local level.

3. Contribute to the SDG Local Action advocacy strategy to showcase the key role of local and regional governments for Agenda 2030

- Develop advocacy, visibility and promotional material that are necessary for the project;

- Analyze project data and link with SDG targets and Agenda 2030 narrative;

- Maintain and regularly update the project repository/archive of all communications material including photos videos and audios;

- Assist the Research Analyst to design and implement baseline surveys, public perception surveys, impact assessments/ tracking surveys including the development of survey report templates, design and layout of reports and related tasks;

- Assist the Research Analyst in gathering information to prepare the project metrics reports;

- Support the project team, including the UNDP Country Office staff in addressing their communications needs in regards to SDG local action.

4. Facilitate knowledge and capacity building, knowledge sharing and advocacy relevant to the assigned thematic area(s)

- Identify, synthesize and document best practices and lessons learned that are generated from the project and implementing partners.

Competencies

Core Competencies

- Achieve Results: LEVEL 1: Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline.

- Think Innovatively: LEVEL 1: Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements.

- Learn Continuously: LEVEL 1: Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback.

- Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 1: Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible.

- Act with Determination: LEVEL 1: Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident.

- Engage and Partner: LEVEL 1: Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships.

- Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 1: Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination.

Cross-Functional & Technical Competencies

Business Management

- Communication: Ability to communicate in a clear, concise and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience. Ability to manage communications internally and externally, through media, social media and other appropriate channels

- Digital Awareness and Literacy: Ability and inclination to rapidly adopt new technologies, either through skilfully grasping their usage or through understanding their impact and empowering others to use them as needed.

Business Development

- Knowledge Generation: Ability to research information and to turn it into useful knowledge, relevant for context, or responsive to a stated need. Ability to apply existing concepts to new situations, and to develop new concepts to generate workable solutions and new approaches. Knowledge of relevant concepts, conceptual models, and theories that can be useful in addressing new situations.

Communications

- Campaign Management: Ability to produce and implement communications and advocacy campaigns which lead to impactful change.

- Creative direction and copywriting: Ability to creatively communicate concepts in an engaging and simple way.

- Media Relations: Ability to develop media relations across all aspects of media work including relationships with media and preparing media materials such as messages.

- Multimedia writing/editing: Ability to create and/or edit written content for multimedia.

Required Skills and Experience

Education:

- Advanced university degree (masters degree or equivalent) in Communications, Literature, History, Journalism, Social and Political Sciences, International Development or Urban studies is required; or

- A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the areas stated above, in combination with additional 2 years of qualifying experience, will be given due consideration in lieu of master´s degree.

Experience:

- Applicants with a master’s degree (or equivalent) in a relevant field of study are not required to have professional work experience.

- Applicants with a bachelor’s degree (or equivalent) are required to have a minimum of two (2) years of relevant professional experience in international development, communications or political and social issues, with at least one (1) year of experience working with urban related issues.

Desired Skills:

- Proven experience in working with local governments and their associations is an asset;

- Experience working on Agenda 2030 or other UN global agendas will be an asset;

- Proven professional experience in communications, advocacy, knowledge management, or knowledge generation related to urban development issues is an asset;

- Experience in the usage of computers and office software packages (MS Word, Excel, etc.) and social media assets (Canva, X, LinkedIn, Instagram, Bluesky or similar) is desired;

- Proven track record of strong analytical, written, verbal, interpersonal, and intercultural communication skills is desired.

Required Language(s):

- Fluency in English and Chinese language is required.

- Working knowledge of any other UN language is an asset.

Office/Unit/Project Description

The Volunteer Services Centre (VSC), part of UNV’s Management Services, supports a growing global portfolio of over 15,000 UN Volunteers (2025), delivering timely and high-quality services across the full volunteer lifecycle. This includes recruitment, pre-assignment processing, contract administration, payroll, separation, and evacuation support for UN Volunteers serving with UN agencies, funds, programmes, and missions. With a presence in 13 locations worldwide, VSC ensures consistent and compliant service delivery across diverse operational contexts.

Under the guidance and supervision of the Operations Associate/Team Leader (G7) for the duty station, the Operations Associate supports the delivery of end-to-end volunteer lifecycle services within the VSC. The role contributes to timely onboarding, contract administration, and accurate management of benefits & entitlements, and lifecycle events.

The incumbent ensures the integrity, transparency, and accuracy of service delivery in line with the UN Volunteers Conditions of Service (COS), policies, and procedures, while maintaining high-quality outputs and consistency across multiple countries and stakeholders.

VSC collaborates closely with the Volunteer Solutions Section (VSS), headquarter units, Regional Offices, Field Units, the UNDP Global Shared Services Centre, and other UN partners to deliver coordinated services. The Operations Associate advises stakeholders on policies and procedures, promotes a collaborative and client-focused approach, and supports the timely implementation of the VSC work plan.

Scope of Work

3.1. Identification of suitable candidates primarily UN Volunteer assignments

- Provide recruitment services in adherence to established UN Volunteers’ Conditions of Service, regulations and policies;

- Verify quality and consistency of Description of Assignments (DOAs), and provide guidance on designing DOAs to UN host entities, UNV Regional Offices and Field Units;

- Advertise relevant assignments in line with established processes;

- Identify suitable candidates for UN Volunteer assignments in diverse areas of expertise and for various host entities, as per corporate Key Performance Indicators, and according to DOA requirements and in compliance with UNV’s Recruitment and Selection policy;

- Alert supervisor about deficiencies or risks, liaise with Regional Offices and Field Units on exceptional situations and provide guidance on applicable regulations, rules and policies to ensure full compliance with accountability framework;

- Keep relevant parties updated on status of identification and negotiate adjustments when required;

- Contribute to a fair workload distribution by supporting the identification and submission of candidates for UN Volunteer assignments across regions when needed;

- Record actions and data in the volunteer management systems;

- Ensure accurate data management in official databases;

- Facilitate timely resolution of queries related to volunteer recruitment.

3.2 Outreach and support to talent acquisition

- Coordinate with the Volunteer Solutions Section, Regional Offices and Field Units to remain informed of evolving demand for UN Volunteer profiles;

- Use social media and other sourcing channels to identify candidates, identify gaps in the existing talent pool, and support regional and national outreach campaigns and networks of talent sources in coordination with the Talent Acquisition team and relevant communication colleagues;

- Manage communication with candidates as it relates to the outcome of their applications;

- Contribute to the production of insightful recruitment analytics reports with regards to critical vacancies taking into account UNV’s priorities of gender parity and workforce diversity.

3.3 Recruitment compliance, clearances and case management

- Conduct reference checks, obtain relevant pre- and post-submission clearances, and verify performance appraisals for selected candidates against established standards of competence and integrity;

- Flag deficiencies, risks and exceptional situations to the supervisor; liaise with Regional Offices, Field Units and Host Entities; and provide guidance on applicable rules, policies and the accountability framework;

- Keep relevant parties informed of recruitment status, negotiate adjustments when required, record actions and data in volunteer management systems, and support the timely resolution of recruitment-related queries.

3.4 Knowledge building and continuous improvement

- Contribute to recruitment training materials and corporate activities that strengthen the recruitment capacity of UNV personnel;

- Capture and share lessons learnt from candidate identification; contribute to knowledge networks and communities of practice; and provide input on recruitment policies, systems and processes to improve the timeliness and quality of VSC services;

- Serve, on a rotational basis, as a VSC focal point on assigned topics and perform other duties within the functional profile as required for the efficient functioning of the office and the organization.

4. Institutional Arrangement

The Recruitment Associate is part of the Volunteer Services Centre and is administratively supported by the respective Regional Office. The position will report to the Operations Associate, Recruitment (G6) under the substantive guidance of G7 Operations Associate, Volunteer Recruitment and overall leadership of Chief, Volunteer Services Centre (VSC). The position has no supervisory or managerial responsibilities.

Background

The Green and Inclusive Cities in Mongolia (GICM) Project is implemented under the National Implementation Modality (NIM), with the Ministry of Environment and Climate Change (MECC) serving as the implementing partner and UNDP providing implementation support, technical assistance, quality assurance, and oversight. Funded by the Global Environment Facility (GEF), the project supports national and local governments in accelerating the transition toward sustainable, resilient, low-carbon, and people-centered urban development. The project promotes integrated urban planning, climate-smart infrastructure, sustainable mobility systems, resource-efficient urban services, enhanced urban biodiversity, and accessible green public spaces. It also strengthens institutional capacities and inclusive governance mechanisms to ensure meaningful participation of citizens, communities, civil society organizations, the private sector, and vulnerable groups in urban development and decision-making processes. Through these interventions, the project contributes to creating greener, more resilient, and more inclusive cities that improve quality of life while advancing Mongolia's climate and sustainable development objectives.

The Eliminating Hazardous Chemicals from Supply Chains in Mongolia Project is implemented under the National Implementation Modality (NIM), with the Ministry of Food, Agriculture and Light Industry (MOFALI) serving as the implementing partner and the UNDP providing implementation support, technical assistance, quality assurance, and oversight. Funded by GEF, the project supports national efforts to reduce the use and release of hazardous chemicals across key economic sectors and supply chains.

The project seeks to strengthen the policy and regulatory framework for chemicals management, enhance institutional and technical capacities, improve industry practices, promote the adoption of safer and more sustainable alternatives, and increase transparency and accountability among public and private sector stakeholders. It also supports knowledge generation, awareness raising, and multi-stakeholder engagement to facilitate informed decision-making and responsible chemicals management throughout product life cycles. Through these interventions, the project contributes to reducing environmental pollution and health risks, advancing circular economy principles, and accelerating Mongolia's transition toward greener production systems and sustainable consumption patterns.

The Admin and Finance Associate will provide administrative, financial, and logistical support for the effective implementation of the GEF Funded projects of UNDP Mongolia. Under the direct supervision of the respective Project Managers and in close coordination with the UNDP Country Office operations team, the incumbent will support project budgeting, financial planning and reporting, travel and event logistics, asset and inventory management, records management, and compliance with UNDP, GEF, and national implementation modality (NIM) requirements. The Associate will ensure timely processing of financial transactions, maintain accurate project documentation, monitor expenditures against approved budgets, support project audits and reviews, and facilitate administrative coordination among implementing partners, government institutions, service providers, and other stakeholders to ensure efficient and accountable project delivery and achievement of project results.

UNDP adopts a portfolio approach to accommodate changing business needs and leverage linkages across interventions to achieve its strategic goals. Therefore, UNDP personnel are expected to work across units, functions, teams, and projects in multidisciplinary teams in order to enhance and enable horizontal collaboration.

Working closely with Project Managers, implementing partners, and the UNDP Country Office, the Associate supports financial management, administrative processes, logistics, and reporting to facilitate the timely and accountable delivery of project results.

Under the overall guidance and direct supervision of the Project Managers, the Admin and Finance Associate is responsible for project implementation support services, ensuring effective operational management of the project and transparent utilization of financial resources. Background

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) is the UN’s global development network, advocating for change and connecting countries to knowledge, experience and resources to help people build a better life. We are on the ground in 170 countries and territories, working with governments and people on their own solutions to global and national development challenges to help empower lives and build resilient nations.

UNDP Turkmenistan was appointed by the Country Coordinating Mechanism (CCM) as the Principal Recipient (PR) for the Global Fund to fight AIDS, Tuberculosis and Malaria TB grant implementation in 2010. As the PR, UNDP is responsible for management and coordination of the implementation of the programme, monitoring and evaluation (M&E), and effective and transparent use of the Global Fund resources. Up to date UNDP has implemented TB grants with total budget more than $42 mln. The implementing partners of the grant: Ministry of Health (MoH), Ministry of Interior (MoI), World Health Organization (WHO), National Red Crescent Society (NRCS) and the National TB Programme. In 2025-2027 Turkmenistan implements Transitional TB grant aiming gradual phase-out from the Global Fund support in 2027-2030. In the transitional grant UNDP’s role will be to support MoH and NTP with building national policies and capacities to advance transition to full domestic funding of the TB grant and at the same time to ensure universal access to timely and quality diagnosis and treatment of all forms of TB.

Besides the Global Fund’s TB grant, UNDP country office implements financing agreements funded by MoH aiming at control of infectious diseases (TB, HIV, viral hepatitis, blood-born infections, sexually transmitted infections). Since 2017 UNDP implemented more than $69 mln Government funding for improving control of infectious diseases. The projects funded by the Global Fund and by the MoH are thematically combined and contribute to implementation of the plan for sustainability and transition of the National TB Programme to full domestic funding. The projects include technical assistance, capacity building, introduction of innovations for lab detection of infectious diseases, as well as procurement of quality-assured health products (reagents, commodities, medicines, medical equipment) for the needs of national programmes. Under the supervision of the Project Manager, the Laboratory Associate will lead on those activities implemented in collaboration with the national and international counterparts.

Supply of lab reagents, consumables and equipment for TB and other infectious diseases:

- Follow up on proper implementation of diagnostic algorithms in the scope of the project.

- To assist national partners with preparation of the annual needs’ estimation for procurement of lab supplies for detection of TB and other infectious diseases (reagents for sputum microscopy, culture investigations, PCR, drug susceptibility testing, reagents for clinical lab tests, various consumables, PPE, lab equipment).

- To assist national partners with preparing specifications and quantification for procurement of lab supplies, compare the specifications and quantifications of lab reagents and consumables offered by the suppliers, provide inputs in clarification process.

- To assist national partners with preparing distribution lists for the delivered lab supplies; advise on re-distribution of lab supplies between laboratories as a preventive/corrective measure in case of risk of stockout or expiry of lab supplies at some labs.

- Monitor implementation and quarterly/annual reporting of national targets on testing, laboratory supply and quality control of laboratory services related to TB.

- To assist with preparing quarterly reports on stock of the lab supplies, analyze the reports and warn on potential stock-out or expiring items.

- To verify status of the lab equipment and physical count of inventory items provided by the project to laboratories.

- Participate in regular (quarterly and annual) monitoring visits to TB and other infectious diseases’ facilities across Turkmenistan for routine supervision and verification purposes.

Infection control, Quality Assurance, maintenance and calibration of lab equipment in TB and other infectious diseases laboratories:

- To identify and monitor the needs in maintenance and calibration of the lab equipment supported by UNDP projects.

- To support implementation of annual maintenance and calibration plans. The incumbent will be required to accompany engineers conducting various maintenance or calibration services.

- To assist national partners with implementing the necessary infection control measures. Contribute to implementation of the External and Internal Quality Assurance plans.

- To contribute to introduction of innovations for national counterparts, including specialized lab technologies and digital tools;

- To contribute to capacity building activities for the national implementing partners as per identified needs through formal training, on-site training, supervisory visits etc;

- Contribute to preparation of TORs and provides logistical support with organization of missions/trainings etc;

- To follow up recommendations of SNRL, WHO and other experts with regard to strengthening national TB and other infectious diseases’ laboratories.

- Provide sound contributions and support to knowledge networks, communities of practice, and digital knowledge platforms.

jobs.description:
Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:
